extraction_notes.note: The hand-written proof fact after 'Proof of (dFdG)' runs to the end of Section 3.5 and so also contains the Brouwer argument that finishes Proposition 3.1. I kept the fact span with a proves edge to the claim ClP6, and nested it in the prose proof PP9, which proves PrP2. Because the proof fact exists, ClP6 is a claim with a separate proof node, not a claim whose argument is its steps (step rule 7).
The proof of Proposition 3.1 covers Sections 3.1-3.5. I modelled it as two proof parts (PP5 in 3.1, PP9 in 3.5) plus the claims (BS3') and (BS2'), each with its own hand-written proof in 3.3 and 3.4.
theorem or definition: the sentence asserts conservation of mass and energy and also introduces M and E. I typed it as an uncited standard result.

The lemma statement has no attribution, but its proof assigns part (i) to standard properties of L and part (ii) to MMR1 Prop. 2.2, so I marked it external. The (Q,Y_0) computation is the paper's own, inside PP1.

The definitions of f_0 and q_0 appear in the introduction, in Section 2.2 and again in Appendix A, with small differences (c_0 in R vs c_0<0, an extra c_0 factor). I kept every numbered copy as its own equation node instead of merging them with also_stated_at.
Inside the proof of (dFdG) the paper writes 'we have using (dFdG)' when computing G'(s^*). The intended reference is probably (dg). I kept the \ref edge as written.

Not extracted: the literature discussion in Section 1.2 and in comment 3 of Section 1.3, the acknowledgments, and the section-opening meta sentences. The formal computations of the strategy section 1.4 are heuristic remarks, not results.

metadata.extraction_comment: The proofs of Proposition 2.4 and of Claim 2 are \begin{proof} environments whose proves edges syntax did not fill (a remark sits between the proposition and its proof), so I added them by hand with basis inferred.

nodes.name: L2-critical generalized Korteweg-de Vries equation (gKdV)
nodes.statement_short: The L^2-critical gKdV Cauchy problem u_t+(u_xx+u^5)_x=0, u(0)=u_0.

nodes.name: gKdV equation
nodes.statement: {\rm (gKdV)}\quad \left\{\begin{array}{ll} u_t + (u_{xx} + u^5)_x =0, \quad & (t,x)\in [0,T)\times {\mathbb R}, \\ u(0,x)= u_0(x), & x\in {\mathbb R}. \end{array} \right.
nodes.label: kdv

nodes.name: Local well-posedness of gKdV in H^1 (Kenig-Ponce-Vega)
nodes.statement: The Cauchy problem is locally well-posed in the energy space $H^1$ from Kenig, Ponce and Vega \cite{KPV,KPV2}. Given $u_0 \in H^1$, there exists a unique\footnote{in a certain sense} maximal solution $u(t)$ of \eqref{kdv} in $C([0,T), H^1)$ with either $T=+\infty$, or $T<+\infty$ and then $\mathop{\rm lim}_{t\to T} \|u_x(t)\|_{L^2} = +\infty$.
conclusions: there exists a unique\footnote{in a certain sense} maximal solution $u(t)$ of \eqref{kdv} in $C([0,T), H^1)$ with either $T=+\infty$, or $T<+\infty$ and then $\mathop{\rm lim}_{t\to T} \|u_x(t)\|_{L^2} = +\infty$
nodes.statement_short: H^1 data give a unique maximal solution; finite maximal time forces blow-up of the H^1 norm.

nodes.name: Conservation of mass and energy
nodes.statement: For $H^1$ solution, the mass and the energy are conserved by the flow: $\forall t\in [0,T)$,  $$M(u(t))=\int u^2(t)= M(u_0), \ \ E(u(t))= \frac 12 \int u_x^2(t) - \frac 16 \int u^6(t)= E(u_0).$$
conclusions: the mass and the energy are conserved by the flow
nodes.statement_short: Mass M(u)=int u^2 and energy E(u)=1/2 int u_x^2 - 1/6 int u^6 are conserved.

nodes.name: Symmetries of gKdV
nodes.statement:
Equation \eqref{kdv} has the following invariances: if $u(t,x)$ is solution of \eqref{kdv} then $-u(t,x)$, $ u(-t,-x)$ and 
 $$\lambda_0^{\frac12}u(\lambda_0^3 (t-t_0),\lambda_0 (x -x_0)), \ \ (\lambda_0,t_0,x_0)\in \mathbb{R}^*_+\times \mathbb{R}\times \mathbb{R}$$ are also  solutions of \eqref{kdv}.
conclusions:
then $-u(t,x)$, $ u(-t,-x)$ and 
 $$\lambda_0^{\frac12}u(\lambda_0^3 (t-t_0),\lambda_0 (x -x_0)), \ \ (\lambda_0,t_0,x_0)\in \mathbb{R}^*_+\times \mathbb{R}\times \mathbb{R}$$ are also  solutions of \eqref{kdv}
nodes.statement_short: Sign change, reflection and scaling/translation map gKdV solutions to solutions.

nodes.name: Solitons and ground state Q
nodes.statement:
The family of  traveling wave solutions of \eqref{kdv},  called solitons, plays a distinguished role in the analysis:
$$u(t,x) = Q_{\lambda_0}(x-\lambda_0^{-2} t-x_0), \ \ (\lambda_0,x_0)\in\mathbb{R}^*_+\times \mathbb{R},$$ with  
\begin{equation} Q_\lambda(x) = \frac{1}{\lambda^{\frac 12} }Q \left(\frac x\lambda\right) ,\quad Q(x) =   \left(\frac {3}{\cosh^{2}\left( 2 x\right)}\right)^{\frac14}, \quad
Q''+Q^5 =Q.
\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Solitons Q_lambda(x-lambda^{-2}t-x_0) with Q=(3/cosh^2(2x))^{1/4} solving Q''+Q^5=Q.

nodes.name: Ground state Q and its rescalings
nodes.statement: Q_\lambda(x) = \frac{1}{\lambda^{\frac 12} }Q \left(\frac x\lambda\right) ,\quad Q(x) = \left(\frac {3}{\cosh^{2}\left( 2 x\right)}\right)^{\frac14}, \quad Q''+Q^5 =Q.
nodes.label: eq:Q

nodes.name: Sharp Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality
nodes.statement: \forall v\in H^1,\quad \int |v|^6 \leq \int v_x^2 \left(\frac {\int v^2}{\int Q^2}\right)^2.
conclusions: \int |v|^6 \leq \int v_x^2 \left(\frac {\int v^2}{\int Q^2}\right)^2.
nodes.statement_short: For v in H^1, int v^6 <= int v_x^2 (int v^2 / int Q^2)^2.
nodes.label: gn

nodes.name: Global existence below the ground state mass
nodes.statement:
Moreover,  from   \eqref{gn},   mass and energy conservations, for
initial data in $H^1$  such that $\|u_0\|_{L^2}<\|Q\|_{L^2}$, the corresponding solution $u(t)$ of \eqref{kdv} is bounded in $H^1$ and thus globally defined in time.
conclusions: the corresponding solution $u(t)$ of \eqref{kdv} is bounded in $H^1$ and thus globally defined in time

nodes.name: Set A of well-decaying data and tube T_alpha*
nodes.section: 1.2 On the classification of the flow near $Q$
nodes.statement_short: A: H^1-perturbations of Q with decay on the right; T_alpha*: L^2 tube around the soliton family.

nodes.name: Classification of the flow in A
nodes.statement:
\noindent{\bf Classification in $\mathcal A$ {\rm (\cite{MMR1,MMR2})}.} 
Let $0<\alpha_0\ll\alpha^*\ll 1$.
{\sl Let   $u_0 \in \mathcal{A}$ and 
  $u \in \mathcal C ([0,T),H^1)$ be the corresponding solution of \eqref{kdv}.
Then, one of the following three scenarios occurs:


\medskip

\noindent{\bf (Blow up)}  For all $t\in [0,T),$ $u(t)\in \mathcal{T}_{\alpha^*}$ and the solution blows up in finite time $T<+\infty$ with
\begin{equation} \|u_x(t)\|_{L^2} \sim \frac {\|Q'\|_{L^2}}{\ell_0 (T-t)} \quad \hbox{as $t\uparrow T$ for some $\ell_0>0$.} 
\end{equation}
 

\noindent{\bf (Soliton)}  The solution is global and
\begin{equation}
  u(t,  \cdot +x(t))\to Q_{\lambda_\infty} \hbox{ in $H^1_{\rm loc}$ as $t\to +\infty$ for  $|\lambda_\infty-1| + |x'(t)-1|\lesssim \delta(\alpha_0)$},
\end{equation} 
where $\delta(\alpha_0)\to 0$  as $\alpha_0\to 0$.
\smallskip


\noindent{\bf (Exit and $S$ dynamics)} The solution  $u$ exits the tube   $\mathcal{T}_{\alpha^*}$ at some time  $t_u\in (0,T)$, and  there exist    $\lambda_u>0$, $x_u\in \mathbb{R}$,  such that
$$\| {\lambda_u^{\frac 12}} u(t_u, \lambda_u x+x_u) - S(t^*,x)\|_{L^2} \leq \delta(\alpha_0),$$
where $\delta(\alpha_0)\to 0$  as $\alpha_0\to 0$ and where $t^*>0$ depends only on $\alpha^*$.\\
Moreover, assume that $S$ scatters at $+\infty$, then  $u$ is global  and scatters at $+\infty$.

u}\ \ \mbox{as}\ \ t	o +\infty. \end{equation} Moreover, such solutions can be taken arbitrarily close in $H^1$ to the family of solitons.
conclusions: Moreover, such solutions can be taken arbitrarily close in $H^1$ to the family of solitons.
nodes.statement_short: Near-soliton H^1 solutions exist that blow up at rate t^{-nu} (nu>11/13), or grow up like e^t or t^nu.
nodes.label: th:1

nodes.name: Finite time blow up rate t^{-nu}
nodes.statement: \|u_x(t)\|_{L^2} \sim t^{-\nu}\ \ \mbox{as}\ \ t\downarrow 0^+.
nodes.label: th:1:1

nodes.name: Exponential grow up
nodes.statement: \|u_x(t)\|_{L^2} \sim e^{t} \ \ \mbox{as}\ \ t\to +\infty.
nodes.label: th:1:4

nodes.name: Power grow up
nodes.statement: \|u_x(t)\|_{L^2} \sim t^{\nu}\ \ \mbox{as}\ \ t\to +\infty.
nodes.label: th:1:5

nodes.name: Sharpness of the results of MMR1, MMR2
nodes.statement: {\it 1. Sharpness of the results in \cite{MMR1, MMR2}}. Theorem \ref{th:1} above shows the optimality of the results in  \cite{MMR1, MMR2} since it proves that some decay assumption (such as $u_0\in \mathcal A$) is required to obtain a unique  stable blow up rate $1/(T-t)$. This is in contrast with the nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation, for which the stable blow up rate is obtained in $H^1$, without additional decay assumption (see \cite{MRjams} and references therein). Note from the proof that the solutions obtained in Theorem \ref{th:1} are expected to be unstable (except may be for $\nu<1$ in \eqref{th:1:1}). Indeed, they are constructed using a topogical argument involving two possible directions of instability.
nodes.statement_short: Slow decay is needed: without decay, the stable 1/(T-t) rate fails, unlike for NLS; solutions are expected unstable.

nodes.name: Sharpness of the H^1 blow up result
nodes.statement: It is proved in \cite{Mjams, MMannals} that initial data $u_0$ such that \eqref{classe} generate solutions that blow up in finite or infinite time. The proof is by obstruction and Liouville classification and does not provide any estimate on the blow up speed. This $H^1$ result is also sharp in the sense that  from Theorem~\ref{th:1},  both finite or infinite time blow up may occur in $H^1$.  All these results  thus complement each other.
nodes.statement_short: Theorem 1.1 shows both finite and infinite time blow up occur in H^1, complementing the obstruction result.

nodes.name: On the role of tails
nodes.statement: {\it 3. On the role of tails.} As one can see from the proof of Theorem \ref{th:1}, the blow up rate is directly related to the precise behavior of the initial data on the right. In particular, other type of blow up speeds can be produced by similar arguments by adjusting the tail of the initial data. A   similar phenomenon was observed for global in time growing up solutions to the parabolic energy critical harmonic heat flow by Gustafson, Nakanishi and Tsai \cite{NT2}. There an explicit formula on the growth of the solution at infinity is given directly in terms of the initial data which is conceptually very similar to what we observe for (gKdV).
nodes.statement_short: The blow-up rate is dictated by the tail of the data on the right; other rates can be produced similarly.

nodes.name: On the decay assumption
nodes.statement:
{\it 4. On the   decay assumption}. In \cite{MMR1} (see the definition of $\mathcal A$), the assumption $\int y^{10} \varepsilon^2<1$ is not sharp.
In Theorem \ref{th:1}, the solution contains a tail  of the form $x^{-\theta}$ for $x\gg 1$, where $\theta\in(1,\frac {29}{18})$.

nodes.name: Sharp decay assumption for the stable blow up rate
nodes.statement: By now, it is not clear what is the sharp decay assumption on the initial data required to get  the stable blow up rate in \cite{MMR1}.

nodes.name: Scalar product
nodes.statement: For $f,g\in L^2$, we note the scalar product: $$(f,g)=\int f(x)g(x)dx.$$

nodes.name: Generator of L2 scaling Lambda
nodes.statement: We introduce the generator of the $L^2$ scaling symmetry $$ \Lambda f=\frac12f+yf'. $$

nodes.name: Linearized operator L
nodes.genus: linearized operator close to the ground state

nodes.name: Small constant delta(alpha*)
nodes.statement: For a given  small constant $0<\alpha^*\ll1 $,  $\delta(\alpha^*)$ denotes a   small constant with $$\delta(\alpha^*)\to 0\ \ \mbox{as}\ \ \alpha^*\to 0.$$

nodes.name: Characteristic function
nodes.statement: We denote by  ${\mathbf{1}}_I$   the characteristic function of the interval $I$.

nodes.name: Slowly decaying tail f_0 and its gKdV evolution q_0 (heuristic setting)
nodes.statement:
Given $c_0\in \mathbb{R}$,  $x_0\gg 1$, $\theta>1$, we fix
 a smooth function $f_0$ which corresponds to a slowly decaying tail:
 \begin{equation} f_0(x)= c_0 x^{-\theta} \hbox{ for $x>\frac {x_0}2$},\quad
f_0(x)=0 \hbox{ for $x<\frac {x_0}4$}, 
\end{equation}
and  
 $q_0$   the solution of 
\begin{equation} \partial_t q_0 + \partial_x(\partial_x^2 q_0 + q_0^5)=0,\quad
 q_0(0,x)= f_0(x).
\end{equation}

nodes.name: Tail f_0 (introduction)
nodes.statement: f_0(x)= c_0 x^{-\theta} \hbox{ for $x>\frac {x_0}2$},\quad f_0(x)=0 \hbox{ for $x<\frac {x_0}4$},
nodes.label: deffzintro

nodes.name: Equation of q_0 (introduction)
nodes.statement: \partial_t q_0 + \partial_x(\partial_x^2 q_0 + q_0^5)=0,\quad q_0(0,x)= f_0(x).
nodes.label: defqzintro

nodes.name: Decomposition ansatz with tail correction
nodes.statement:
We then consider the solution to {\rm (\ref{kdv})} with initial data $Q+f_0$ and claim that it admits a decomposition of the form  
\begin{equation} u(t,x)  =  \frac 1{\lambda^{\frac 12}(t)} \left( Q_{b(t)} + \lambda^{\frac 12}(t) q_0(t,x(t)) Y_0 + \varepsilon   \right) \left( t,\frac {x-x(t)}{\lambda(t)}\right)
+q_0(t,x)
\end{equation}
for some $$\|\varepsilon(t)\|_{H^1}\ll 1$$
and where $Y_0$ is a fixed function (see Lemma \ref{lemmainvert} for the definition of $Y_0$ and Proposition \ref{le:2} for the justification of this correction term). 
An essential feature of the nonlinear (gKdV) flow is that $q_0(t,x)$ conserves for $x\gtrsim t$  the slow decay of   $f_0(x)$ (see Lemma \ref{le:qz}). This tail then acts like an external force on the coupled  system of modulation equations driving $(b(t),\lambda(t),x(t))$ and modify its behavior.
nodes.statement_short: Solution with data Q+f_0 is decomposed as rescaled Q_b + p Y_0 + eps plus q_0; the tail acts as a forcing.

nodes.name: Decomposition (uu)
nodes.statement: u(t,x) = \frac 1{\lambda^{\frac 12}(t)} \left( Q_{b(t)} + \lambda^{\frac 12}(t) q_0(t,x(t)) Y_0 + \varepsilon \right) \left( t,\frac {x-x(t)}{\lambda(t)}\right) +q_0(t,x)
nodes.label: uu

nodes.name: Renormalized time s (heuristic)
nodes.statement:
Let us consider the global renormalized time 
\begin{equation} \frac {ds}{dt} = \frac 1 {\lambda^3}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Renormalized time ds/dt
nodes.statement: \frac {ds}{dt} = \frac 1 {\lambda^3}.
nodes.label: sharpintro

nodes.name: Formal modulation dynamics with tail and the exotic regimes
nodes.statement:
Then, explicit computations similar to the ones in \cite{MMR1} yield to leading order (neglecting $\varepsilon$ and higher order terms in $(b,\lambda,x)$) the set of coupled modulation equations in the setting of the decomposition {\rm (\ref{uu})}:
  \begin{equation} \quad \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda}+b=0,\quad x_s = \lambda,\quad \frac d{ds} \left( \frac b{\lambda^2} + \frac 4 {\int Q} c_0   \lambda^{-\frac 32} x^{-\theta} \right)=0.
 \end{equation}
 This system is to be compared to the unperturbed one obtained in \cite{MMR1}, for $u_0\in \mathcal{A}$ (without tail):
 \begin{equation} \frac {ds}{dt} = \frac 1 {\lambda^3}, \quad 
 \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda}+b=0,\quad x_s = \lambda,\quad \frac d{ds}   \left(\frac b{\lambda^2}\right)  =0,\end{equation}
which leads to the universal blow up regime $$\frac b{\lambda^2} = \ell_0, \ \ \lambda(t) = \ell_0 (T-t)\ \ \mbox{for some}\ \ \ell_0>0.$$ We now integrate explicitly {\rm (\ref{dynsyst})} and fit the parameters of the tail $(c_0,\theta)$ to obtain the blow up regimes described in Theorem \ref{th:1}. Integrating  in $s$, we find
$$
 \frac b{\lambda^2} + \frac 4 {\int Q} c_0   \lambda^{-\frac 32} x^{-\theta} =\ell_0,
$$
where $\ell_0$ is a constant. We focus on the threshold regime $\ell_0=0$ leading to:
 \begin{equation}
 \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda}+b=0,\quad x_s = \lambda,\quad 
 \frac b{\lambda^2} + \frac 4 {\int Q} c_0   \lambda^{-\frac 32} x^{-\theta}=0,
 \end{equation}
 which can now be integrated as follows:
 $$
 \lambda^{-\frac 12}\lambda_s = \frac 4 {\int Q} c_0   \lambda x^{-\theta}
 = \frac 4 {\int Q} c_0 x_s x^{-\theta}
 $$
 or equivalently after integration:
 $$
   \lambda^{\frac 12}(s) + \frac 2 {\int Q}   \frac {1}{\theta-1}c_0 x^{-\theta+1}(s) = \ell_1.
 $$
 We focus again on the threshold regime $\ell_1=0$ leading to:
 $$
   \lambda^{\frac 12}(s) = -\frac 2 {\int Q}   \frac {1}{\theta-1}c_0 x^{-\theta+1}(s).
 $$ 
We see that $c_0<0$ is necessary at this point and
$$
x_s(s) = \lambda(s) = \left(\frac 2 {\int Q}   \frac {1}{\theta-1}c_0\right)^2 x^{-2 \theta+2}(s).
$$
By integration on $[s_0,s]$, choosing $ x^{2\theta-1}(s_0)=(2\theta- 1)\left(\frac 2 {\int Q}   \frac {1}{\theta-1}c_0\right)^2 s_0$, we obtain 
$$
x^{2\theta-1}(s) =  (2\theta- 1)\left(\frac 2 {\int Q}   \frac {1}{\theta-1}c_0\right)^2 s,
$$
and thus
$$
\lambda(s) =  (2\theta- 1)^{\frac {-2\theta+2}{2\theta-1}} \left(\frac 2 {\int Q}   \frac {1}{\theta-1} c_0\right)^{\frac {2}{2 \theta-1}}  s^{- \frac {2(\theta-1)}{2\theta-1}}.
$$
Set
$$
\beta =   \frac { 2(\theta-1)} {2\theta-1},\quad
\theta = \frac {1-\frac \beta2}{1-\beta}, \quad c_0 =-\frac { \int Q}2(\theta-1) (2\theta-1)^{\theta-1} ,$$
so that 
\begin{equation} \lambda(s) = s^{-\beta}, \quad 
x(s) = \frac 1{1-\beta} s^{1-\beta},\quad
b(s) =\frac {\beta}s.
\end{equation}
Of course, one can check directly that \eqref{eq:blx} are solutions of the system \eqref{dynsyst}
but the above computation reveals the two instability directions
\begin{equation} \ell_0=\ell_1= 0,
\end{equation}
and justifies the use of a topological argument to construct the solution.
nodes.statement_short: Formal integration of the tail-forced modulation system gives lambda=s^{-beta}, b=beta/s with two instability directions.

nodes.name: Perturbed modulation system
nodes.statement: \quad \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda}+b=0,\quad x_s = \lambda,\quad \frac d{ds} \left( \frac b{\lambda^2} + \frac 4 {\int Q} c_0 \lambda^{-\frac 32} x^{-\theta} \right)=0.
nodes.label: dynsyst

nodes.name: Unperturbed modulation system
nodes.statement: \frac {ds}{dt} = \frac 1 {\lambda^3}, \quad \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda}+b=0,\quad x_s = \lambda,\quad \frac d{ds} \left(\frac b{\lambda^2}\right) =0,
nodes.label: dynsystbis

nodes.name: Threshold modulation system
nodes.statement: \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda}+b=0,\quad x_s = \lambda,\quad \frac b{\lambda^2} + \frac 4 {\int Q} c_0 \lambda^{-\frac 32} x^{-\theta}=0,

nodes.name: Explicit solution (eq:blx)
nodes.statement: \lambda(s) = s^{-\beta}, \quad x(s) = \frac 1{1-\beta} s^{1-\beta},\quad b(s) =\frac {\beta}s.
nodes.label: eq:blx

nodes.name: Control of the remainder via mixed energy/virial functional
nodes.statement:
We now aim at constructing an exact solution which  corresponds to   control  the remainder term $\varepsilon(t,x)$. Note that we may now choose $\varepsilon_0(x)$ to be {\it well localized on the right}, and we therefore adapt the machinery developed in \cite{MMR1} to construct a mixed energy/Virial functional $$\mathcal F\sim \int\psi\varepsilon_y^2+\varphi\varepsilon^2-\frac 13  \psi\left[(Q_b+\varepsilon)^6-Q_b^6-6Q_b^5\varepsilon\right]$$ for well chosen cut off functions $(\psi,\varphi)$ which are exponentially decaying to the left, and polynomially growing to the right. Roughly speaking, in the above regime \eqref{eq:blx}, this functional enjoys two fundamental properties:
\\
-- Coercivity :
 $$\mathcal F \gtrsim \|\varepsilon\|_{H^1_{\rm loc}}^2.$$
 -- Lyapounov monotonicity :  
\begin{equation} \frac{d}{ds}\left\{s^j {\mathcal F}\right\}+ s^j \|\varepsilon\|_{H^1_{\rm loc}}^2
\lesssim s^{j-4}, \ \ j\geq 0.
\end{equation}
Time integration of the monotonicity formula {\rm (\ref{cnkneneoe})} in the regime dictated by {\rm (\ref{eq:blx})} yields  sufficient uniform estimates on $\varepsilon$. Therefore, it only remains to adjust the initial parameters $(b(s_0),\lambda(s_0))$ in order to asymptotically satisfy the unstable conditions {\rm (\ref{unstabomodesintro})}. This is achieved using a simple topological argument, as in \cite{MMC} but in a blow up setting (see also \cite{RH}, \cite{S}, \cite{MRR}, \cite{CoteZaag}).
nodes.statement_short: A mixed energy/virial Lyapunov functional F controls eps; a topological argument fixes initial parameters.

nodes.name: Lyapounov monotonicity (heuristic)
nodes.statement: \frac{d}{ds}\left\{s^j {\mathcal F}\right\}+ s^j \|\varepsilon\|_{H^1_{\rm loc}}^2 \lesssim s^{j-4}, \ \ j\geq 0.
nodes.label: cnkneneoe

nodes.name: From renormalized to original time: the blow up scenarios
nodes.statement:
The above strategy is implemented for all $0<\beta<\frac{11}{20}$. Now we show how the behavior of the parameters  {\rm (\ref{eq:blx})} (see the precise estimates in \eqref{sharp}) in renormalized time leads to the  scenarios of Theorem \ref{th:1} in the original time $t$  (after possible scaling and time translation to adjust constants).

\smallskip

\noindent{-- Blow up in finite time:}
for 
$
\frac 13 < \beta < \frac {11}{20}.
$
From \eqref{sharpintro}, {\rm (\ref{eq:blx})}: $$\int_{s_0}^{+\infty}    {\lambda^3(s)} ds=T<+\infty$$ and the 
solution $u(t)$ blows up in finite time $T$.
Moreover,
$$  T-t=\int_{s(t)}^{+\infty}{\lambda^3(s')}{ds'} 
\sim \frac {s^{ -( 3 \beta-1)}}{3\beta-1}  , \quad \lambda(t) \sim  \left[ (3\beta-1)(T-t)\right]^{\frac {\beta}{3\beta-1}}, 
$$
which implies  $\|u_x(t)\|_{L^2} \sim \|Q'\|_{L^2} \lambda^{-1} (t) \sim C (T-t)^{-\nu}$ for any $\nu\in (\frac {11}{13},+\infty).$ 

\medskip

\noindent{-- Grow up in infinite time:}  for $ 
\beta = \frac 13,
$ 
the solution $u(t)$ is global in time since $\int_{s_0}^{+\infty}  {\lambda^3(s)} ds =+\infty$.
Moreover, for some $c_0$ and some $c_1 >0$,
$$
t=\int_{s_0}^{s(t)}{\lambda^3(s')}{ds'} 
=  {\rm log} s + c_0 +O(s^{-\frac 1{10}}),\quad  s\sim  c_1 e^t  ,\quad
 \lambda(t)\sim  c_1^{-\frac 13} e^{-\frac t 3}  .
$$
This means grow up in infinite time for $u(t)$ with exponential growth. Scaling and time translation   lead to any exponential rate $e^{-ct}$, $c>0$. Finally, for $0<\beta< \frac 13,$
we also obtain a global solution $u(t)$  since
$$\int_{s_0}^{+\infty} \lambda^3(s) ds \geq 2^{-3} \int_{s_0}^{+\infty} s^{-3 \beta} ds = +\infty,$$
and 
$$t= \int_{s_0}^{t(s)} \lambda^3(s') ds' \sim 
\frac 1{1-3 \beta} s^{1-3 \beta}  ,
\quad  \lambda(t) \sim  (1-3 \beta)^{\frac \beta{1-3 \beta}} t^{\frac \beta{1-3 \beta}}  ,
$$
which means   grow up rates $t^\nu$ at $+\infty$, for any $\nu=\frac {\beta}{1-3\beta}>0$.
nodes.statement_short: Integrating dt=lambda^3 ds: beta in (1/3,11/20) gives finite time blow up, beta=1/3 exponential and beta<1/3 power grow up.

nodes.name: Function space Y
nodes.statement:
Let the functional space
       ${\mathcal Y}$ be the set of functions $f\in \mathcal C^\infty({{\mathbb R}},{{\mathbb R}})$ such that
\begin{equation} \forall k\in \mathbb{N},\ \exists C_k,\, r_k>0,\ \forall y\in {{\mathbb R}},\quad |f^{(k)}(y)|\leq C_k (1+|y|)^{r_k} {e^{-|y|}},
\end{equation}
and $L$ be the linearized operator close to $Q$ given by {\rm (\ref{deflplus})}.

nodes.statement: \forall k\in \mathbb{N},\ \exists C_k,\, r_k>0,\ \forall y\in {{\mathbb R}},\quad |f^{(k)}(y)|\leq C_k (1+|y|)^{r_k} {e^{-|y|}},

nodes.name: Invertibility of L
nodes.statement: {\rm (i)} There exists a unique $Y_0\in \mathcal Y$, even, such that \begin{equation} L Y_0= 5 Q^4 ,\quad (Q,Y_0)=-\frac 34 \int Q . \end{equation} {\rm (ii)} There exists a unique function $P$ such that $P' \in \mathcal{Y}$ and \begin{equation} (L P)'={\Lambda} Q, \ \ \mathop{\rm lim}_{y \to -\infty} P(y) = \frac 12 \int Q, \ \ \mathop{\rm lim}_{y \to +\infty} P(y) =0, \end{equation} \begin{equation} (P, Q) = \frac 1{16} \left(\int Q\right)^2 > 0,\quad (P, Q')=0. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: There are unique profiles Y_0 (LY_0=5Q^4) and P ((LP)'=Lambda Q) with prescribed limits and inner products.
nodes.label: lemmainvert

nodes.statement: L Y_0= 5 Q^4 ,\quad (Q,Y_0)=-\frac 34 \int Q .

nodes.name: Equation of P

nodes.label: eq:23

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.1
nodes.statement: Note that the existence and uniqueness of $Y_0$ follows readily from standard properties of the operator $L$ (see e.g. \cite{MMR1}). Moreover, $$ (Q,Y_0)= -\frac 12 (L\Lambda Q,Y_0) =-\frac 12(\Lambda Q,5Q^4 ) =-\frac 34 \int Q^5=-\frac 34 \int Q. $$ Part (ii) is taken from \cite{MMR1}, Proposition 2.2.
nodes.statement_short: Existence of Y_0 by standard properties of L; (Q,Y_0) computed via L(Lambda Q)=-2Q; part (ii) cited from MMR1.

nodes.name: Cut-off chi_b
nodes.statement:
More precisely, let $\chi\in {\mathcal C}^{\infty}({\mathbb R})$ be such that $0\leq \chi \leq 1$, $\chi'\geq 0$ on $\mathbb{R}$,
$\chi\equiv 1$ on $[-1,+\infty)$, $\chi\equiv 0$ on $(-\infty,-2]$, and define
\begin{equation} \chi_b(y)= \chi\left(|b|^{\gamma} {y} \right),\ \ \gamma = \frac 34.
\end{equation}

nodes.name: Cut-off chi_b
nodes.statement: \chi_b(y)= \chi\left(|b|^{\gamma} {y} \right),\ \ \gamma = \frac 34.
nodes.label: defgamma

nodes.name: Approximate self-similar profiles Q_b
nodes.statement: Let \begin{equation} \quad Q_b(y) = Q(y) + b \chi_b(y) P (y). \end{equation} Then:\\ {\rm (i) Estimates on $Q_b$:} For all $y \in \mathbb{R}$, \begin{align} & |Q_b(y)|\lesssim e^{-|y|} + |b| \left( {\mathbf{1}}_{[-2,0]}(|b|^\gamma y) + e^{-\frac {|y|}{2}} \right), \\ & |Q_b^{(k)}(y)|\lesssim e^{-|y|} + |b| e^{-\frac {|y|}{2}} +|b|^{1+k \gamma} {\mathbf{1}}_{[-2,-1]}(|b|^\gamma y),\quad \text{for $k\geq 1$}. \end{align} \noindent {\rm (ii) Equation of $Q_b$:} let \begin{equation} -\Psi_b=\left(Q_b''- Q_b+ Q_b^5\right)'+b {\Lambda} Q_b, \end{equation} then, for all $y\in \mathbb{R}$, \begin{align} & |\Psi_b(y)|\lesssim |b|^{1+ \gamma} {\mathbf{1}}_{[-2 ,-1]}(|b|^{\gamma}y) + b^2 \left(e^{-\frac {|y|} 2}+ {\mathbf{1}}_{[- 2,0]}(|b|^{\gamma}y) \right), \\ & |\Psi_b^{(k)}(y)|\lesssim |b|^{1+ (k+1) \gamma} {\mathbf{1}}_{[-2 ,-1]}(|b|^{\gamma}y) + b^2 e^{-\frac {|y|} 2} ,\quad \text{for $k\geq 1$}. \end{align} {\rm (iii) Mass and energy properties of $Q_b$:} \begin{align} & \left|\int Q_b^2 - \left( \int Q^2 + 2b \int PQ \right)\right| \lesssim |b|^{2-\gamma}, \\ & \left| E(Q_b) + b \int PQ\right|\lesssim b^2 . \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Q_b=Q+b chi_b P satisfies pointwise bounds, solves the self-similar equation up to Psi_b, and has mass ~ int Q^2+2b(P,Q).
nodes.label: cl:2

nodes.name: Profile Q_b
nodes.statement: \quad Q_b(y) = Q(y) + b \chi_b(y) P (y).

nodes.name: Slowly decaying tail f_0
nodes.statement:
Let $c_0<0$,  $x_0\gg 1$, $\theta>1$  and let
$f_0$ be a smooth function such that 
 \begin{equation} f_0(x)=\left\{\begin{array}{ll}c_0 x^{-\theta} & \hbox{ for $x>\frac {x_0}2$},\\ 0 & \hbox{ for $x<\frac {x_0}4$,}\end{array}\right.
\end{equation}
and 
\begin{equation} \left|\frac {d^{k}f_0}{dx^k} (x)\right| \lesssim   |x|^{-\theta - k}, \ \ \forall (x,k)\in \mathbb{R}\times \mathbb{N}.
\end{equation}
nodes.section: 2.2 Definition of the tail on the right

nodes.name: Tail f_0
nodes.statement: f_0(x)=\left\{\begin{array}{ll}c_0 x^{-\theta} & \hbox{ for $x>\frac {x_0}2$},\\ 0 & \hbox{ for $x<\frac {x_0}4$,}\end{array}\right.

nodes.section: 2.2 Definition of the tail on the right
nodes.label: estfz

nodes.name: Tail solution q_0
nodes.statement:
Let $q_0$ be the solution of 
\begin{equation} \partial_t q_0 + \partial_x(\partial_x^2 q_0 + q_0^5)=0,\quad
 q_0(0,x)= f_0(x).
\end{equation}

nodes.name: Equation of q_0
nodes.statement: \partial_t q_0 + \partial_x(\partial_x^2 q_0 + q_0^5)=0,\quad q_0(0,x)= f_0(x).

nodes.name: Asymptotic behavior of q_0
nodes.statement: The solution $q_0$ of \eqref{defqz} is global, smooth and bounded in $H^1$. Moreover, $\forall t\geq 0,\ \forall x>\frac t 2+\frac {x_0}2$, \begin{equation} \forall k\geq 0,\quad |\partial_x^k q_0(t,x) -f_0^{(k)}(x) | \lesssim t^{\frac 38} x^{-\theta-\frac {19}8 - k } \lesssim x^{-\theta-2 - k }, \end{equation} \begin{equation} |\partial_tq_0(t,x) | \lesssim x^{-\theta-3} . \end{equation}
nodes.section: 2.2 Definition of the tail on the right
conclusions: The solution $q_0$ of \eqref{defqz} is global, smooth and bounded  in $H^1$.
nodes.statement_short: q_0 is global and keeps the x^{-theta} tail of f_0 for x > t/2 + x_0/2, up to lower order errors.

nodes.name: Tail persistence estimate
nodes.statement: \forall k\geq 0,\quad |\partial_x^k q_0(t,x) -f_0^{(k)}(x) | \lesssim t^{\frac 38} x^{-\theta-\frac {19}8 - k } \lesssim x^{-\theta-2 - k },

nodes.name: Parameters c_0, lambda_0, x_0
nodes.statement: Let $c_0\in \mathbb{R}$, $\lambda_0\ll 1$ and $x_0\gg 1$.

nodes.name: Tail-subtracted solution w
w close to Q
nodes.statement:
We assume that $w$ is close to $Q$ in the following sense : there exist $(\lambda_1(t),x_1(t))\in \mathbb{R}^*_+\times \mathbb{R}$ and $\varepsilon_1(t)$ such that
\begin{align} \forall t\in [0,t_0], \ \ &
\lambda_1(t)<\frac {10}9 \lambda_0,\quad x_1(t)> \frac 9{10} x_0,
\\ & w(t,x)=\frac{1}{\lambda^{\frac 12}_1(t)}(Q+\varepsilon_1)\left(t,\frac{x-x_1(t)}{\lambda_1(t)}\right)
\end{align}
with 
\begin{equation} \forall t\in [0,t_0],\ \
 \|\varepsilon_1(t)\|_{L^2}+\left(\int (\partial_y \varepsilon_1)^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{2}} dy \right)^{\frac 12}\leq \alpha^*
\end{equation}
for some small enough universal constant $\alpha^*>0$.

nodes.name: A priori decomposition of w
nodes.statement: \forall t\in [0,t_0], \ \ & \lambda_1(t)<\frac {10}9 \lambda_0,\quad x_1(t)> \frac 9{10} x_0, \\ & w(t,x)=\frac{1}{\lambda^{\frac 12}_1(t)}(Q+\varepsilon_1)\left(t,\frac{x-x_1(t)}{\lambda_1(t)}\right)

assumptions: Assume {\rm (\ref{decompo0})}--{\rm (\ref{hypeprochien})} for $\alpha^*$ small enough, and assume $x_0$ large enough and $\lambda_0$ small enough.
conclusions: There exist $\mathcal C^1$ functions $({\lambda}, x,{b}):[0,t_0]\to (0,+\infty)\times \mathbb{R}^2$ such that

Here, we will treat only the terms coming from $q$ and $pY_0$ in \eqref{eqofeps} and we refer the reader to \cite{MMR1} for more details on the other terms. \medskip \emph{Proof of \eqref{eq:2002bis} and \eqref{eq:2003}.} It follows from computations in \cite{MMR1} proof of Lemma~2.7 and Claim ef{cl:one} that  egin{align*} & \left| \left( { rac{{\lambda}_s}{{\lambda}}} + {b} ight) -  rac {( \varepsilon,L(\Lambda Q)')}{\|\Lambda Q\|_{L^2}^2} ight| \ & \lesssim \left( \left| { rac{{\lambda}_s}{{\lambda}}}+ {b} ight| +|b|ight)\left(|p|+ |b| + \left( \int \varepsilon^2 {e^{- rac{|y|}{10}}} ight)^{ rac 12} ight) + |p| \left( \int \varepsilon^2 {e^{- rac{|y|}{10}}} ight)^{ rac 12} \ & + \left| { rac{x_s}{{\lambda}}} - 1 ight| \left( |b| + \left( \int \varepsilon^2 {e^{- rac{|y|}{10}}} ight)^{ rac 12} ight) +|p_s|+|{b}_{s}|+\int \varepsilon^2 e^{- rac{|y|}{10}} + p^8 +  rac {\lambda}{x} |p| . \end{align*} We proceed similarly for $ rac{x_s}{\lambda}-1$, taking into account different cancellations due to parity properties  egin{align*} & \left|\left( { rac{x_s}{{\lambda}}} - 1 ight) -  rac {( \varepsilon,L(y \Lambda Q)')}{\|\Lambda Q\|_{L^2}^2} ight| \ & \lesssim \left( \left| { rac{{\lambda}_s}{{\lambda}}}+ {b} ight| + \left| { rac{x_s}{{\lambda}}} - 1 ight| +|b|ight)\left(|p|+|b| + \left( \int \varepsilon^2 {e^{- rac{|y|}{10}}} ight)^{ rac 12} ight) \ &+|{b}_{s}|+\int \varepsilon^2 e^{- rac{|y|}{10}} +p^2 + rac \lambda x |p|. \end{align*} Then, taking the scalar product of \eqref{eqofeps} by $Q$ and arguing similarly, we have the following rough estimate for $b_s$:  egin{align*} |{b}_{s}| &\lesssim \left| { rac{{\lambda}_s}{{\lambda}}} + {b}ight|^2 + \left| { rac{x_s}{{\lambda}}} - 1 ight|^2 + {|b|}^2 + \int \varepsilon^2 {e^{- rac{|y|}{10}}} + |p| \left( \int \varepsilon^2 {e^{- rac{|y|}{10}}} ight)^{ rac 12} \ &+|p_s| + |b| |p| +p^8 + rac \lambda x |p| . \end{align*} Combining these estimates with (from \eqref{cl.2bis}) $$ |p_s| \leq \left|  rac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} ight| |p| +  rac {\lambda}{x} |p|\left( \left| rac{x_s}{\lambda} - 1ight| + 1 ight) \leq |b| |p| +\left|  rac{\lambda_s}{\lambda}+bight| |p| +  rac \lambda x |p|\left( \left| rac{x_s}{\lambda} - 1ight| + 1 ight), $$ from \eqref{cl.2tri}, we obtain \eqref{eq:2002bis} and \eqref{eq:2003}. \medskip \emph{Proof of \eqref{fond}.} First, we derive a refined equation for $b_s$, taking the scalar product of equation \eqref{eqofeps} by $Q$ and proceeding as in \cite{MMR1}, proof of Lemma 2.7. Recall from \cite{MMR1}, $$(\Psi_b,Q)= - rac {b^2}{8} \|Q\|_{L^1}^2 + O(|b|^3),\quad (\Phi_b, Q) = - rac {b_s}{16} \|Q\|_{L^1}^2 +O(|b|^{10}). $$ Note also that from direct computations and parity properties  egin{align*} &\left|\left( ((\varepsilon+pY_0 + Q_b)^5 - Q_b^5 - p5Q^4 Y_0 - 5Q^4 \varepsilon)_y,Qight) - 20 bp((Q^3Y_0 P )_y,Q) ight| \ &+ \left| \left((\widetilde W)_y,Qight)-20 bp (( P Q^3)_y,Q)ight|\ & \lesssim |b|^3 +|p|^3 + \int \varepsilon^2 {e^{- rac{|y|}{10}}} + (|p|+|b|) \left(\int \varepsilon^2 {e^{- rac{|y|}{10}}} ight)^{ rac 12} . \end{align*} (See \cite{MMR1} for details on the nonlinear terms in $\varepsilon$.) Using \eqref{cl.4bis} and the above estimates we find egin{align} & igg| b_s + 2b^2 -  rac {16}{(\int Q)^2}  igg( - p_s (Y_0,Q) -  rac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} p (Y_0,\Lambda Q) 
onumber\ & - bp \left[ 20 ((Q^3Y_0 P)_y,Q) + 20 ((PQ^3)_y,Q) ight] + c_0 	heta \left(\int Qight) \lambda^{ rac 32}(s) x^{-	heta-1}(s)  igg) igg|\ & \lesssim |b|^3+ |p|^3 +\int \varepsilon^2 {e^{- rac{|y|}{10}}} +(|p|+|b|) \left(\int \varepsilon^2 {e^{- rac{|y|}{10}}} ight)^{ rac 12} + rac {\lambda^2}{x^2} |p|+ rac {\lambda}{x^3} |p|. \end{align} We claim the following cancellation  egin{equation} - (Y_0,\Lambda Q) + 20 ((Q^3Y_0 P)_y,Q) + 20 ((PQ^3)_y,Q) =0. \end{equation} Indeed, $L(P')= (LP)' + 20 Q^3 Q' P = \Lambda Q + 20 Q^3 Q' P,$ and so from \eqref{eq:23},  egin{align*} & - (Y_0,\Lambda Q) + 20 ((Q^3Y_0 P)_y,Q) + 20 ((PQ^3)_y,Q) \ &= - (Y_0,\Lambda Q)- 20 (Y_0+1,PQ^3 Q')\ & = - (Y_0+1 , L(P')) + \int \Lambda Q = - (L(Y_0+1),P') -  rac 12 \int Q \ & = - \int P' -  rac 12 \int Q = P(-\infty) -  rac 12 \int Q =0. \end{align*} Thus,  egin{align*} & \left| -  rac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} p (Y_0,\Lambda Q) + bp \left[ 20 ((Q^3Y_0 P)_y,Q) + 20 ((PQ^3)_y,Q) ight] ight| = |p| \left|  rac{\lambda_s}{\lambda}+b ight| |(Y_0,\Lambda Q)|. \end{align*} \medskip Now, from $(Y_0,Q) =-  rac 34 \int Q$ (see \eqref{YQ}), using \eqref{cl.1bis} and \eqref{cl.2bis} we note that  egin{align} &  rac {16}{(\int Q)^2}  igg( - p_s (Y_0,Q)+ c_0 	heta \left(\int Qight) \lambda^{ rac 32}(s) x^{-	heta-1}(s)  igg)
onumber \ & =  rac {12}{(\int Q)} c_0 \lambda^{ rac 12} x^{-	heta} \left(  rac 12  rac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} + rac 	heta 3  rac {x_s}{x} ight) +O\left( rac {\lambda}{x^{3}}| p|ight) + O\left(  rac {\lambda}{x} |p| \left| rac{x_s}{\lambda}-1ight|ight). \end{align} Therefore,  egin{align} & igg| b_s + 2b^2 -  rac {4}{(\int Q)} c_0 \lambda^{ rac 12} x^{-	heta} \left(  rac 32  rac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} + 	heta  rac {x_s}{x} ight)  igg| 
onumber \ & \lesssim |b|^3 +|p|^3 + \int \varepsilon^2 {e^{- rac{|y|}{10}}} + (|p|+|b|) \left(\int \varepsilon^2 {e^{- rac{|y|}{10}}} ight)^{ rac 12} +  rac {\lambda^2}{x^2} |p| +  rac {\lambda}{x^3} |p| . \end{align} Now, we prove \eqref{fond}. By direct computation, $$  rac d{ds}\left(  rac 4{\left(\int Qight)}c_0 	heta \lambda^{- rac 32}(s) x^{-	heta}ight) = -  rac {4}{(\int Q)} c_0 \lambda^{- rac 32} x^{-	heta} \left(  rac 32  rac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} + 	heta  rac {x_s}{x} ight) $$ $$  rac d{ds}\left(  rac b{\lambda^2}ight) =  rac {b_s}{\lambda^2} - 2  rac{\lambda_s}{\lambda}  rac b{\lambda^2} =  rac {b_s}{\lambda^2} + 2  rac {b^2}{\lambda^2} - 2 \left(  rac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} +bight)  rac b{\lambda^2}.$$ and \eqref{fond} follows from \eqref{eq:b} and \eqref{eq:2002bis}.
nodes.statement_short: Implicit function theorem for the decomposition; conservation laws for (ii); projecting the eps equation on Q, Lambda Q, yLambda Q for (iii). The key step is the cancellation (cancel) of the p-terms in the b_s equation.

nodes.name: Decomposition of u
nodes.statement: u(t,x) & = \frac 1{\lambda^{\frac 12}(t)} \left( Q_{b(t)} + p(t) Y_0+ \varepsilon \right) \left( t,\frac {x-x(t)}{\lambda(t)}\right) +q_0(t,x) \\ & = \frac 1{\lambda^{\frac 12}(t)} \left( Q_{b(t)} + p(t) Y_0+ \varepsilon + q \right) \left(t, \frac {x-x(t)}{\lambda(t)}\right).
nodes.label: dec:2

nodes.name: Equation of eps_Y
nodes.statement: \nonumber \partial_s \varepsilon_Y & = (-\partial_{y}^2 \varepsilon_Y + \varepsilon_Y - (\varepsilon_Y+Q_b)^5 +Q_b^5)_y - (5 Q^4 q)_y +\frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} \Lambda \varepsilon_Y \\ & + \left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right) {\Lambda} Q_b + \left(\frac { x_{s}}{\lambda} -1\right) (Q_b + \varepsilon_Y)_y + \Phi_{b} + \Psi_{{b}} -W_y,
nodes.label: eqofepsY

nodes.name: Equation of eps
nodes.statement: \nonumber \partial_s \varepsilon & = \left(-\partial_{y}^2 \varepsilon + \varepsilon - (\varepsilon +p Y_0 +Q_b)^5 +Q_b^5 + p5Q^4 Y_0\right)_y \\ & -p_s Y_0 +( 5 Q^4 (p-q) )_y +\frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} (\Lambda \varepsilon+p\Lambda Y_0) + \left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right) {\Lambda} Q_b \nonumber \\ &+ \left(\frac { x_{s}}{\lambda} -1\right) (Q_b + \varepsilon+p Y_0)_y + \Phi_{b} + \Psi_{{b}} -W_y,
nodes.label: eqofeps

nodes.name: Claim 1: estimates on q, p and W
nodes.statement: {\rm (a) Estimates on $q(s)$.} \begin{equation} \|q(s)\|_{L^2} \lesssim x_0^{-\theta+\frac 12}, \quad \|q_y(s)\|_{L^2}\lesssim \lambda(s) x_0^{-\theta-\frac 12}, \quad \|q(s)\|_{L^\infty}\lesssim \lambda^{\frac 12} (s) x_0^{-\theta}. \end{equation} {\rm (b) Properties of the function $p(s)$:} \begin{equation} \left|p(s) - c_0 \lambda^{\frac 12}(s) x^{-\theta}(s)\right| \lesssim c_0 \lambda^{\frac 12}(s) x^{-\theta-2}(s)\lesssim x^{-2}(s) |p(s)|, \end{equation} \begin{equation} e^{-\frac{3|y|}{4}} |p(s)-q(s,y)| \lesssim \frac {\lambda(s)}{x(s)} |p(s)| e^{-\frac {|y|} 4} , \end{equation} \begin{equation} \left| \left( (5Q^4(p-q))_y ,Q\right) - c_0 \left( \int Q\right) \theta \lambda^{-\frac 32} x^{-\theta-1} \right| \lesssim \frac {\lambda^2(s)}{x^2(s)} |p(s)|+\frac {\lambda(s)}{x^3(s)} |p(s)|, \end{equation} \begin{equation} \left| p_s - \frac 12 \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} p + \theta \frac {x_s} x p \right| \leq \frac {\lambda}{x^{3}}|p| \left(\left|\frac{x_s}{\lambda} - 1\right| + 1 \right), \end{equation} \begin{equation} |p_s| \lesssim \left| \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda}\right| |p| + \frac {\lambda}{x} |p| \left(\left|\frac{x_s}{\lambda} - 1\right| + 1 \right). \end{equation} {\rm (c) Estimates for the remainder term $W$:} Let \begin{align*} \widetilde W&=5(Q_b+ \varepsilon+p Y_0)^4 p- 5 Q^4 p + 10(Q_b+\varepsilon+p Y_0)^3 p^2 \\ &+ 10(Q_b+\varepsilon+p Y_0)^2 p^3 + 5(Q_b+\varepsilon+p Y_0) p^4. \end{align*} Then, \begin{equation} \int |W-\widetilde W| e^{-\frac 34 {|y|}} \lesssim \left( |p|+|b| + \left( \int \varepsilon^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{10}} \right)^{\frac 12}\right) \frac {\lambda}{x} |p| , \end{equation} \begin{equation} |((\widetilde W)_y,\Lambda Q)|+|((\widetilde W)_y,Q)|\lesssim b^2 + p^8 +|b| |p| +|p| \left(\int \varepsilon^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{10}}\right)^{\frac 12} +\int \varepsilon^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{10}} , \end{equation} \begin{equation} |((\widetilde W)_y,y \Lambda Q)| \lesssim \int \varepsilon^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{10}} + b^2 + p^2. \end{equation}
conclusions: {\rm (a) Estimates on $q(s)$.}
nodes.statement_short: Bounds on q, the function p(s) ~ c_0 lambda^{1/2} x^{-theta}, its derivative, and the remainder W.
nodes.label: cl:one

nodes.name: Norms of q
nodes.statement: \|q(s)\|_{L^2} \lesssim x_0^{-\theta+\frac 12}, \quad \|q_y(s)\|_{L^2}\lesssim \lambda(s) x_0^{-\theta-\frac 12}, \quad \|q(s)\|_{L^\infty}\lesssim \lambda^{\frac 12} (s) x_0^{-\theta}.
nodes.label: L2H1q

nodes.name: Asymptotics of p
nodes.statement: \left|p(s) - c_0 \lambda^{\frac 12}(s) x^{-\theta}(s)\right| \lesssim c_0 \lambda^{\frac 12}(s) x^{-\theta-2}(s)\lesssim x^{-2}(s) |p(s)|,
nodes.label: cl.1bis

nodes.name: p - q localized
nodes.statement: e^{-\frac{3|y|}{4}} |p(s)-q(s,y)| \lesssim \frac {\lambda(s)}{x(s)} |p(s)| e^{-\frac {|y|} 4} ,
nodes.label: cl.2

nodes.name: Projection of (5Q^4(p-q))_y on Q
nodes.statement: \left| \left( (5Q^4(p-q))_y ,Q\right) - c_0 \left( \int Q\right) \theta \lambda^{-\frac 32} x^{-\theta-1} \right| \lesssim \frac {\lambda^2(s)}{x^2(s)} |p(s)|+\frac {\lambda(s)}{x^3(s)} |p(s)|,
nodes.label: cl.4bis

nodes.name: Equation for p_s
nodes.statement: \left| p_s - \frac 12 \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} p + \theta \frac {x_s} x p \right| \leq \frac {\lambda}{x^{3}}|p| \left(\left|\frac{x_s}{\lambda} - 1\right| + 1 \right),
nodes.label: cl.2bis

nodes.name: Bound on p_s
nodes.statement: |p_s| \lesssim \left| \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda}\right| |p| + \frac {\lambda}{x} |p| \left(\left|\frac{x_s}{\lambda} - 1\right| + 1 \right).
nodes.label: cl.2tri

nodes.name: W minus tilde W
nodes.statement: \int |W-\widetilde W| e^{-\frac 34 {|y|}} \lesssim \left( |p|+|b| + \left( \int \varepsilon^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{10}} \right)^{\frac 12}\right) \frac {\lambda}{x} |p| ,
nodes.label: cl.3

nodes.name: Projections of tilde W
nodes.statement: |((\widetilde W)_y,\Lambda Q)|+|((\widetilde W)_y,Q)|\lesssim b^2 + p^8 +|b| |p| +|p| \left(\int \varepsilon^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{10}}\right)^{\frac 12} +\int \varepsilon^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{10}} ,
nodes.label: cl.4

nodes.name: Projection of tilde W on yLambdaQ
nodes.statement: |((\widetilde W)_y,y \Lambda Q)| \lesssim \int \varepsilon^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{10}} + b^2 + p^2.
nodes.label: cl.5

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 1
nodes.statement:
{\it Proof of} (a). Since $q_0(t)$ is solution of \eqref{kdv}, for all $t$, $$ \|q_0(t)\|_{L^2}= \|f_0\|_{L^2} \lesssim x_0^{-	heta+ rac 12},\quad E(q_0(t)) = E(f_0) \lesssim x_0^{-	heta-  rac 12}, $$ and \eqref{L2H1q} follows.\ {\it Proof of} (b). Since $p(s) = \lambda^{ rac 12}(s) q_0(s,x(s))$, \eqref{cl.1bis} follows from \eqref{surX} and \eqref{leqz3}. In particular, since $c_0<0$, $p<0$. Next, by \eqref{surX}, \eqref{leqz3} and \eqref{estfz}, splitting the two cases $\lambda |y|< rac {x(s)}{4}$ and $\lambda |y| >  rac {x(s)}{4}$, we have  egin{align} & e^{- rac{3|y|}{4}} |p(s)-q(s,y)| = e^{- rac{3|y|}{4}} \lambda^{ rac 12}(s) |q_0(s,x(s))-q_0(s,\lambda(s) y +x(s))| 
onumber\ &\lesssim |y| e^{-  rac {|y|} 2 } \lambda^{ rac 32}(s) \left( e^{-  rac { |y|} 4} \|q_0'(s)\|_{L^\infty(x> rac 34 x(s))} + e^{- rac {x(s)}{16\lambda(s)}}\|q_0'(s)\|_{L^\infty} ight)
onumber \ & \lesssim c_0 e^{- rac {|y|} 4} \lambda^{ rac 32}(s) \left( x^{-	heta-1}(s) + e^{- rac {x(s)}{16\lambda(s)}} x_0^{-	heta-1} ight)
onumber \ &\lesssim c_0 e^{- rac {|y|} 4} \lambda^{ rac 32}(s) x^{-	heta-1}(s) \lesssim  rac {\lambda}{x} |p| e^{- rac {|y|} 4}.\end{align} Next, by \eqref{surX} and \eqref{leqz3},  egin{align*} &\left( (5Q^4(p-q))_y ,Qight) = -5 \int Q^4 Q_y (p-q)= -\int Q^5 q_y \ &= -\lambda^{ rac 32}(s) \int Q^5(y) \partial_x q_0(s,\lambda(s) y +x(s)) dy\ &= - \lambda^{ rac 32} f_0'( x(s)) \int Q^5 - \lambda^{ rac 32} \int Q^5 \left(f_0'(\lambda y + x(s)) -f_0'(x(s))ight)dy \ & -\lambda^{ rac 32}(s) \int Q^5(y) \left( \partial_x q_0(s,\lambda(s) y +x(s) )-f_0'(\lambda y+x(s))ight) dy\ & =c_0 \left( \int Qight) 	heta \lambda^{ rac 32}(s) x^{-	heta -1}(s) + O\left( \lambda^{ rac 32}e^{- rac 54 x(s) } ight) + O\left( \lambda^{ rac 52} x^{-	heta-2}ight) +O\left( \lambda^{ rac 32} x^{-	heta-3}(s)ight)\ & =c_0 \left( \int Qight) 	heta \lambda^{ rac 32}(s) x^{-	heta -1}(s) + O\left( rac {\lambda^2}{x^2} |p| ight) + O\left( rac {\lambda}{x^3} |p| ight), \end{align*} where we have split the integrals above into $|y| > rac 14 x(s)$ and $|y|< rac 14 x(s)$ and using the fact that for $|y|< rac 14 x(s)$, $\lambda y + x(s) >x(s)-|y|>  rac 34 x(s) >  rac 12 t +  rac 12 x_0$, so that \eqref{leqz3} holds for $x= \lambda y + x(s)$, and {m (ef{cl.4bis})} is proved.\ Now, we prove \eqref{cl.2bis}. By explicit differentiation and Lemma ef{le:qz},  egin{align*} p_s -  rac 12  rac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} p & = \lambda^{ rac 12}(q_0)_s(s,x(s)) + \lambda^{ rac 12} x_s \partial_x q_0(s,x(s))\ & = \lambda^{ rac 72} (q_0)_t(s,x(s)) + \lambda^{ rac 12} x_s f_0'(x(s)) + O\left(  rac {\lambda}{x^{3}} |p| \left(\left| rac{x_s}{\lambda} - 1ight| + 1 ight) ight)\ & = -	heta  rac {x_s} x |p| + O\left(  rac {\lambda}{x^{3}} |p| \left(\left| rac{x_s}{\lambda} - 1ight| + 1 ight) ight). \end{align*} Since $|x_s| \leq \lambda (| rac{x_s}{\lambda} -1| + 1)$, \eqref{cl.2tri} follows.\ {\it Proof of} (c). For \eqref{cl.3}, we first note  egin{align*} \widetilde W - W &=5\left[(Q_b+ \varepsilon+p Y_0)^4 - Q^4ight] (p-q) + 10(Q_b+\varepsilon+p Y_0)^3 (p^2-q^2) \ &+ 10(Q_b+\varepsilon+p Y_0)^2 (p^3-q^3) + 5(Q_b+\varepsilon+p Y_0) (p^4-q^4). \end{align*} Thus,  egin{align*} & \int e^{- rac 34 {|y|}} |W-\widetilde W| \ &\lesssim \left( |p|+|b| ight) \int e^{-  rac 34 {|y|}} |p-q| + \left( \int \varepsilon^2 e^{- rac {|y|}{10}} ight)^{ rac 12}\left( \int e^{-( rac 32- rac 1{10}) {|y|}} |p-q|^2ight)^{ rac 12} \ & + \int e^{- rac 34 {|y|}} |p^2-q^2| \lesssim \left( |p|+|b| + \left( \int \varepsilon^2 e^{- rac {|y|}{10}} ight)^{ rac 12}ight)  rac {\lambda}{x}|p|, \end{align*} using \eqref{cl.2}, and the following similar estimate $$ e^{- rac 34 {|y|}} |p^2-q^2| \lesssim  rac {\lambda}{x} p^2 e^{- rac {|y|}{4}}. $$ Next, \eqref{cl.4} follows from the parity properties and then direct estimates. \eqref{cl.5} follows from direct estimates. Note that $p^2$ appears in \eqref{cl.5} because there is no cancellation due to parity for this term. This concludes the proof of Claim ef{cl:one}.
nodes.statement_short: Direct estimates from conservation laws for q_0, Lemma 2.3 asymptotics of the tail, and parity.

nodes.name: Estimate of p - q
nodes.statement:
& e^{- rac{3|y|}{4}} |p(s)-q(s,y)| = e^{- rac{3|y|}{4}} \lambda^{ rac 12}(s) |q_0(s,x(s))-q_0(s,\lambda(s) y +x(s))| 
onumber\ &\lesssim |y| e^{-  rac {|y|} 2 } \lambda^{ rac 32}(s) \left( e^{-  rac { |y|} 4} \|q_0'(s)\|_{L^\infty(x> rac 34 x(s))} + e^{- rac {x(s)}{16\lambda(s)}}\|q_0'(s)\|_{L^\infty} ight)
onumber \ & \lesssim c_0 e^{- rac {|y|} 4} \lambda^{ rac 32}(s) \left( x^{-	heta-1}(s) + e^{- rac {x(s)}{16\lambda(s)}} x_0^{-	heta-1} ight)
onumber \ &\lesssim c_0 e^{- rac {|y|} 4} \lambda^{ rac 32}(s) x^{-	heta-1}(s) \lesssim  rac {\lambda}{x} |p| e^{- rac {|y|} 4}.
nodes.label: pmq

nodes.name: Refined b_s equation
nodes.statement: &\bigg| b_s + 2b^2 - \frac {16}{(\int Q)^2} \bigg( - p_s (Y_0,Q) - \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} p (Y_0,\Lambda Q) \nonumber\\ & - bp \left[ 20 ((Q^3Y_0 P)_y,Q) + 20 ((PQ^3)_y,Q) \right] + c_0 \theta \left(\int Q\right) \lambda^{\frac 32}(s) x^{-\theta-1}(s) \bigg)\bigg|\\ & \lesssim |b|^3+ |p|^3 +\int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}} +(|p|+|b|) \left(\int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}} \right)^{\frac 12} +\frac {\lambda^2}{x^2} |p|+\frac {\lambda}{x^3} |p|.
nodes.label: eq:bautre

nodes.name: Non-cancelling p_s term
nodes.statement: & \frac {16}{(\int Q)^2} \bigg( - p_s (Y_0,Q)+ c_0 \theta \left(\int Q\right) \lambda^{\frac 32}(s) x^{-\theta-1}(s) \bigg)\nonumber \\ & = \frac {12}{(\int Q)} c_0 \lambda^{\frac 12} x^{-\theta} \left( \frac 12 \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} +\frac \theta 3 \frac {x_s}{x} \right) +O\left(\frac {\lambda}{x^{3}}| p|\right) + O\left( \frac {\lambda}{x} |p| \left|\frac{x_s}{\lambda}-1\right|\right).
nodes.label: pascancel

nodes.name: Equation for b_s with tail
nodes.statement: &\bigg| b_s + 2b^2 - \frac {4}{(\int Q)} c_0 \lambda^{\frac 12} x^{-\theta} \left( \frac 32 \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} + \theta \frac {x_s}{x} \right) \bigg| \nonumber \\ & \lesssim |b|^3 +|p|^3 + \int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}} + (|p|+|b|) \left(\int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}} \right)^{\frac 12} + \frac {\lambda^2}{x^2} |p| + \frac {\lambda}{x^3} |p| .
nodes.label: eq:b

nodes.name: Exponents beta, theta and constant c_0
nodes.statement:
Let $$
\beta =   \frac { 2(\theta-1)} {2\theta-1},\quad
\theta = \frac {1-\frac \beta2}{1-\beta}, \quad 0< \beta< \frac {11}{20}, \quad
1<\theta <\frac {29}{18},$$ and define
\begin{equation} c_0=-\frac {\int Q}2(\theta-1)(2\theta-1)^{\theta-1}.
\end{equation}

nodes.name: Choice of c_0
nodes.statement: c_0=-\frac {\int Q}2(\theta-1)(2\theta-1)^{\theta-1}.
nodes.label: defcobeta

nodes.name: Functions g and f
nodes.statement:
Given $s>s_0$, $(b(s),\lambda(s),x(s))\in \mathbb{R}^*_+\times \mathbb{R}^*_+\times \mathbb{R}$, we define:
 $$
g(s) =\frac {b(s)}{\lambda^2(s)} + \frac 4{\int Q} c_0   \lambda^{-\frac 32}(s) x^{-\theta}(s),\quad
f(s) =   \lambda^{\frac 12} (s) + \frac 2 {\int Q} c_0 \frac {1}{\theta-1} {x^{-\theta+1}(s)}.
$$

nodes.name: Weight functions phi_i and psi
nodes.statement:
Let  $(\varphi_i)_{i=1,2},\psi$  be smooth functions such that:
\begin{eqnarray} \varphi_i(y) =\left\{\begin{array}{lll}e^{y}\ \ \mbox{for} \ \   y<-1,\\
 1+y  \ \ \mbox{for}\ \ -\frac 12<y<\frac 12,\\ 
 y^i\ \ \mbox{for}\ \ \mbox{for}\ \ y>2,
 \end{array}\right.  \ \ \varphi_i'(y) >0, \ \ \forall y\in \mathbb{R},
\end{eqnarray}
\begin{eqnarray} \psi(y) =\left\{\begin{array}{ll} e^{2y}\ \ \mbox{for}   \ \ y<-1,\\
 1  \ \ \mbox{for}\ \ y>-\tfrac 12,\end{array}\right.  \ \ \psi'(y) \geq 0 \ \ \forall y\in \mathbb{R}.
\end{eqnarray}

nodes.name: Weight phi_i
nodes.statement: \varphi_i(y) =\left\{\begin{array}{lll}e^{y}\ \ \mbox{for} \ \ y<-1,\\ 1+y \ \ \mbox{for}\ \ -\frac 12<y<\frac 12,\\ y^i\ \ \mbox{for}\ \ \mbox{for}\ \ y>2, \end{array}\right. \ \ \varphi_i'(y) >0, \ \ \forall y\in \mathbb{R},
nodes.label: defphi1bis

nodes.name: Weight psi
nodes.statement: \psi(y) =\left\{\begin{array}{ll} e^{2y}\ \ \mbox{for} \ \ y<-1,\\ 1 \ \ \mbox{for}\ \ y>-\tfrac 12,\end{array}\right. \ \ \psi'(y) \geq 0 \ \ \forall y\in \mathbb{R}.
nodes.label: defphi2

nodes.name: Rescaled weights and norms N_i, N_i,loc
nodes.statement:
Let $B> 100$ and
 $$\psi_B(y)=\psi\left(\frac yB\right), \ \ \varphi_{i,B}=\varphi_i\left(\frac yB\right), \ \ i=1,2,$$ 
 and define the following norms on $\varepsilon$
  \begin{equation} {\mathcal{N}_i}  (s)  = \int  \varepsilon_y^2(s,y) \psi_{B}(y)dy + \int  \varepsilon^2(s,y) \varphi_{i,B}(y)   dy, 
\end{equation} 
\begin{equation} {\mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}} (s)  =    \int\varepsilon^2 (s,y)     \varphi'_{i,B} (y) dy,\quad i=1,2.
\end{equation}

nodes.name: Norm N_i
nodes.statement: {\mathcal{N}_i} (s) = \int \varepsilon_y^2(s,y) \psi_{B}(y)dy + \int \varepsilon^2(s,y) \varphi_{i,B}(y) dy,
nodes.label: eq:no

nodes.name: Local norm N_i,loc
nodes.statement: {\mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}} (s) = \int\varepsilon^2 (s,y) \varphi'_{i,B} (y) dy,\quad i=1,2.
nodes.label: eq:noloc

nodes.name: Bootstrap
nodes.statement: Let $s_0=s_0(\beta)>1$ large enough and set \begin{equation} x_0= x (s_0)= \frac 1{(1-\beta)}{s_0^{1-\beta}}. \end{equation} Let $\varepsilon_0\in H^1$ be such that \begin{equation} s_0^{10}\left[ \int_{y>0} y^{10} \varepsilon^2_0(y) dy+\|\varepsilon_0\|^2_{H^1} \right]<1, \quad (\varepsilon_0, y {\Lambda} Q )=(\varepsilon_0,\Lambda Q) =(\varepsilon_0,Q)=0.\end{equation} Then, there exists \begin{equation} (\lambda_0,b_0)\in\mathcal D =\left \{(\lambda,b) \ : \ | \lambda - s_0^{-\beta}| \leq s_0^{-\beta - \frac 1{10}}, \ |b - \beta s_0^{-1}| \leq s_0^{-1-\frac 1{10}}\right\}, \end{equation} such that the solution of \eqref{kdv} with initial data \begin{equation} u_0(x) = \frac 1{\lambda^{\frac 12}_0} \left( Q_{b_0} + \lambda^{\frac 12}_0 q_0(s_0,x_0) Y_0+ \varepsilon_0 \right) \left( \frac {x-x_0}{\lambda_0}\right) +q_0(s_0,x) \end{equation} has a decomposition $(b(s),\lambda(s),x(s), \varepsilon(s))$ as in Proposition \ref{le:2} which satisfies\footnote{recall that $s=s(t)$ is the rescaled time {\rm (\ref{rescaledtime})}.} on $[s_0,+\infty)$: $$\leqno{\rm (BS1)}\quad \left(|g(s)| s^{1 - 2 \beta + \frac 15} \right)^2+ \left(|f(s)| s^{\frac \beta 2 + \frac 1{10}}\right)^2\leq 1; $$ $$\leqno{\rm (BS2)}\quad |b(s)|\leq {10} s^{-1}, \ \frac 1{10} s^{-\beta}\leq \lambda(s) \leq 10 s^{-\beta}, \ \frac 1{10} s^{1-\beta} \leq (1-\beta) x(s) \leq 10 s^{1-\beta}; $$ $$\leqno{\rm (BS3)}\quad \int_{y>0}y^{10}\varepsilon^2(s,y)dy\leq 10 \lambda^{-10} ,\quad \mathcal N_{i}(s) \leq s^{-\frac 52},\quad \|\varepsilon(s)\|_{H^1} \lesssim \delta(\alpha^*). $$ Moreover, \begin{equation} \left| \frac {(1-\beta)}{s^{1-\beta}} x (s) - 1\right| +\left| s^{\beta} \lambda(s) -1\right| +\left| \frac {s}{\beta } b(s) -1\right| \lesssim s^{-\frac 1{10}}, \end{equation} \begin{equation} \lambda^{-1} \|\varepsilon_y(s)\|_{L^2}+ \|\varepsilon(s)\|_{L^2} \lesssim 1. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: For suitable initial (lambda_0,b_0) the solution satisfies the bootstrap bounds for all s and lambda ~ s^{-beta}, b ~ beta/s, x ~ s^{1-beta}/(1-beta).
nodes.label: PR:BS

nodes.name: Smallness of eps_0
nodes.statement: s_0^{10}\left[ \int_{y>0} y^{10} \varepsilon^2_0(y) dy+\|\varepsilon_0\|^2_{H^1} \right]<1, \quad (\varepsilon_0, y {\Lambda} Q )=(\varepsilon_0,\Lambda Q) =(\varepsilon_0,Q)=0.
nodes.label: A2

nodes.name: Set D of initial parameters
nodes.statement: (\lambda_0,b_0)\in\mathcal D =\left \{(\lambda,b) \ : \ | \lambda - s_0^{-\beta}| \leq s_0^{-\beta - \frac 1{10}}, \ |b - \beta s_0^{-1}| \leq s_0^{-1-\frac 1{10}}\right\},
nodes.label: estimation2

nodes.name: Initial data u_0
nodes.statement: u_0(x) = \frac 1{\lambda^{\frac 12}_0} \left( Q_{b_0} + \lambda^{\frac 12}_0 q_0(s_0,x_0) Y_0+ \varepsilon_0 \right) \left( \frac {x-x_0}{\lambda_0}\right) +q_0(s_0,x)
nodes.label: defu0

nodes.name: Bootstrap bound (BS1)
nodes.statement: \leqno{\rm (BS1)}\quad \left(|g(s)| s^{1 - 2 \beta + \frac 15} \right)^2+ \left(|f(s)| s^{\frac \beta 2 + \frac 1{10}}\right)^2\leq 1;

nodes.name: Bootstrap bound (BS2)
nodes.statement: \leqno{\rm (BS2)}\quad |b(s)|\leq {10} s^{-1}, \ \frac 1{10} s^{-\beta}\leq \lambda(s) \leq 10 s^{-\beta}, \ \frac 1{10} s^{1-\beta} \leq (1-\beta) x(s) \leq 10 s^{1-\beta};

nodes.name: Bootstrap bound (BS3)
nodes.statement: \leqno{\rm (BS3)}\quad \int_{y>0}y^{10}\varepsilon^2(s,y)dy\leq 10 \lambda^{-10} ,\quad \mathcal N_{i}(s) \leq s^{-\frac 52},\quad \|\varepsilon(s)\|_{H^1} \lesssim \delta(\alpha^*).

nodes.name: Sharp asymptotics of parameters
nodes.statement: \left| \frac {(1-\beta)}{s^{1-\beta}} x (s) - 1\right| +\left| s^{\beta} \lambda(s) -1\right| +\left| \frac {s}{\beta } b(s) -1\right| \lesssim s^{-\frac 1{10}},
nodes.label: sharp

nodes.name: H1 bound on eps
nodes.statement: \lambda^{-1} \|\varepsilon_y(s)\|_{L^2}+ \|\varepsilon(s)\|_{L^2} \lesssim 1.
nodes.label: sharpe

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.1 from Proposition 3.1
nodes.statement: Let us observe that {\rm (\ref{sharp})} now gives the leading order behavior of the scaling parameter $\lambda(s)=\frac{1}{s^{\beta}}(1+o(1))$, and the conclusion of Theorem \ref{th:1} now immediately follow from the change of variables {\rm (\ref{rescaledtime})} depending on the value of $\beta$ as in step (iv) of section \ref{vneovnoen}.
nodes.statement_short: Change of variables dt = lambda^3 ds applied to lambda(s) ~ s^{-beta} gives the regimes of Theorem 1.1.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 3.1 (setup by contradiction)
nodes.statement:
The rest of this section is therefore devoted to the proof of Proposition \ref{PR:BS}. First observe by uniqueness of the decomposition that
$$
b_0=b(s_0),\quad  \lambda(s_0)=\lambda_0 \quad x(s_0)=x_0, \quad \varepsilon(s_0)=\varepsilon_0.
$$
We now argue by contradiction, assuming that for all 
$(\lambda_0,b_0)\in \mathcal D$,    we have
$$
s^*(\lambda_0,b_0) := \mathop{\rm sup} \left\{
s\geq s_0 \hbox{ such that   (BS1)-(BS2)-(BS3) holds on $[s_0,s]$}
\right\} <+\infty.
$$
We will derive a contradiction by first closing the bootstrap bounds (BS1)-(BS2)-(BS3), and then finding a couple $(\lambda_0,b_0)$ using a topological argument.
nodes.statement_short: Argue by contradiction on the exit time s^*; close (BS2)-(BS3), then select (lambda_0,b_0) topologically.

nodes.name: Consequences of the bootstrap estimates
nodes.statement: {\rm (i)} For $s_0=s_0(\beta)$ large enough, there holds: \begin{itemize} \item if $\beta>\frac 13$, for all $s\in (s_0,s^*)$, $t(s)= \int_{s_0}^{s} \lambda^3(s') ds'<1$; \item if $0<\beta\leq \frac 13$, for all $t>0$, $x(t) \geq \frac 23 t + \frac 23 {x_0}$. \end{itemize} {\rm (ii)} For all $s\in (s_0,s^*)$, \begin{equation} 0< -p(s) \lesssim \frac 1 s,\quad \frac {\lambda}{x} \lesssim \frac 1 s, \end{equation} \begin{equation} \left|\frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} +b\right| + \left| \frac{x_s}{\lambda} - 1\right| \lesssim \left(\int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}} \right)^{\frac 12} + \frac 1{s^2},\end{equation} \begin{equation} \left| \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} \right| \lesssim \frac 1 s + \left(\int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}} \right)^{\frac 12},\quad \left| x_s \right| \lesssim s^{-\beta}\left( 1+\left(\int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}} \right)^{\frac 12} \right) , \end{equation} \begin{equation} |b_s|+ |p_s| \lesssim \int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}} + \frac 1{s^2}, \end{equation} \begin{align} & \left| \frac d{ds} \left(\frac b{\lambda^2} +\frac 4{\left(\int Q\right)}c_0 \lambda^{-\frac 32}(s) x^{-\theta}(s)\right) \right| \nonumber \\ &\lesssim \frac 1{\lambda^2} \left( \frac 1{s^{\frac {29}{10}}} + \frac 1 s \left(\int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}} \right)^{\frac 12} + \int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}}\right). \end{align} {\rm (iii)} For all $s\in (s_0,s^*)$, \begin{align} &\|\varepsilon(s)\|_{L^2}^2 \lesssim \left| \int u^2(0) - \int Q^2\right|+ s^{-1} + x_0^{-\theta+\frac 12},\\ & \frac 1{\lambda^2} \|\varepsilon_y(s)\|_{L^2}^2 \lesssim |E(u(0))|+ s^{- \frac 1{10}} + x_0^{-\theta-\frac 12} . \end{align}
nodes.section: 3.2 First consequences of the bootstrap bounds
conclusions: For all $s\in (s_0,s^*)$,
nodes.statement_short: Under the bootstrap bounds: time and position controls, p ~ 1/s, and refined modulation and conservation-law bounds.
nodes.label: le:3.1

nodes.name: Bounds on p and lambda/x
nodes.statement: 0< -p(s) \lesssim \frac 1 s,\quad \frac {\lambda}{x} \lesssim \frac 1 s,
nodes.section: 3.2 First consequences of the bootstrap bounds
nodes.label: BSp

nodes.name: Modulation bound
nodes.statement: \left|\frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} +b\right| + \left| \frac{x_s}{\lambda} - 1\right| \lesssim \left(\int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}} \right)^{\frac 12} + \frac 1{s^2},
nodes.section: 3.2 First consequences of the bootstrap bounds
nodes.label: BSlsl

nodes.name: Bounds on lambda_s and x_s
nodes.statement: \left| \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} \right| \lesssim \frac 1 s + \left(\int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}} \right)^{\frac 12},\quad \left| x_s \right| \lesssim s^{-\beta}\left( 1+\left(\int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}} \right)^{\frac 12} \right) ,
nodes.section: 3.2 First consequences of the bootstrap bounds
nodes.label: BSparam

nodes.name: Bounds on b_s and p_s
nodes.statement: |b_s|+ |p_s| \lesssim \int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}} + \frac 1{s^2},
nodes.section: 3.2 First consequences of the bootstrap bounds
nodes.label: BSbsps

nodes.name: Bound on d/ds of g
nodes.statement: & \left| \frac d{ds} \left(\frac b{\lambda^2} +\frac 4{\left(\int Q\right)}c_0 \lambda^{-\frac 32}(s) x^{-\theta}(s)\right) \right| \nonumber \\ &\lesssim \frac 1{\lambda^2} \left( \frac 1{s^{\frac {29}{10}}} + \frac 1 s \left(\int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}} \right)^{\frac 12} + \int \varepsilon^2 {e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}}\right).
nodes.section: 3.2 First consequences of the bootstrap bounds
nodes.label: BSfond

nodes.name: Conservation law bounds
nodes.statement: &\|\varepsilon(s)\|_{L^2}^2 \lesssim \left| \int u^2(0) - \int Q^2\right|+ s^{-1} + x_0^{-\theta+\frac 12},\\ & \frac 1{\lambda^2} \|\varepsilon_y(s)\|_{L^2}^2 \lesssim |E(u(0))|+ s^{- \frac 1{10}} + x_0^{-\theta-\frac 12} .
nodes.section: 3.2 First consequences of the bootstrap bounds
nodes.label: BSeps

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 2
nodes.statement: Let $\frac 13 <\beta<\frac {11}{20}$. Then $$ t(s) = \int_{s_0}^{s} \lambda^3(s') ds' \leq 10^3 \int_{s_0}^{s} (s')^{-3 \beta} ds' \leq \frac {10^3} {3\beta-1} \left(s_0^{-3\beta+1}-s^{-3\beta +1}\right) <1 $$ for $s_0$ large enough. For $\beta = \frac 13$, $$ t(s) = \int_{s_0}^{s} \lambda^3(s') ds' \leq 10^3\, {\rm log}\frac s{s_0} \quad \hbox{so that} \quad s \geq s_0 e^{10^{-3} t}. $$ Thus, $$ x(s) \geq \frac 3{20} s^{\frac 23} \geq \frac 3{20} s_0^{\frac 23} e^{\frac 23 10^{-3} t}\geq 10 t^3 . $$ for $s_0$ large enough. Since $x(s) \geq \frac 45 x_0$, we obtain $x(t) > t^3 + \frac 12 x_0$. Finally, for $0<\beta <\frac 13$, $$ t(s) = \int_{s_0}^{s} \lambda^3(s') ds' \leq \frac {10^3} {1-3\beta} \left(s^{1-3\beta}-s_0^{1-3\beta}\right) $$ so that for $s_0$ large $$s \geq \left( \frac {(1-3\beta) t}{10^3}+s_0^{1-3\beta}\right)^{\frac 1 {1-3\beta}} \geq 100 t^{\frac {1+\beta}{1-\beta}}, $$ and $$x(s) \geq \frac 3{20} s^{1-\beta} \geq 15 t^{1+\beta}.$$ Since $x(s) \geq \frac 45 x_0$, we obtain $x(t) > t^{1+\beta} + \frac 23 x_0$.\\ The estimate \eqref{BSp} is a consequence of \eqref{cl.1bis} and $\frac \beta 2 + (1-\beta) \theta = 1$, so that $$ 0< p \lesssim \lambda^{\frac 12 } x^{-\theta} (s) \lesssim s^{-\frac \beta 2} s^{-\theta (1-\beta)} \lesssim \frac 1s. $$ The estimates \eqref{BSlsl}-\eqref{BSfond} are immediate consequences of \eqref{eq:2002bis}-\eqref{fond}, \eqref{cl.2tri}, the bootstrap assumptions and the upper bound $\beta<\frac {11}{20}$.
nodes.section: 3.2 First consequences of the bootstrap bounds
nodes.statement_short: Integrate lambda^3 under (BS2) separately for beta>1/3, beta=1/3, beta<1/3; the rest follows from Claim 1 and Prop 2.4.

nodes.name: Improved bootstrap bound (BS3')
nodes.statement:
We now close the bounds on $\varepsilon$ and claim the improved bound: for all $s\in [s_0,s^*]$,
 $$\leqno{\rm (BS3')}\quad
\int_{y>0}y^{10}\varepsilon^2(s,x)dx\leq 5 \lambda^{-10} ,\quad 
\mathcal N_{i}(s) \leq \frac 12 s^{-\frac 52},\quad \|\varepsilon(s)\|_{H^1} \lesssim \delta(\alpha^*).
$$
nodes.statement_short: Under the bootstrap, the weighted tail, N_i norms and H^1 norm of eps satisfy improved bounds.

nodes.name: Improved bound (BS3')
nodes.statement: \leqno{\rm (BS3')}\quad \int_{y>0}y^{10}\varepsilon^2(s,x)dx\leq 5 \lambda^{-10} ,\quad \mathcal N_{i}(s) \leq \frac 12 s^{-\frac 52},\quad \|\varepsilon(s)\|_{H^1} \lesssim \delta(\alpha^*).

nodes.name: Weight phi_10
nodes.statement:
Let $\varphi_{10}$ be a smooth function such that
$$\varphi_{10}(y)=\left\{\begin{array}{ll} 0\ \ \mbox{for}\ \ y\leq 0, \\ y^{10}\ \  \mbox{for}\ \ y\geq 1\end{array}\right., \quad 0\leq \varphi_{10}\lesssim \varphi_{10}' \hbox{ for $0<y<1$}.$$

nodes.name: Dynamical control of the tail on the right
nodes.statement: For all $s\in [s_0,s^*]$,\begin{equation} {\lambda^{-10}}\frac{d}{ds}\left\{\lambda^{10}\int\varphi_{10}\varepsilon^2\right\}\lesssim \mathcal N_{1,\rm loc}+\frac 1{s^2}. \end{equation}
conclusions: {\lambda^{-10}}\frac{d}{ds}\left\{\lambda^{10}\int\varphi_{10}\varepsilon^2\right\}\lesssim \mathcal N_{1,\rm loc}+\frac 1{s^2}.
nodes.statement_short: lambda^{-10} d/ds(lambda^{10} int phi_10 eps^2) <~ N_1,loc + 1/s^2.
nodes.label: lemmatail

nodes.name: Tail monotonicity
nodes.statement: {\lambda^{-10}}\frac{d}{ds}\left\{\lambda^{10}\int\varphi_{10}\varepsilon^2\right\}\lesssim \mathcal N_{1,\rm loc}+\frac 1{s^2}.
nodes.label: keyestimate

nodes.name: Monotonicity formula
nodes.statement: There exist $\mu>0$ such that the following holds for $B>100$ large enough. Let the energy--virial Lyapounov functionals for $i=1,2$, \begin{align} {\mathcal F}_{i} & = \int \Big[\varepsilon_y^2\psi_B + \varepsilon^2 \varphi_{i,B} \\ &- \frac 13 \left((\varepsilon {+} Q_b{+}pY_0{+}q)^6 - (Q_b{+}pY_0{+}q)^6 - 6 \varepsilon \left(Q_b^5{+}q^5{+}5Q^4(pY_0{+}q)\right)\right)\psi_B\Big] .\nonumber \end{align} Then the following estimates hold on $[s_0, s^*]$:\\ {\em (i) Lyapounov control}: for $i=1,2$, $j\geq 0$ \begin{equation} \frac{d}{ds}\left[ s^j {\mathcal F_{i}} \right]+ {\mu} s^j \int \left(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2\right) \varphi'_{i,B} \lesssim s^{j-4} +s^{j-9+10 \beta} . \end{equation} {\em (iii) Coercivity of $\mathcal F_{i}$ and pointwise bounds}: for $i=1,2$, $j\geq 0$, \begin{equation} -\frac 1{s^4} + \mathcal N_i \lesssim \mathcal F_{i}\lesssim \frac 1{s^4} + \mathcal N_i .\end{equation}
conclusions: \frac{d}{ds}\left[ s^j {\mathcal F_{i}} \right]+ {\mu} s^j \int \left(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2\right) \varphi'_{i,B} \lesssim s^{j-4} +s^{j-9+10 \beta} .
-\frac 1{s^4} + \mathcal N_i \lesssim \mathcal F_{i}\lesssim \frac 1{s^4} + \mathcal N_i .
nodes.statement_short: Energy-virial functionals F_i are coercive, ~N_i, and satisfy a Lyapunov inequality d/ds(s^j F_i) + mu s^j local norm <~ s^{j-4}+s^{j-9+10beta}.
nodes.label: propasymtp

nodes.name: Energy-virial functional F_i
nodes.statement: {\mathcal F}_{i} & = \int \Big[\varepsilon_y^2\psi_B + \varepsilon^2 \varphi_{i,B} \\ &- \frac 13 \left((\varepsilon {+} Q_b{+}pY_0{+}q)^6 - (Q_b{+}pY_0{+}q)^6 - 6 \varepsilon \left(Q_b^5{+}q^5{+}5Q^4(pY_0{+}q)\right)\right)\psi_B\Big] .\nonumber
nodes.label: feps

nodes.name: Lyapounov control
nodes.statement: \frac{d}{ds}\left[ s^j {\mathcal F_{i}} \right]+ {\mu} s^j \int \left(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2\right) \varphi'_{i,B} \lesssim s^{j-4} +s^{j-9+10 \beta} .
nodes.label: lyapounovconrolbis

nodes.name: Coercivity of F_i
nodes.statement: -\frac 1{s^4} + \mathcal N_i \lesssim \mathcal F_{i}\lesssim \frac 1{s^4} + \mathcal N_i .
nodes.label: lowerbound

nodes.name: Proof of (BS3')
nodes.statement: From Lemma \ref{lemmatail}, (BS2) and (BS3), $$ \frac d{ds} \left\{ \lambda^{10} \int \varphi_{10} \varepsilon^2 \right\} \lesssim \lambda^{10}\left(\mathcal N_{1,\rm loc} + s^{-2}\right) \lesssim s^{-10 \beta -2}, $$ so that by integration on $[s_0,s]$, and \eqref{A2}, $$ \lambda^{10}(s)\int \varphi_{10} \varepsilon^2(s) \leq \lambda^{10}(s_0) \int \varphi_{10} \varepsilon^2(s_0) + Cs_0^{-1-10\beta} \leq 2. $$ By the properties of $\varphi_{10}$ and \eqref{A2}, we obtain \begin{equation} \lambda^{10}(s) \int_{y>0}y^{10} \varepsilon^2(s,y) dy \leq 3. \end{equation} Now, we apply Lemma \ref{propasymtp} with $j=\frac 52 $. We find by \eqref{lyapounovconrolbis} and $\beta< \frac {11}{20}$, \begin{equation} \frac d{ds} \left[ s^{\frac 52} \mathcal F_i\right] \lesssim s^{-\frac 32} + s^{-1-10 (\frac {11}{20}-\beta)}. \end{equation} The initial smallness {\rm (\ref{A2})} ensures $$s_0^{10}|\mathcal F_i(0)|\lesssim 1$$ and thus the time integration of {\rm (\ref{neovneogbgeo})} on $[s_0,s^*]$ yields: $$ \mathcal F_i (s)\lesssim s^{- \frac 52} s_0^{-\delta} $$ for some $\delta=\delta(\beta)>0$. Using \eqref{lowerbound}, we conclude: $$ \mathcal N_i(s) \leq s^{- \frac 52} s_0^{-\delta} +s^{-4} \leq \frac 12 s^{- \frac 52} $$ for $s_0$ large enough, which together with \eqref{aa3} and the control of the full $H^1$ norm through the conservation laws {\rm (\ref{twobound})}, {\rm (\ref{energbound})} concludes the proof of (BS3').
nodes.statement_short: Integrate the tail monotonicity of Lemma 3.2 and the Lyapunov control of Lemma 3.3 with j=5/2, then use coercivity.

nodes.name: Weighted tail bound
nodes.statement: \lambda^{10}(s) \int_{y>0}y^{10} \varepsilon^2(s,y) dy \leq 3.
nodes.label: aa3

nodes.name: Integrated Lyapunov inequality
nodes.statement: \frac d{ds} \left[ s^{\frac 52} \mathcal F_i\right] \lesssim s^{-\frac 32} + s^{-1-10 (\frac {11}{20}-\beta)}.
nodes.label: neovneogbgeo

nodes.name: Improved bootstrap bound (BS2')
nodes.statement:
We claim: for all $s\in [s_0,s^*]$,$$\leqno{\rm (BS2')}\quad 
|b(s)|\leq   {5} s^{-1},
\
\frac 1{5} s^{-\beta}\leq \lambda(s) \leq 5 s^{-\beta},
\  
\frac 1{5} s^{1-\beta} \leq (1-\beta) x(s) \leq 5 s^{1-\beta}.
$$
nodes.statement_short: Improved bounds on b, lambda and x under the bootstrap.

nodes.name: Improved bound (BS2')
nodes.statement: \leqno{\rm (BS2')}\quad |b(s)|\leq {5} s^{-1}, \ \frac 1{5} s^{-\beta}\leq \lambda(s) \leq 5 s^{-\beta}, \ \frac 1{5} s^{1-\beta} \leq (1-\beta) x(s) \leq 5 s^{1-\beta}.

nodes.name: Proof of (BS2')
nodes.statement: First, note that from \eqref{fond}, \eqref{eq:2002bis}, and using (BS2)-(BS3), $\frac 13 \leq \beta\leq \frac 9{10}$, we have on $[s_0,s^*]$: \begin{equation} \left| g_s \right| \lesssim s^{-\frac 9 4 + 2 \beta }, \end{equation} \begin{equation} \left| \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} + b \right| \lesssim s^{-\frac 54}, \end{equation} \begin{equation} \left| \frac{x_s}{\lambda} -1 \right|\lesssim s^{-\frac 54}. \end{equation} By (BS1) and (BS2), we have using $(1-\beta)(\theta-1) =\frac \beta 2$ the estimate: \begin{align} & \left| \lambda (s) - \left(\frac 2 {\int Q} c_0 \frac {1}{\theta-1}\right)^2 {x^{-2 \theta+2}(s)} \right| \\ &= \left| \lambda^{\frac 12} (s) + \frac 2 {\int Q} c_0 \frac {1}{\theta-1} {x^{-\theta+1}(s)}\right| \left| \lambda^{\frac 12} (s) - \frac 2 {\int Q} c_0 \frac {1}{\theta-1} {x^{-\theta+1}(s)}\right|\nonumber \\ &\lesssim |f(s)| \left( \lambda^{\frac 12} (s)+x^{-\theta+1}(s)\right) \lesssim s^{-\frac \beta 2 - \frac 1{10} } \left( s^{-\frac \beta 2} + s^{-(1-\beta)(\theta-1)}\right) \lesssim s^{- \beta - \frac 1{10}}.\nonumber \end{align} Using \eqref{dx}, we find $$ \left| x_s (s) - \left(\frac 2 {\int Q} c_0 \frac {1}{\theta-1}\right)^2 {x^{-2 \theta+2}(s)} \right| \lesssim s^{- \beta - \frac 1{10}} + s^{-\frac 54 - \beta } \lesssim s^{- \beta - \frac 1{10}}. $$ and hence\begin{equation} \left| \left(x^{\frac 1{1-\beta}}\right)_s - (1-\beta)^{-(1-\beta)} \right| \lesssim s^{-\frac 1{10}}, \end{equation} from $2\theta-1=\frac 1{1-\beta}$ and the choice of $c_0$ in {\rm (\ref{defcobeta})} which gives: $$ (1-\beta)^{-(1-\beta)}= (2\theta-1)\left(\frac 2 {\int Q} c_0 \frac {1}{\theta-1}\right)^2. $$ Since from {\rm (\ref{initixzero})}: $$ \frac {(1-\beta) }{s_0^{1-\beta}} x (s_0)= 1,$$ the time integration of {\rm (\ref{vnkrvrnorn})} on $[s_0,s]$ yields $$ \left|x^{\frac 1{\beta-1}}(s) - (1-\beta)^{-\frac 1{\beta-1}} s \right| \lesssim s^{1-\frac 1{10}}. $$ Thus, \begin{equation} \left| \frac {(1-\beta)}{s^{1-\beta}} x (s) - 1\right| \lesssim s^{-\frac 1{10}}. \end{equation} Inserting \eqref{aa2} into \eqref{bbb2}, we find for $\lambda$, \begin{equation} \left| s^{\beta} \lambda(s) -1\right| \lesssim s^{-\frac 1{10}}. \end{equation} Finally, using $|g(s)| \leq s^{-1 + 2 \beta - \frac 1{5}}$, we find \begin{equation} \left| \frac {s}{\beta } b(s) -1\right| \lesssim s^{-\frac 1{10}}. \end{equation} From \eqref{aa2}, \eqref{aaa2} and \eqref{aaaa2}, (BS2') follows for $s_0$ large enough.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 3.1 (topological choice of lambda_0, b_0)
nodes.statement:
We now claim from a standard topological argument based on the ougoing behavior of the ODE's for $(f,g)$ that we can find $(b_0,\lambda_0)\in \mathcal D$ such that the remaining condition $(BS1)$ is closed.\\
Indeed, let $$
G(s) = g(s) s^{1-2 \beta + \frac 1{5}},\quad
F(s) = f(s) s^{\frac \beta 2+ \frac 1{10}},
$$
and
$$
H(s) = F^2(s) + G^2(s).
$$
From (BS2') and (BS3'), since $s^*=s^*(x_0,b_0)<+\infty$, it follows from a standard continuity argument that at $s=s^* \geq s_0,$
\begin{equation} H(s^*)=1.
\end{equation}
We first claim the strict outgoing behavior:
\begin{equation} H'(s^*)\geq \frac {1}{20 s^*}.
\end{equation}
\emph{Proof of \eqref{dFdG}.}
Since
$$
G'(s) = \left(1- 2 \beta +\frac 1{5}\right) g(s)s^{-2 \beta + \frac 1{5}}
+g'(s) s^{1-2 \beta + \frac 1{5}},
 $$
 we have using {\rm (\ref{dFdG})}:
 \begin{equation} G'(s^*)= \left(1- 2 \beta +\frac 1{5}\right) \frac {G(s^*)}{s^*}
 +O\left((s^*)^{-(1+\frac 1{20})}\right).
 \end{equation}
 Similarly,
 $$
 F'(s^*)= \left(\frac \beta 2+ \frac 1{10}\right) f(s^*) (s^*)^{\frac \beta 2+ \frac 1{10}-1}
 + f'(s^*) (s^*)^{\frac \beta 2+ \frac 1{10}}.
 $$
 We now estimate $f'(s)$. By direct computations and then \eqref{dl}, \eqref{dx}
 and (BS1)-(BS2), 
 \begin{align*}
 f'(s) &= \frac 12 \frac {\lambda_s}{\lambda} \lambda^{\frac 12} - \frac 2{\int Q}c_0 
   x_s x^{-\theta}  \\
 & = \frac 12 \lambda^{\frac 52} \left[
 \frac b{\lambda^2}  - \frac 4{\int Q} c_0  \lambda^{-\frac 32} x^{-\theta}\right]
+O\left(s^{-\frac 54-\frac \beta 2}\right) \\
 &= \frac 12 \lambda^{\frac 52} g(s) + O\left(s^{-\frac 54-\frac \beta 2}\right) 
 = O\left(s^{-1  -\frac \beta 2 -\frac 1{5}}\right).
 \end{align*}
 Thus, 
 \begin{equation} F'(s^*)=\left(\frac \beta 2+ \frac 1{10}\right) \frac {F(s^*)} {s^*} + O\left( (s^*)^{-1-\frac 1{10}} \right). 
 \end{equation}
 
 Therefore
 $$
 H'(s^*) = 2 F'(s^*)F(s^*) + 2 G'(s^*) G(s^*) 
 \geq \frac 1{10} \frac {H(s^*)}{s^*} + O\left((s^*)^{-1-\frac 1{20}}\right)
 \geq \frac 1{20s^*},
 $$
for $s_0$ large enough.

\medskip

By  standard arguments (see e.g. the proof of Lemma 6 in \cite{MMC}),
the strict outgoing behavior {\rm (\ref{dFdG})} ensures that the map $(\lambda_0,b_0)\in \mathcal D \to s^*(x_0,b_0)$
is continuous.
We  define the continuous maps
\begin{align*}
 \lambda_0(F_0) &= s_0^{-\beta}\left( 1 - F_0 s_0^{-\frac 1{10}} \right)^2
\\
  b_0(F_0,G_0) &= \beta s_0^{-1+\frac \beta 2} \lambda_0^{\frac 12}(F_0 ) \left( 1+ \frac 1\beta G_0 s_0^{\frac 32\beta - \frac 1{5}}  \lambda_0^{\frac 32} (F_0)
   \right)\\
  & = \beta s_0^{-1} \left| 1 - F_0 s_0^{-\frac 1{10}}\right|
  \left( 1+ \frac 1\beta G_0 s_0^{- \frac 1{5}}  \left| 1 - F_0 s_0^{-\frac 1{10}}\right|^3
   \right)
\end{align*}
so that
\begin{align*}
G_0 &= s_0^{1-2 \beta +\frac 1{5}} \left( \frac {b_0}{\lambda_0^2} 
- \frac 4{\int Q} c_0  \lambda_0^{-\frac 32} x_0^{-\theta}\right)\\
F_0 &= s_0^{\frac \beta 2 +\frac 1{10}} \left( \lambda_0^{\frac 12} 
+\frac 2{\int Q} c_0 \frac 1{\theta-1} x_0^{-\theta+1} \right).
\end{align*}

Now, consider the continous map
\begin{align*}
\mathcal M \ : \ \   \   \mathcal B_{\mathbb{R}^2}  &\to  \mathcal S_{\mathbb{R}^2} ,\\
   (F_0,G_0) &\mapsto \left(F(s^*(\lambda_0(F_0),b_0(F_0,G_0))), G(s^*(\lambda_0(F_0),b_0(F_0,G_0)))\right).
\end{align*}
where $\mathcal B_{\mathbb{R}^2}$ and $\mathcal S_{\mathbb{R}^2} $ are, respectively, the ball and  the sphere of $\mathbb{R}^2$ of radius $1$. For $(F_0,G_0)\in \mathcal S_{\mathbb{R}^2}$, we have
$\mathcal M(F_0,G_0) = (F_0,G_0)$, in other words, 
$\mathcal M$ is the identity on the sphere
$\mathcal S_{\mathbb{R}^2}$. The existence of such a continuous map 
$\mathcal M$ is  in contradiction with Brouwer's fixed point theorem. Therefore, there exists $\lambda_0$ and $b_0$ such that
\begin{equation} | \lambda_0 - s_0^{-\beta}| \leq s_0^{-\beta - \frac 1{10}},
\quad |b_0 - \beta s_0^{-1}| \leq s_0^{-1- \frac 1{10}},
\end{equation}
and $s^*(\lambda_0,b_0)=+\infty$. 
In particular (BS1)-(BS2)-(BS3) hold on $[s_0,+\infty)$.\\
Finally, \eqref{aa2}, \eqref{aaa2} and \eqref{aaaa2} imply \eqref{sharp}.\\

This concludes the proof of Proposition \ref{PR:BS} and therefore also of Theorem \ref{th:1}.
