nodes.name: Step 1: decomposition by the implicit function theorem
nodes.statement:
{\bf step 1} Proof of  (i). This is a standard modulation claim. As usual, the decomposition is first performed for a fixed time $t$.
  For $t\in [0,t_0]$ fixed, define the map
  $$
 \Theta: (\bar b,\bar \lambda,\bar x,w,z_0) \mapsto \left( \int Q\bar \varepsilon  , \int \Lambda Q \bar \varepsilon  ,\int Q' \bar \varepsilon  \right),
  $$
  where $x_0=1/z_0$,
  $$
  \bar \varepsilon(y)=\varepsilon_{(\bar b,{\bar \lambda},\bar x,w_1,z_0)}(y) =  {\bar \lambda}^{\frac 12}   w_1\left(t, {\bar \lambda} y + \bar x\right)  -  {\bar \lambda}^{\frac 12} {\lambda_1^{\frac 12}(t)} q_0\left(t,x_1(t) + \bar x\right)Y_0(y)- Q_{\bar b}(y),
  $$
  $$
  w_1(t,y)= { \lambda_1(t)}^{\frac 12}   w \left(t, {\lambda_1(t)} y + x_1(t)\right)=Q(y)+\varepsilon_1(t,y).
  $$
 We have $\bar \varepsilon|_{(0,1,0,Q,0)}=0,$ so that $\Theta(0,1,0,Q,0)=0$ and
 $$
  \quad \partial_{\bar b} \bar \varepsilon |_{(0,1,0,Q,0)}= P,
 \quad \partial_{\bar \lambda} \bar \varepsilon|_{(0,1,0,Q,0)}= \Lambda Q,
 \quad \partial_{\bar x} \bar \varepsilon|_{(0,1,0,Q,0)}= Q'.
 $$
 so that  differentiating the map $\Theta$ with respect to the variables $(\bar b,\bar \lambda,\bar x)$
 at the point $(0,1,0,Q,0)$ we find the Jacobian matrix
 $$
 \left(\begin{array}{ ccc }  (P,Q) & (P,\Lambda Q) & (P,Q') \\ (\Lambda Q,Q) & (\Lambda Q,\Lambda Q) & (\Lambda Q,Q') \\   (Q',Q) & (Q',\lambda Q)  & (Q',Q')\\  \end{array}\right)=
  \left(\begin{array}{ ccc }  (P,Q) & (P,\Lambda Q) & 0\\0 & (\Lambda Q,\Lambda Q) &0 \\ 0 & 0  & (Q',Q')\\  \end{array}\right),
 $$
 which is not degenerate since $(P,Q)>0$. It follows from these observations that we can apply the implicit function theorem to $\Theta$: for $w_1$ small and $x_0$ large, there exists
 a unique $(\bar b ,\bar \lambda , \bar x)=(\bar b ,\bar \lambda , \bar x)(w_1,x_0)$ close to $(0,1,0)$ such that $\Theta(\bar b,\bar \lambda,\bar x,w_1,\tfrac 1{x_0})=0$. Then, we  define $b(t)=\bar b(w_1(t),x_0)$, $\lambda(t)=\bar \lambda(w_1(t),x_0) \lambda_1(t)$, $x(t)=\bar x(w_1(t),x_0)+x_1(t)$
 and $\varepsilon(t)=\bar \varepsilon(t)$.
 The regularity of $(b(t),\lambda(t),x(t))$   now follow
 from standard arguments.
 It follows  that we have the following decomposition of $u(t,x)$:
\begin{align}
u(t,x) & =  \frac 1{\lambda^{\frac 12}(t)} \left( Q_{b(t)} + p(t) Y_0+ \varepsilon   \right) \left( t,\frac {x-x(t)}{\lambda(t)}\right)
+q_0(t,x) \\
& = \frac 1{\lambda^{\frac 12}(t)} \left( Q_{b(t)} + p(t) Y_0+ \varepsilon + q \right) \left(t, \frac {x-x(t)}{\lambda(t)}\right) .
\end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Construct (b,lambda,x) by the implicit function theorem.

nodes.name: Fixed-time reduction
nodes.statement: {\bf step 1} Proof of  (i). This is a standard modulation claim. As usual, the decomposition is first performed for a fixed time $t$.
nodes.statement_short: Standard modulation: first decompose at fixed time.

nodes.name: Map Theta
nodes.statement:
For $t\in [0,t_0]$ fixed, define the map
  $$
 \Theta: (\bar b,\bar \lambda,\bar x,w,z_0) \mapsto \left( \int Q\bar \varepsilon  , \int \Lambda Q \bar \varepsilon  ,\int Q' \bar \varepsilon  \right),
  $$
  where $x_0=1/z_0$,
  $$
  \bar \varepsilon(y)=\varepsilon_{(\bar b,{\bar \lambda},\bar x,w_1,z_0)}(y) =  {\bar \lambda}^{\frac 12}   w_1\left(t, {\bar \lambda} y + \bar x\right)  -  {\bar \lambda}^{\frac 12} {\lambda_1^{\frac 12}(t)} q_0\left(t,x_1(t) + \bar x\right)Y_0(y)- Q_{\bar b}(y),
  $$
  $$
  w_1(t,y)= { \lambda_1(t)}^{\frac 12}   w \left(t, {\lambda_1(t)} y + x_1(t)\right)=Q(y)+\varepsilon_1(t,y).
  $$
nodes.statement_short: Define the map Theta of the three orthogonality projections.

nodes.name: Nondegenerate Jacobian
nodes.statement:
We have $\bar \varepsilon|_{(0,1,0,Q,0)}=0,$ so that $\Theta(0,1,0,Q,0)=0$ and
 $$
  \quad \partial_{\bar b} \bar \varepsilon |_{(0,1,0,Q,0)}= P,
 \quad \partial_{\bar \lambda} \bar \varepsilon|_{(0,1,0,Q,0)}= \Lambda Q,
 \quad \partial_{\bar x} \bar \varepsilon|_{(0,1,0,Q,0)}= Q'.
 $$
 so that  differentiating the map $\Theta$ with respect to the variables $(\bar b,\bar \lambda,\bar x)$
 at the point $(0,1,0,Q,0)$ we find the Jacobian matrix
 $$
 \left(\begin{array}{ ccc }  (P,Q) & (P,\Lambda Q) & (P,Q') \\ (\Lambda Q,Q) & (\Lambda Q,\Lambda Q) & (\Lambda Q,Q') \\   (Q',Q) & (Q',\lambda Q)  & (Q',Q')\\  \end{array}\right)=
  \left(\begin{array}{ ccc }  (P,Q) & (P,\Lambda Q) & 0\\0 & (\Lambda Q,\Lambda Q) &0 \\ 0 & 0  & (Q',Q')\\  \end{array}\right),
 $$
 which is not degenerate since $(P,Q)>0$.
nodes.statement_short: Compute the Jacobian at (0,1,0,Q,0); it is nondegenerate since (P,Q)>0.

nodes.name: Implicit function theorem
nodes.statement:
It follows from these observations that we can apply the implicit function theorem to $\Theta$: for $w_1$ small and $x_0$ large, there exists
 a unique $(\bar b ,\bar \lambda , \bar x)=(\bar b ,\bar \lambda , \bar x)(w_1,x_0)$ close to $(0,1,0)$ such that $\Theta(\bar b,\bar \lambda,\bar x,w_1,\tfrac 1{x_0})=0$. Then, we  define $b(t)=\bar b(w_1(t),x_0)$, $\lambda(t)=\bar \lambda(w_1(t),x_0) \lambda_1(t)$, $x(t)=\bar x(w_1(t),x_0)+x_1(t)$
 and $\varepsilon(t)=\bar \varepsilon(t)$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the implicit function theorem to obtain the modulation parameters.

nodes.name: Resulting decomposition of u
nodes.statement:
The regularity of $(b(t),\lambda(t),x(t))$   now follow
 from standard arguments.
 It follows  that we have the following decomposition of $u(t,x)$:
\begin{align}
u(t,x) & =  \frac 1{\lambda^{\frac 12}(t)} \left( Q_{b(t)} + p(t) Y_0+ \varepsilon   \right) \left( t,\frac {x-x(t)}{\lambda(t)}\right)
+q_0(t,x) \\
& = \frac 1{\lambda^{\frac 12}(t)} \left( Q_{b(t)} + p(t) Y_0+ \varepsilon + q \right) \left(t, \frac {x-x(t)}{\lambda(t)}\right) .
\end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Regularity by standard arguments; the decomposition (dec:2)-(dec:1) follows.

nodes.name: Step 2: equation of eps and bounds on q, p, W
nodes.statement:
{\bf step 2} Equation of $\varepsilon$ and a priori bounds. To write the equation of $\varepsilon$, we first derive the equation of $w$ from the equations of $u(t)$ and $q_0(t)$:
 \begin{equation} w_t + (w_{xx} + w^5)_x = - (W_0)_x,
 \end{equation}
 where
 \begin{equation} W_0 = 5 w^4 q_0 + 10 w^3 q_0^2 + 10w^2 q_0^3 + 5w q_0^4.
  \end{equation}
  Second,   set 
  $ 
 \varepsilon_Y(s,y)= p(s) Y_0(y) +\varepsilon(s,y)$ so that
 $$
 w(s,x) = \frac{1}{\lambda^{\frac 12}(s)} \left( Q_{b(s)} +
 \varepsilon_Y \right)\left(s,\frac {x-x(s)}{\lambda(s)}\right).
  $$
By standard computations, we obtain for $\varepsilon_Y$:
  \begin{align}  \nonumber  
  \partial_s \varepsilon_Y & = (-\partial_{y}^2 \varepsilon_Y + \varepsilon_Y - (\varepsilon_Y+Q_b)^5 +Q_b^5)_y
- (5 Q^4 q)_y +\frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} \Lambda \varepsilon_Y
\\
& + \left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right) {\Lambda} Q_b 
+ \left(\frac { x_{s}}{\lambda} -1\right) (Q_b + \varepsilon_Y)_y   
+ \Phi_{b}  
 + \Psi_{{b}}   -W_y, \end{align}
where  $$
W=5(Q_b+ \varepsilon_Y)^4 q- 5 Q^4 q + 10(Q_b+\varepsilon_Y)^3 q^2 + 10(Q_b+\varepsilon_Y)^2 q^3 + 5(Q_b+\varepsilon_Y) q^4.
$$
Finally, we replace   $ 
 \varepsilon(s,y) = \varepsilon_Y(s,y)- p(s) Y_0(y) $ and use $L Y_0 = 5 Q^4  $, to obtain
   \begin{align}  \nonumber  
  \partial_s \varepsilon  &  = \left(-\partial_{y}^2 \varepsilon  + \varepsilon  - (\varepsilon +p Y_0 +Q_b)^5 +Q_b^5 + p5Q^4 Y_0\right)_y
\\ & -p_s Y_0 +(  5 Q^4 (p-q) )_y +\frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} (\Lambda \varepsilon+p\Lambda Y_0)
 + \left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right) {\Lambda} Q_b 
\nonumber \\
&+ \left(\frac { x_{s}}{\lambda} -1\right) (Q_b + \varepsilon+p  Y_0)_y   
+ \Phi_{b}  
 + \Psi_{{b}}   -W_y, \end{align}
and
\begin{align*}
W&=5(Q_b+ \varepsilon+p  Y_0)^4 q- 5 Q^4 q + 10(Q_b+\varepsilon+p  Y_0)^3 q^2 \\
&+ 10(Q_b+\varepsilon+p  Y_0)^2 q^3 + 5(Q_b+\varepsilon+p  Y_0) q^4.
\end{align*}
We now claim the following bounds which we will be used along the proof:

\begin{claim} {\rm (a) Estimates on $q(s)$.}
\begin{equation} \|q(s)\|_{L^2} \lesssim x_0^{-\theta+\frac 12}, \quad
\|q_y(s)\|_{L^2}\lesssim \lambda(s) x_0^{-\theta-\frac 12}, \quad
\|q(s)\|_{L^\infty}\lesssim \lambda^{\frac 12} (s) x_0^{-\theta}.
\end{equation}
 {\rm (b) Properties of the function $p(s)$:}
\begin{equation} \left|p(s) - c_0 \lambda^{\frac 12}(s) x^{-\theta}(s)\right| \lesssim
c_0 \lambda^{\frac 12}(s) x^{-\theta-2}(s)\lesssim  x^{-2}(s) |p(s)|,
\end{equation}
\begin{equation} e^{-\frac{3|y|}{4}} |p(s)-q(s,y)|     \lesssim \frac {\lambda(s)}{x(s)} |p(s)| e^{-\frac {|y|} 4} 
,
\end{equation}
\begin{equation} \left| \left( (5Q^4(p-q))_y ,Q\right) - c_0 \left( \int Q\right) \theta \lambda^{-\frac 32} x^{-\theta-1} \right| 
\lesssim  \frac {\lambda^2(s)}{x^2(s)} |p(s)|+\frac {\lambda(s)}{x^3(s)} |p(s)|,
\end{equation}
\begin{equation} \left| p_s - \frac 12   \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} p + \theta \frac {x_s} x p \right| \leq 
\frac {\lambda}{x^{3}}|p|   \left(\left|\frac{x_s}{\lambda} - 1\right|  + 1 \right),
\end{equation}
\begin{equation} |p_s| \lesssim  \left| \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda}\right| |p| + \frac {\lambda}{x} |p| \left(\left|\frac{x_s}{\lambda} - 1\right|  + 1 \right).
\end{equation}
{\rm (c) Estimates for the remainder term $W$:} Let 
\begin{align*}
\widetilde W&=5(Q_b+ \varepsilon+p  Y_0)^4 p- 5 Q^4 p + 10(Q_b+\varepsilon+p  Y_0)^3 p^2 \\
&+ 10(Q_b+\varepsilon+p  Y_0)^2 p^3 + 5(Q_b+\varepsilon+p  Y_0) p^4.
\end{align*}
Then,
\begin{equation} \int |W-\widetilde W| e^{-\frac 34 {|y|}}  \lesssim
\left(  |p|+|b| + \left( \int \varepsilon^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{10}} \right)^{\frac 12}\right)  \frac {\lambda}{x} |p| ,
\end{equation}
\begin{equation} |((\widetilde W)_y,\Lambda Q)|+|((\widetilde W)_y,Q)|\lesssim 
 b^2 + p^8 +|b| |p|  +|p| \left(\int \varepsilon^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{10}}\right)^{\frac 12} +\int \varepsilon^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{10}}  ,
\end{equation}
\begin{equation} |((\widetilde W)_y,y \Lambda Q)| \lesssim 
\int \varepsilon^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{10}} + b^2 + p^2.
\end{equation}
\end{claim}

\begin{proof}[Proof of Claim \ref{cl:one}]
{\it Proof of} (a). Since $q_0(t)$ is solution of \eqref{kdv}, for all $t$,
$$
\|q_0(t)\|_{L^2}= \|f_0\|_{L^2} \lesssim x_0^{-\theta+\frac 12},\quad
E(q_0(t)) = E(f_0) \lesssim x_0^{-\theta- \frac 12},
$$
and  \eqref{L2H1q} follows.\\

{\it Proof of} (b). Since $p(s) = \lambda^{\frac 12}(s) q_0(s,x(s))$, 
\eqref{cl.1bis} follows from \eqref{surX} and \eqref{leqz3}. In particular, since $c_0<0$, $p<0$.

Next, by \eqref{surX}, \eqref{leqz3} and \eqref{estfz},  splitting the two cases $\lambda |y|<\frac {x(s)}{4}$
and $\lambda |y| > \frac {x(s)}{4}$, we have
\begin{align}
&  e^{-\frac{3|y|}{4}} |p(s)-q(s,y)|  =
e^{-\frac{3|y|}{4}} \lambda^{\frac 12}(s) |q_0(s,x(s))-q_0(s,\lambda(s) y +x(s))| 
\nonumber\\
&\lesssim  |y| e^{-  \frac {|y|} 2 } \lambda^{\frac 32}(s) \left(  e^{- \frac { |y|} 4}  \|q_0'(s)\|_{L^\infty(x>\frac 34 x(s))}
+   e^{-\frac {x(s)}{16\lambda(s)}}\|q_0'(s)\|_{L^\infty} \right)\nonumber \\
&   \lesssim c_0 e^{-\frac {|y|} 4}  \lambda^{\frac 32}(s)  \left(      x^{-\theta-1}(s)
+   e^{-\frac {x(s)}{16\lambda(s)}} x_0^{-\theta-1} \right)\nonumber \\
&\lesssim c_0 e^{-\frac {|y|} 4}  \lambda^{\frac 32}(s)        x^{-\theta-1}(s)  
 \lesssim \frac {\lambda}{x} |p| e^{-\frac {|y|} 4}. \end{align}
Next, by \eqref{surX} and \eqref{leqz3},
\begin{align*}
&\left( (5Q^4(p-q))_y ,Q\right) = -5 \int Q^4 Q_y  (p-q)= -\int Q^5 q_y 
\\
&= -\lambda^{\frac 32}(s) \int Q^5(y) \partial_x q_0(s,\lambda(s) y +x(s)) dy\\
&= - \lambda^{\frac 32}  f_0'( x(s)) \int Q^5  - \lambda^{\frac 32} \int Q^5 \left(f_0'(\lambda y + x(s)) -f_0'(x(s))\right)dy  \\ & -\lambda^{\frac 32}(s) \int Q^5(y) \left( \partial_x q_0(s,\lambda(s) y +x(s) )-f_0'(\lambda y+x(s))\right) dy\\
&
 =c_0 \left( \int Q\right) \theta   \lambda^{\frac 32}(s)  x^{-\theta -1}(s) 
 + O\left( \lambda^{\frac 32}e^{-\frac 54   x(s) } \right) + O\left( \lambda^{\frac 52} x^{-\theta-2}\right) 
+O\left( \lambda^{\frac 32} x^{-\theta-3}(s)\right)\\
&
 =c_0 \left( \int Q\right) \theta   \lambda^{\frac 32}(s)  x^{-\theta -1}(s) 
 + O\left(\frac {\lambda^2}{x^2} |p|  \right)
 + O\left(\frac {\lambda}{x^3} |p|  \right),
 \end{align*}
where we have split the integrals above  into $|y| >\frac 14 x(s)$ and $|y|<\frac 14 x(s)$ and using the fact that for $|y|<\frac 14 x(s)$, $\lambda y + x(s) >x(s)-|y|> \frac 34 x(s)   > \frac 12 t + \frac 12 x_0$, so that
 \eqref{leqz3} holds for $x= \lambda y + x(s)$, and {\rm (\ref{cl.4bis})} is proved.\\
Now, we prove \eqref{cl.2bis}. By
explicit differentiation and Lemma \ref{le:qz},
\begin{align*}
p_s - \frac 12 \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} p & = 
\lambda^{\frac 12}(q_0)_s(s,x(s)) + \lambda^{\frac 12} x_s \partial_x q_0(s,x(s))\\
& = \lambda^{\frac 72} (q_0)_t(s,x(s)) + \lambda^{\frac 12} x_s f_0'(x(s))   
+ O\left(  \frac {\lambda}{x^{3}} |p| \left(\left|\frac{x_s}{\lambda} - 1\right|  + 1 \right) \right)\\
& = -\theta \frac {x_s} x |p| + O\left(  \frac {\lambda}{x^{3}} |p| \left(\left|\frac{x_s}{\lambda} - 1\right|  + 1 \right) \right).
\end{align*} 
Since $|x_s| \leq \lambda (|\frac{x_s}{\lambda} -1| + 1)$, \eqref{cl.2tri} follows.\\


{\it Proof of} (c). For \eqref{cl.3}, we first note
\begin{align*}
\widetilde W - W &=5\left[(Q_b+ \varepsilon+p  Y_0)^4 -   Q^4\right]  (p-q) + 10(Q_b+\varepsilon+p  Y_0)^3 (p^2-q^2) \\
&+ 10(Q_b+\varepsilon+p  Y_0)^2 (p^3-q^3) + 5(Q_b+\varepsilon+p  Y_0) (p^4-q^4).
\end{align*}

Thus, 
 \begin{align*}
&  \int e^{-\frac 34 {|y|}} |W-\widetilde W|  \\ &\lesssim
\left(  |p|+|b| \right) \int   e^{- \frac 34 {|y|}}  |p-q|
+   \left( \int \varepsilon^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{10}} \right)^{\frac 12}\left( \int   e^{-(\frac 32-\frac 1{10}) {|y|}}  |p-q|^2\right)^{\frac 12}  \\ & + \int   e^{-\frac 34 {|y|}} |p^2-q^2|   \lesssim
\left(  |p|+|b| + \left( \int \varepsilon^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{10}} \right)^{\frac 12}\right)  \frac {\lambda}{x}|p|,
\end{align*}
 using \eqref{cl.2}, and the following similar estimate
$$
e^{-\frac 34 {|y|}} |p^2-q^2| \lesssim \frac {\lambda}{x} p^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{4}}.
$$
Next, \eqref{cl.4} follows from the parity properties and then direct estimates. \eqref{cl.5} follows from direct estimates. Note that   $p^2$   appears in \eqref{cl.5} because there is no cancellation due to parity for this term. This concludes the proof of Claim \ref{cl:one}.
\end{proof}
nodes.statement_short: Derive the equation of eps and state Claim 1.

nodes.name: Equation of w
nodes.statement_short: Equation of w = u - q_0 with forcing W_0.

nodes.name: eps_Y
nodes.statement:
Second,   set 
  $ 
 \varepsilon_Y(s,y)= p(s) Y_0(y) +\varepsilon(s,y)$ so that
 $$
 w(s,x) = \frac{1}{\lambda^{\frac 12}(s)} \left( Q_{b(s)} +
 \varepsilon_Y \right)\left(s,\frac {x-x(s)}{\lambda(s)}\right).
  $$
nodes.statement_short: Introduce eps_Y = p Y_0 + eps.

nodes.name: Equation of eps_Y
nodes.statement:
By standard computations, we obtain for $\varepsilon_Y$:
  \begin{align}  \nonumber  
  \partial_s \varepsilon_Y & = (-\partial_{y}^2 \varepsilon_Y + \varepsilon_Y - (\varepsilon_Y+Q_b)^5 +Q_b^5)_y
- (5 Q^4 q)_y +\frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} \Lambda \varepsilon_Y
\\
& + \left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right) {\Lambda} Q_b 
+ \left(\frac { x_{s}}{\lambda} -1\right) (Q_b + \varepsilon_Y)_y   
+ \Phi_{b}  
 + \Psi_{{b}}   -W_y, \end{align}
where  $$
W=5(Q_b+ \varepsilon_Y)^4 q- 5 Q^4 q + 10(Q_b+\varepsilon_Y)^3 q^2 + 10(Q_b+\varepsilon_Y)^2 q^3 + 5(Q_b+\varepsilon_Y) q^4.
$$
nodes.statement_short: Equation of eps_Y by standard computations.

nodes.name: Equation of eps
nodes.statement:
Finally, we replace   $ 
 \varepsilon(s,y) = \varepsilon_Y(s,y)- p(s) Y_0(y) $ and use $L Y_0 = 5 Q^4  $, to obtain
   \begin{align}  \nonumber  
  \partial_s \varepsilon  &  = \left(-\partial_{y}^2 \varepsilon  + \varepsilon  - (\varepsilon +p Y_0 +Q_b)^5 +Q_b^5 + p5Q^4 Y_0\right)_y
\\ & -p_s Y_0 +(  5 Q^4 (p-q) )_y +\frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} (\Lambda \varepsilon+p\Lambda Y_0)
 + \left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right) {\Lambda} Q_b 
\nonumber \\
&+ \left(\frac { x_{s}}{\lambda} -1\right) (Q_b + \varepsilon+p  Y_0)_y   
+ \Phi_{b}  
 + \Psi_{{b}}   -W_y, \end{align}
and
\begin{align*}
W&=5(Q_b+ \varepsilon+p  Y_0)^4 q- 5 Q^4 q + 10(Q_b+\varepsilon+p  Y_0)^3 q^2 \\
&+ 10(Q_b+\varepsilon+p  Y_0)^2 q^3 + 5(Q_b+\varepsilon+p  Y_0) q^4.
\end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Substitute eps = eps_Y - pY_0 and use LY_0=5Q^4.

nodes.name: Claim 1 and its proof
nodes.statement:
We now claim the following bounds which we will be used along the proof:

\begin{claim} {\rm (a) Estimates on $q(s)$.}
\begin{equation} \|q(s)\|_{L^2} \lesssim x_0^{-\theta+\frac 12}, \quad
\|q_y(s)\|_{L^2}\lesssim \lambda(s) x_0^{-\theta-\frac 12}, \quad
\|q(s)\|_{L^\infty}\lesssim \lambda^{\frac 12} (s) x_0^{-\theta}.
\end{equation}
 {\rm (b) Properties of the function $p(s)$:}
\begin{equation} \left|p(s) - c_0 \lambda^{\frac 12}(s) x^{-\theta}(s)\right| \lesssim
c_0 \lambda^{\frac 12}(s) x^{-\theta-2}(s)\lesssim  x^{-2}(s) |p(s)|,
\end{equation}
\begin{equation} e^{-\frac{3|y|}{4}} |p(s)-q(s,y)|     \lesssim \frac {\lambda(s)}{x(s)} |p(s)| e^{-\frac {|y|} 4} 
,
\end{equation}
\begin{equation} \left| \left( (5Q^4(p-q))_y ,Q\right) - c_0 \left( \int Q\right) \theta \lambda^{-\frac 32} x^{-\theta-1} \right| 
\lesssim  \frac {\lambda^2(s)}{x^2(s)} |p(s)|+\frac {\lambda(s)}{x^3(s)} |p(s)|,
\end{equation}
\begin{equation} \left| p_s - \frac 12   \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} p + \theta \frac {x_s} x p \right| \leq 
\frac {\lambda}{x^{3}}|p|   \left(\left|\frac{x_s}{\lambda} - 1\right|  + 1 \right),
\end{equation}
\begin{equation} |p_s| \lesssim  \left| \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda}\right| |p| + \frac {\lambda}{x} |p| \left(\left|\frac{x_s}{\lambda} - 1\right|  + 1 \right).
\end{equation}
{\rm (c) Estimates for the remainder term $W$:} Let 
\begin{align*}
\widetilde W&=5(Q_b+ \varepsilon+p  Y_0)^4 p- 5 Q^4 p + 10(Q_b+\varepsilon+p  Y_0)^3 p^2 \\
&+ 10(Q_b+\varepsilon+p  Y_0)^2 p^3 + 5(Q_b+\varepsilon+p  Y_0) p^4.
\end{align*}
Then,
\begin{equation} \int |W-\widetilde W| e^{-\frac 34 {|y|}}  \lesssim
\left(  |p|+|b| + \left( \int \varepsilon^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{10}} \right)^{\frac 12}\right)  \frac {\lambda}{x} |p| ,
\end{equation}
\begin{equation} |((\widetilde W)_y,\Lambda Q)|+|((\widetilde W)_y,Q)|\lesssim 
 b^2 + p^8 +|b| |p|  +|p| \left(\int \varepsilon^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{10}}\right)^{\frac 12} +\int \varepsilon^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{10}}  ,
\end{equation}
\begin{equation} |((\widetilde W)_y,y \Lambda Q)| \lesssim 
\int \varepsilon^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{10}} + b^2 + p^2.
\end{equation}
\end{claim}

\begin{proof}[Proof of Claim \ref{cl:one}]
{\it Proof of} (a). Since $q_0(t)$ is solution of \eqref{kdv}, for all $t$,
$$
\|q_0(t)\|_{L^2}= \|f_0\|_{L^2} \lesssim x_0^{-\theta+\frac 12},\quad
E(q_0(t)) = E(f_0) \lesssim x_0^{-\theta- \frac 12},
$$
and  \eqref{L2H1q} follows.\\

{\it Proof of} (b). Since $p(s) = \lambda^{\frac 12}(s) q_0(s,x(s))$, 
\eqref{cl.1bis} follows from \eqref{surX} and \eqref{leqz3}. In particular, since $c_0<0$, $p<0$.

Next, by \eqref{surX}, \eqref{leqz3} and \eqref{estfz},  splitting the two cases $\lambda |y|<\frac {x(s)}{4}$
and $\lambda |y| > \frac {x(s)}{4}$, we have
\begin{align}
&  e^{-\frac{3|y|}{4}} |p(s)-q(s,y)|  =
e^{-\frac{3|y|}{4}} \lambda^{\frac 12}(s) |q_0(s,x(s))-q_0(s,\lambda(s) y +x(s))| 
\nonumber\\
&\lesssim  |y| e^{-  \frac {|y|} 2 } \lambda^{\frac 32}(s) \left(  e^{- \frac { |y|} 4}  \|q_0'(s)\|_{L^\infty(x>\frac 34 x(s))}
+   e^{-\frac {x(s)}{16\lambda(s)}}\|q_0'(s)\|_{L^\infty} \right)\nonumber \\
&   \lesssim c_0 e^{-\frac {|y|} 4}  \lambda^{\frac 32}(s)  \left(      x^{-\theta-1}(s)
+   e^{-\frac {x(s)}{16\lambda(s)}} x_0^{-\theta-1} \right)\nonumber \\
&\lesssim c_0 e^{-\frac {|y|} 4}  \lambda^{\frac 32}(s)        x^{-\theta-1}(s)  
 \lesssim \frac {\lambda}{x} |p| e^{-\frac {|y|} 4}. \end{align}
Next, by \eqref{surX} and \eqref{leqz3},
\begin{align*}
&\left( (5Q^4(p-q))_y ,Q\right) = -5 \int Q^4 Q_y  (p-q)= -\int Q^5 q_y 
\\
&= -\lambda^{\frac 32}(s) \int Q^5(y) \partial_x q_0(s,\lambda(s) y +x(s)) dy\\
&= - \lambda^{\frac 32}  f_0'( x(s)) \int Q^5  - \lambda^{\frac 32} \int Q^5 \left(f_0'(\lambda y + x(s)) -f_0'(x(s))\right)dy  \\ & -\lambda^{\frac 32}(s) \int Q^5(y) \left( \partial_x q_0(s,\lambda(s) y +x(s) )-f_0'(\lambda y+x(s))\right) dy\\
&
 =c_0 \left( \int Q\right) \theta   \lambda^{\frac 32}(s)  x^{-\theta -1}(s) 
 + O\left( \lambda^{\frac 32}e^{-\frac 54   x(s) } \right) + O\left( \lambda^{\frac 52} x^{-\theta-2}\right) 
+O\left( \lambda^{\frac 32} x^{-\theta-3}(s)\right)\\
&
 =c_0 \left( \int Q\right) \theta   \lambda^{\frac 32}(s)  x^{-\theta -1}(s) 
 + O\left(\frac {\lambda^2}{x^2} |p|  \right)
 + O\left(\frac {\lambda}{x^3} |p|  \right),
 \end{align*}
where we have split the integrals above  into $|y| >\frac 14 x(s)$ and $|y|<\frac 14 x(s)$ and using the fact that for $|y|<\frac 14 x(s)$, $\lambda y + x(s) >x(s)-|y|> \frac 34 x(s)   > \frac 12 t + \frac 12 x_0$, so that
 \eqref{leqz3} holds for $x= \lambda y + x(s)$, and {\rm (\ref{cl.4bis})} is proved.\\
Now, we prove \eqref{cl.2bis}. By
explicit differentiation and Lemma \ref{le:qz},
\begin{align*}
p_s - \frac 12 \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} p & = 
\lambda^{\frac 12}(q_0)_s(s,x(s)) + \lambda^{\frac 12} x_s \partial_x q_0(s,x(s))\\
& = \lambda^{\frac 72} (q_0)_t(s,x(s)) + \lambda^{\frac 12} x_s f_0'(x(s))   
+ O\left(  \frac {\lambda}{x^{3}} |p| \left(\left|\frac{x_s}{\lambda} - 1\right|  + 1 \right) \right)\\
& = -\theta \frac {x_s} x |p| + O\left(  \frac {\lambda}{x^{3}} |p| \left(\left|\frac{x_s}{\lambda} - 1\right|  + 1 \right) \right).
\end{align*} 
Since $|x_s| \leq \lambda (|\frac{x_s}{\lambda} -1| + 1)$, \eqref{cl.2tri} follows.\\


{\it Proof of} (c). For \eqref{cl.3}, we first note
\begin{align*}
\widetilde W - W &=5\left[(Q_b+ \varepsilon+p  Y_0)^4 -   Q^4\right]  (p-q) + 10(Q_b+\varepsilon+p  Y_0)^3 (p^2-q^2) \\
&+ 10(Q_b+\varepsilon+p  Y_0)^2 (p^3-q^3) + 5(Q_b+\varepsilon+p  Y_0) (p^4-q^4).
\end{align*}

Thus, 
 \begin{align*}
&  \int e^{-\frac 34 {|y|}} |W-\widetilde W|  \\ &\lesssim
\left(  |p|+|b| \right) \int   e^{- \frac 34 {|y|}}  |p-q|
+   \left( \int \varepsilon^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{10}} \right)^{\frac 12}\left( \int   e^{-(\frac 32-\frac 1{10}) {|y|}}  |p-q|^2\right)^{\frac 12}  \\ & + \int   e^{-\frac 34 {|y|}} |p^2-q^2|   \lesssim
\left(  |p|+|b| + \left( \int \varepsilon^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{10}} \right)^{\frac 12}\right)  \frac {\lambda}{x}|p|,
\end{align*}
 using \eqref{cl.2}, and the following similar estimate
$$
e^{-\frac 34 {|y|}} |p^2-q^2| \lesssim \frac {\lambda}{x} p^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{4}}.
$$
Next, \eqref{cl.4} follows from the parity properties and then direct estimates. \eqref{cl.5} follows from direct estimates. Note that   $p^2$   appears in \eqref{cl.5} because there is no cancellation due to parity for this term. This concludes the proof of Claim \ref{cl:one}.
\end{proof}
nodes.statement_short: Inner Claim 1 with its proof.

nodes.name: Step 3: conservation law estimates
nodes.statement:
{\bf step 3}  Estimates induced by the conservation laws.
By $L^2$ norm conservation,
\begin{align*}
& \int u^2(0) - \int Q^2  = \int Q_b^2 - \int Q^2 + \int (\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^2 + 2 \int (\varepsilon+pY_0 +q) Q_b\\
&= 2 b(P,Q) + O(|b|^{2-\gamma}) +\|\varepsilon\|_{L^2}^2 + O(|b|^{1-\frac \gamma 2}\|\varepsilon\|_{L^2}) +O(|p|+   \|q\|_{L^2}).
\end{align*}
Estimate \eqref{twobound} follows. By energy conservation, $Q''+Q^5= Q$  and $\int \varepsilon Q=0$,
\begin{align*} & 2 \lambda^2 E(u_0)   = 2 E(Q_b + \varepsilon + pY_0 +q) \\& = 2 E(Q_b) - 2 \int (\varepsilon+pY_0 + q) \left( (Q_b-Q)_{yy}+ (Q_b^5 - Q^5) \right)
- 2 \int (pY_0 + q) Q \\ &+ \int (\varepsilon+pY_0 + q)_y^2 - \frac 13 \int \left( (Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0 + q)^6 - Q_b^6 - 6 Q_b^5(\varepsilon+pY+q)\right)\\
& = - 2 b (P,Q) + O(b^2) 
+ O\left( |b|^{1+\frac 32 \gamma} \left( \|\varepsilon\|_{L^2} + |p| + \|q\|_{L^2}\right)\right) - 2 p \left( \int Y_0 Q + \int Q\right)
\\ &+ 2 \int (p-q) Q + \|\varepsilon_y\|_{L^2}^2  + O(p^2) + O\left(\|\varepsilon_y\|_{L^2}(|p|+ \|q_y\|_{L^2})\right) + 2\lambda^2 E(q_0)
\\ &- \frac 13 \int \left( (Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^6 - Q_b^6 - 6Q_b^5 (\varepsilon+pY_0+q) -q^6\right)
\end{align*}
By \eqref{YQ}, we have $\int Y_0 Q + \int Q = \frac 14 \int Q$. Using in addition \eqref{PQ}, \eqref{cl.2}, \eqref{cl.1bis}, we obtain
\begin{align*}
\frac 1{\lambda^2}\|\varepsilon_y\|_{L^2}^2 & \lesssim |E(u_0)| + \left| \frac 14 \frac b{\lambda^2} \int Q + \frac p{\lambda^2}\right| 
+ \frac {b^2}{\lambda^2}+  \frac {|b|^{1+\frac 32 \gamma}}{\lambda^2} \left( \|\varepsilon\|_{L^2} + |p| + \|q\|_{L^2}\right) \\
 & + \frac { |p| }{\lambda x}  + \frac {p^2}{\lambda^2}  +  x_0^{-\theta-\frac 12}\\
 & \lesssim |E(u_0)| + \left| \frac 14 \frac b{\lambda^2} \int Q + c_0 \lambda^{-\frac 32} x^{-\theta} \right|  
+ \frac {b^2}{\lambda^2}+  
 \frac { |p| }{x^2} + \frac { |p| }{\lambda x}  + \frac {p^2}{\lambda^2}  +  x_0^{-\theta-\frac 12} 
  .
\end{align*}

\medskip
nodes.statement_short: Mass and energy conservation give (twobound) and (energbound).

nodes.name: Mass conservation
nodes.statement:
{\bf step 3}  Estimates induced by the conservation laws.
By $L^2$ norm conservation,
\begin{align*}
& \int u^2(0) - \int Q^2  = \int Q_b^2 - \int Q^2 + \int (\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^2 + 2 \int (\varepsilon+pY_0 +q) Q_b\\
&= 2 b(P,Q) + O(|b|^{2-\gamma}) +\|\varepsilon\|_{L^2}^2 + O(|b|^{1-\frac \gamma 2}\|\varepsilon\|_{L^2}) +O(|p|+   \|q\|_{L^2}).
\end{align*}
Estimate \eqref{twobound} follows.
nodes.statement_short: L^2 conservation gives (twobound).

nodes.name: Energy expansion
nodes.statement:
By energy conservation, $Q''+Q^5= Q$  and $\int \varepsilon Q=0$,
\begin{align*} & 2 \lambda^2 E(u_0)   = 2 E(Q_b + \varepsilon + pY_0 +q) \\& = 2 E(Q_b) - 2 \int (\varepsilon+pY_0 + q) \left( (Q_b-Q)_{yy}+ (Q_b^5 - Q^5) \right)
- 2 \int (pY_0 + q) Q \\ &+ \int (\varepsilon+pY_0 + q)_y^2 - \frac 13 \int \left( (Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0 + q)^6 - Q_b^6 - 6 Q_b^5(\varepsilon+pY+q)\right)\\
& = - 2 b (P,Q) + O(b^2) 
+ O\left( |b|^{1+\frac 32 \gamma} \left( \|\varepsilon\|_{L^2} + |p| + \|q\|_{L^2}\right)\right) - 2 p \left( \int Y_0 Q + \int Q\right)
\\ &+ 2 \int (p-q) Q + \|\varepsilon_y\|_{L^2}^2  + O(p^2) + O\left(\|\varepsilon_y\|_{L^2}(|p|+ \|q_y\|_{L^2})\right) + 2\lambda^2 E(q_0)
\\ &- \frac 13 \int \left( (Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^6 - Q_b^6 - 6Q_b^5 (\varepsilon+pY_0+q) -q^6\right)
\end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Expand the energy around Q_b.

nodes.name: Energy bound
nodes.statement:
By \eqref{YQ}, we have $\int Y_0 Q + \int Q = \frac 14 \int Q$. Using in addition \eqref{PQ}, \eqref{cl.2}, \eqref{cl.1bis}, we obtain
\begin{align*}
\frac 1{\lambda^2}\|\varepsilon_y\|_{L^2}^2 & \lesssim |E(u_0)| + \left| \frac 14 \frac b{\lambda^2} \int Q + \frac p{\lambda^2}\right| 
+ \frac {b^2}{\lambda^2}+  \frac {|b|^{1+\frac 32 \gamma}}{\lambda^2} \left( \|\varepsilon\|_{L^2} + |p| + \|q\|_{L^2}\right) \\
 & + \frac { |p| }{\lambda x}  + \frac {p^2}{\lambda^2}  +  x_0^{-\theta-\frac 12}\\
 & \lesssim |E(u_0)| + \left| \frac 14 \frac b{\lambda^2} \int Q + c_0 \lambda^{-\frac 32} x^{-\theta} \right|  
+ \frac {b^2}{\lambda^2}+  
 \frac { |p| }{x^2} + \frac { |p| }{\lambda x}  + \frac {p^2}{\lambda^2}  +  x_0^{-\theta-\frac 12} 
  .
\end{align*}

\medskip
nodes.statement_short: Use (YQ), (PQ) and Claim 1 to get (energbound).

nodes.name: Step 4: modulation equations
nodes.statement_short: Differentiate the orthogonality conditions to obtain (iii).

nodes.name: Method as in MMR1
nodes.statement:
{\bf step 4} Modulation equations. We argue as in \cite{MMR1}, proof of Lemma 2.7, differentiating with respect to $s$ the orthogonality conditions $\int \varepsilon \Lambda Q=0$, $\int \varepsilon Q'=0$ and 
$\int \varepsilon Q=0$ and using \eqref{eqofeps} to obtain   \eqref{eq:2002bis}
and \eqref{eq:2003}.
Here, we  will  treat only  the   terms  coming from $q$ and $pY_0$ in \eqref{eqofeps} and we refer the reader to \cite{MMR1} for more details on the other terms.
\medskip
nodes.statement_short: Argue as in MMR1, treating only the new q and pY_0 terms.

nodes.name: Proof of (eq:2002bis), (eq:2003)
nodes.statement_short: Estimates for lambda_s/lambda+b, x_s/lambda-1 and b_s.

nodes.name: lambda_s/lambda + b
nodes.statement_short: Estimate lambda_s/lambda+b from MMR1 computations and Claim 1.

nodes.name: x_s/lambda - 1
nodes.statement_short: Same for x_s/lambda-1 using parity.

nodes.name: Rough b_s bound
nodes.statement_short: Rough bound on b_s from projection on Q.

nodes.name: Combine with p_s bound
nodes.statement:
Combining these estimates with (from \eqref{cl.2bis})
$$
|p_s| \leq \left|   \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} \right| |p| + \frac {\lambda}{x}  |p|\left( \left|\frac{x_s}{\lambda} - 1\right| + 1 \right)
\leq |b| |p| +\left| \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda}+b\right| |p| +  \frac \lambda x |p|\left( \left|\frac{x_s}{\lambda} - 1\right| + 1 \right),
$$
from \eqref{cl.2tri},
we obtain  \eqref{eq:2002bis} and \eqref{eq:2003}. 









\medskip
nodes.statement_short: Combine with (cl.2tri) to get (eq:2002bis), (eq:2003).

nodes.name: Proof of (fond)
nodes.statement_short: Refined b_s equation, cancellation, and the derivative of b/lambda^2.

nodes.name: Refined b_s equation
nodes.statement:
\emph{Proof of \eqref{fond}.}
First, we derive a refined equation for $b_s$, taking the scalar product of equation \eqref{eqofeps} by $Q$ and proceeding as   in \cite{MMR1},  proof of Lemma 2.7.
nodes.statement_short: Project the eps equation on Q as in MMR1.

nodes.name: Recall projections of Psi_b, Phi_b
nodes.statement_short: Recall (Psi_b,Q), (Phi_b,Q) from MMR1.

nodes.name: Nonlinear terms
nodes.statement_short: Nonlinear terms by parity and direct estimates.

nodes.name: Equation (eq:bautre)
nodes.statement_short: Obtain the b_s equation (eq:bautre).

nodes.name: Cancellation (cancel)
nodes.statement:
We claim  the following cancellation
\begin{equation} - (Y_0,\Lambda Q) + 20 ((Q^3Y_0 P)_y,Q) + 20 ((PQ^3)_y,Q) =0.
\end{equation}
Indeed, 
$L(P')= (LP)' + 20 Q^3 Q' P = \Lambda Q + 20 Q^3 Q' P,$
and so from \eqref{eq:23},
\begin{align*}
& - (Y_0,\Lambda Q) + 20 ((Q^3Y_0 P)_y,Q) + 20 ((PQ^3)_y,Q) 
\\ &= - (Y_0,\Lambda Q)-  20 (Y_0+1,PQ^3 Q')\\
& = - (Y_0+1 , L(P')) + \int \Lambda Q = - (L(Y_0+1),P') - \frac 12 \int Q
\\ & = - \int P' -  \frac 12 \int Q  =  P(-\infty) - \frac 12 \int Q =0.
\end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Prove the cancellation identity using L(P') and P(-infty).

nodes.name: Use of cancellation
nodes.statement:
Thus,
\begin{align*}
& \left| 
 - \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} p 
 (Y_0,\Lambda Q) +  bp \left[ 20 ((Q^3Y_0 P)_y,Q) + 20 ((PQ^3)_y,Q) \right]
\right|  = 
|p| \left| \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda}+b \right|  |(Y_0,\Lambda Q)|.
\end{align*}

\medskip
nodes.statement_short: The p-terms reduce to |p||lambda_s/lambda+b|.

nodes.name: Equation (eq:b)
nodes.statement_short: Compute the remaining p_s term and obtain (eq:b).

nodes.name: Derivative of b/lambda^2
nodes.statement:
Now, we prove \eqref{fond}. By direct computation,
$$
\frac d{ds}\left( \frac 4{\left(\int Q\right)}c_0 \theta   \lambda^{-\frac 32}(s) x^{-\theta}\right) = - \frac {4}{(\int Q)} c_0 \lambda^{-\frac 32} x^{-\theta}  \left(  \frac 32 \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} 
 +  \theta     \frac {x_s}{x}    \right)  
$$
$$
\frac d{ds}\left( \frac b{\lambda^2}\right)
 =   \frac {b_s}{\lambda^2} - 2 \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} \frac b{\lambda^2}
 =   \frac {b_s}{\lambda^2}  + 2 \frac {b^2}{\lambda^2} - 2 \left( \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} +b\right) \frac b{\lambda^2}.$$
 and \eqref{fond} follows from \eqref{eq:b} and \eqref{eq:2002bis}.
nodes.statement_short: Differentiate b/lambda^2 and the tail term; conclude (fond).

nodes.name: Proof of (a)
nodes.statement:
{\it Proof of} (a). Since $q_0(t)$ is solution of \eqref{kdv}, for all $t$,
$$
\|q_0(t)\|_{L^2}= \|f_0\|_{L^2} \lesssim x_0^{-\theta+\frac 12},\quad
E(q_0(t)) = E(f_0) \lesssim x_0^{-\theta- \frac 12},
$$
and  \eqref{L2H1q} follows.\\
nodes.statement_short: Mass and energy conservation for q_0 give (L2H1q).

nodes.name: Asymptotics of p
nodes.statement:
{\it Proof of} (b). Since $p(s) = \lambda^{\frac 12}(s) q_0(s,x(s))$, 
\eqref{cl.1bis} follows from \eqref{surX} and \eqref{leqz3}. In particular, since $c_0<0$, $p<0$.
nodes.statement_short: (cl.1bis) from (surX) and Lemma 2.3; p<0.

nodes.name: Estimate of p-q
nodes.statement:
Next, by \eqref{surX}, \eqref{leqz3} and \eqref{estfz},  splitting the two cases $\lambda |y|<\frac {x(s)}{4}$
and $\lambda |y| > \frac {x(s)}{4}$, we have
\begin{align}
&  e^{-\frac{3|y|}{4}} |p(s)-q(s,y)|  =
e^{-\frac{3|y|}{4}} \lambda^{\frac 12}(s) |q_0(s,x(s))-q_0(s,\lambda(s) y +x(s))| 
\nonumber\\
&\lesssim  |y| e^{-  \frac {|y|} 2 } \lambda^{\frac 32}(s) \left(  e^{- \frac { |y|} 4}  \|q_0'(s)\|_{L^\infty(x>\frac 34 x(s))}
+   e^{-\frac {x(s)}{16\lambda(s)}}\|q_0'(s)\|_{L^\infty} \right)\nonumber \\
&   \lesssim c_0 e^{-\frac {|y|} 4}  \lambda^{\frac 32}(s)  \left(      x^{-\theta-1}(s)
+   e^{-\frac {x(s)}{16\lambda(s)}} x_0^{-\theta-1} \right)\nonumber \\
&\lesssim c_0 e^{-\frac {|y|} 4}  \lambda^{\frac 32}(s)        x^{-\theta-1}(s)  
 \lesssim \frac {\lambda}{x} |p| e^{-\frac {|y|} 4}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Split |y| small/large to get (cl.2).

nodes.name: Projection on Q
nodes.statement:
Next, by \eqref{surX} and \eqref{leqz3},
\begin{align*}
&\left( (5Q^4(p-q))_y ,Q\right) = -5 \int Q^4 Q_y  (p-q)= -\int Q^5 q_y 
\\
&= -\lambda^{\frac 32}(s) \int Q^5(y) \partial_x q_0(s,\lambda(s) y +x(s)) dy\\
&= - \lambda^{\frac 32}  f_0'( x(s)) \int Q^5  - \lambda^{\frac 32} \int Q^5 \left(f_0'(\lambda y + x(s)) -f_0'(x(s))\right)dy  \\ & -\lambda^{\frac 32}(s) \int Q^5(y) \left( \partial_x q_0(s,\lambda(s) y +x(s) )-f_0'(\lambda y+x(s))\right) dy\\
&
 =c_0 \left( \int Q\right) \theta   \lambda^{\frac 32}(s)  x^{-\theta -1}(s) 
 + O\left( \lambda^{\frac 32}e^{-\frac 54   x(s) } \right) + O\left( \lambda^{\frac 52} x^{-\theta-2}\right) 
+O\left( \lambda^{\frac 32} x^{-\theta-3}(s)\right)\\
&
 =c_0 \left( \int Q\right) \theta   \lambda^{\frac 32}(s)  x^{-\theta -1}(s) 
 + O\left(\frac {\lambda^2}{x^2} |p|  \right)
 + O\left(\frac {\lambda}{x^3} |p|  \right),
 \end{align*}
where we have split the integrals above  into $|y| >\frac 14 x(s)$ and $|y|<\frac 14 x(s)$ and using the fact that for $|y|<\frac 14 x(s)$, $\lambda y + x(s) >x(s)-|y|> \frac 34 x(s)   > \frac 12 t + \frac 12 x_0$, so that
 \eqref{leqz3} holds for $x= \lambda y + x(s)$, and {\rm (\ref{cl.4bis})} is proved.\\
nodes.statement_short: Expand the projection to obtain (cl.4bis).

nodes.name: Equation for p_s
nodes.statement:
Now, we prove \eqref{cl.2bis}. By
explicit differentiation and Lemma \ref{le:qz},
\begin{align*}
p_s - \frac 12 \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} p & = 
\lambda^{\frac 12}(q_0)_s(s,x(s)) + \lambda^{\frac 12} x_s \partial_x q_0(s,x(s))\\
& = \lambda^{\frac 72} (q_0)_t(s,x(s)) + \lambda^{\frac 12} x_s f_0'(x(s))   
+ O\left(  \frac {\lambda}{x^{3}} |p| \left(\left|\frac{x_s}{\lambda} - 1\right|  + 1 \right) \right)\\
& = -\theta \frac {x_s} x |p| + O\left(  \frac {\lambda}{x^{3}} |p| \left(\left|\frac{x_s}{\lambda} - 1\right|  + 1 \right) \right).
\end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Differentiate p and use Lemma 2.3 to get (cl.2bis).

nodes.name: Bound on p_s
nodes.statement: Since $|x_s| \leq \lambda (|\frac{x_s}{\lambda} -1| + 1)$, \eqref{cl.2tri} follows.\\
nodes.statement_short: (cl.2tri) follows.

nodes.name: Estimate of W - tilde W
nodes.statement:
{\it Proof of} (c). For \eqref{cl.3}, we first note
\begin{align*}
\widetilde W - W &=5\left[(Q_b+ \varepsilon+p  Y_0)^4 -   Q^4\right]  (p-q) + 10(Q_b+\varepsilon+p  Y_0)^3 (p^2-q^2) \\
&+ 10(Q_b+\varepsilon+p  Y_0)^2 (p^3-q^3) + 5(Q_b+\varepsilon+p  Y_0) (p^4-q^4).
\end{align*}

Thus, 
 \begin{align*}
&  \int e^{-\frac 34 {|y|}} |W-\widetilde W|  \\ &\lesssim
\left(  |p|+|b| \right) \int   e^{- \frac 34 {|y|}}  |p-q|
+   \left( \int \varepsilon^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{10}} \right)^{\frac 12}\left( \int   e^{-(\frac 32-\frac 1{10}) {|y|}}  |p-q|^2\right)^{\frac 12}  \\ & + \int   e^{-\frac 34 {|y|}} |p^2-q^2|   \lesssim
\left(  |p|+|b| + \left( \int \varepsilon^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{10}} \right)^{\frac 12}\right)  \frac {\lambda}{x}|p|,
\end{align*}
 using \eqref{cl.2}, and the following similar estimate
$$
e^{-\frac 34 {|y|}} |p^2-q^2| \lesssim \frac {\lambda}{x} p^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{4}}.
$$
nodes.statement_short: Expand W - tilde W and use (cl.2) to obtain (cl.3).

nodes.name: Projections of tilde W
nodes.statement: Next, \eqref{cl.4} follows from the parity properties and then direct estimates. \eqref{cl.5} follows from direct estimates. Note that   $p^2$   appears in \eqref{cl.5} because there is no cancellation due to parity for this term. This concludes the proof of Claim \ref{cl:one}.
nodes.statement_short: (cl.4), (cl.5) by parity and direct estimates.

nodes.name: Plan
nodes.statement: The rest of this section is therefore devoted to the proof of Proposition \ref{PR:BS}.
nodes.statement_short: The rest of the section proves Proposition 3.1.

nodes.name: Initial values of parameters
nodes.statement:
First observe by uniqueness of the decomposition that
$$
b_0=b(s_0),\quad  \lambda(s_0)=\lambda_0 \quad x(s_0)=x_0, \quad \varepsilon(s_0)=\varepsilon_0.
$$
nodes.statement_short: By uniqueness the decomposition starts at the initial parameters.

nodes.name: Exit time s^*
nodes.statement:
We now argue by contradiction, assuming that for all 
$(\lambda_0,b_0)\in \mathcal D$,    we have
$$
s^*(\lambda_0,b_0) := \mathop{\rm sup} \left\{
s\geq s_0 \hbox{ such that   (BS1)-(BS2)-(BS3) holds on $[s_0,s]$}
\right\} <+\infty.
$$
nodes.statement_short: Assume the exit time s^* is finite for all (lambda_0,b_0) in D.

nodes.name: Strategy
nodes.statement: We will derive a contradiction by first closing the bootstrap bounds (BS1)-(BS2)-(BS3), and then finding a couple $(\lambda_0,b_0)$ using a topological argument.
nodes.statement_short: Close (BS2)-(BS3), then choose (lambda_0,b_0) by a topological argument.

nodes.name: Case beta > 1/3
nodes.statement:
Let $\frac 13 <\beta<\frac {11}{20}$. Then
 $$
 t(s) = \int_{s_0}^{s} \lambda^3(s') ds' \leq 
 10^3 \int_{s_0}^{s} (s')^{-3 \beta} ds'  
 \leq \frac {10^3}  {3\beta-1} \left(s_0^{-3\beta+1}-s^{-3\beta +1}\right)
 <1
 $$
 for $s_0$ large enough.
nodes.statement_short: For beta>1/3 the elapsed time t(s) stays below 1.
nodes.section: 3.2 First consequences of the bootstrap bounds

nodes.name: Case beta = 1/3
nodes.statement:
For $\beta = \frac 13$,
 $$
 t(s) = \int_{s_0}^{s} \lambda^3(s') ds' \leq 10^3\, {\rm log}\frac s{s_0} \quad 
 \hbox{so that} \quad s \geq s_0 e^{10^{-3} t}.
 $$
 Thus,
 $$
 x(s) \geq \frac 3{20} s^{\frac 23} \geq \frac 3{20} s_0^{\frac 23} e^{\frac 23 10^{-3} t}\geq 10 t^3 .
 $$
 for $s_0$ large enough.
 Since $x(s) \geq \frac 45 x_0$, we obtain $x(t) >  t^3 + \frac 12 x_0$.
nodes.statement_short: For beta=1/3 s grows exponentially in t, so x(t) dominates.
nodes.section: 3.2 First consequences of the bootstrap bounds

nodes.name: Case beta < 1/3
nodes.statement:
Finally, for $0<\beta <\frac 13$,
 $$
 t(s) = \int_{s_0}^{s} \lambda^3(s') ds' \leq \frac {10^3}  {1-3\beta} \left(s^{1-3\beta}-s_0^{1-3\beta}\right)
 $$
so that for $s_0$ large
$$s \geq \left( \frac {(1-3\beta) t}{10^3}+s_0^{1-3\beta}\right)^{\frac 1 {1-3\beta}} \geq 100 t^{\frac {1+\beta}{1-\beta}},
 $$
and
 $$x(s) \geq \frac 3{20} s^{1-\beta} \geq 15  t^{1+\beta}.$$
  Since $x(s) \geq \frac 45 x_0$, we obtain $x(t) >  t^{1+\beta} + \frac 23 x_0$.\\
nodes.statement_short: For beta<1/3 s grows polynomially, so x(t) dominates.
nodes.section: 3.2 First consequences of the bootstrap bounds

nodes.name: Bound on p
nodes.statement:
The estimate \eqref{BSp} is a consequence of \eqref{cl.1bis} and
 $\frac \beta 2 + (1-\beta) \theta = 1$, so that
 $$ 0< p \lesssim \lambda^{\frac 12 } x^{-\theta} (s) \lesssim
 s^{-\frac \beta 2} s^{-\theta  (1-\beta)} \lesssim \frac 1s.
 $$
nodes.statement_short: (BSp) from (cl.1bis) and beta/2+(1-beta)theta=1.
nodes.section: 3.2 First consequences of the bootstrap bounds

nodes.name: Remaining estimates
nodes.statement:
The estimates  \eqref{BSlsl}-\eqref{BSfond} are   immediate consequences  of \eqref{eq:2002bis}-\eqref{fond}, 
 \eqref{cl.2tri}, the bootstrap assumptions and the upper bound $\beta<\frac {11}{20}$.
nodes.statement_short: Remaining bounds follow from Proposition 2.4 and the bootstrap.
nodes.section: 3.2 First consequences of the bootstrap bounds

nodes.name: Integrate tail monotonicity
nodes.statement:
From Lemma \ref{lemmatail}, (BS2) and (BS3), 
$$
 \frac d{ds} \left\{ \lambda^{10} \int \varphi_{10} \varepsilon^2 \right\}
\lesssim \lambda^{10}\left(\mathcal N_{1,\rm loc} + s^{-2}\right) 
\lesssim  s^{-10 \beta -2},
$$
so that by integration on $[s_0,s]$, and \eqref{A2},
$$
\lambda^{10}(s)\int \varphi_{10} \varepsilon^2(s) \leq
\lambda^{10}(s_0) \int \varphi_{10} \varepsilon^2(s_0) + Cs_0^{-1-10\beta}
\leq 2.
$$
nodes.statement_short: Integrate Lemma 3.2 on [s_0,s].

nodes.name: Weighted tail bound
nodes.statement_short: Deduce (aa3).

nodes.name: Apply monotonicity formula
nodes.statement_short: Apply Lemma 3.3 with j=5/2.

nodes.name: Integrate in time
nodes.statement:
The initial smallness {\rm (\ref{A2})} ensures $$s_0^{10}|\mathcal F_i(0)|\lesssim 1$$ and thus the time integration of {\rm (\ref{neovneogbgeo})} on $[s_0,s^*]$ yields:
$$
\mathcal F_i (s)\lesssim s^{- \frac 52}  s_0^{-\delta}
$$
for some $\delta=\delta(\beta)>0$.
nodes.statement_short: Integrate using the smallness of the initial data.

nodes.name: Conclude via coercivity
nodes.statement:
Using \eqref{lowerbound}, we conclude:
$$
\mathcal N_i(s) \leq s^{- \frac 52}    s_0^{-\delta} +s^{-4} \leq \frac 12 s^{- \frac 52}
$$
for $s_0$ large enough, which together with \eqref{aa3} and the control of the full $H^1$ norm through the conservation laws {\rm (\ref{twobound})}, {\rm (\ref{energbound})} concludes the proof of (BS3').
nodes.statement_short: Coercivity gives N_i <= s^{-5/2}/2; conclude (BS3').

nodes.name: Bounds on g_s and modulation
nodes.statement_short: From (fond), (eq:2002bis): bounds (dg), (dl), (dx).

nodes.name: lambda in terms of x
nodes.statement:
By (BS1) and (BS2), we have using $(1-\beta)(\theta-1) =\frac \beta 2$ the estimate:
\begin{align}
& \left| \lambda (s) -  \left(\frac 2 {\int Q} c_0 \frac {1}{\theta-1}\right)^2  {x^{-2 \theta+2}(s)} \right| \\ &=
\left| \lambda^{\frac 12} (s) + \frac 2 {\int Q} c_0 \frac {1}{\theta-1} {x^{-\theta+1}(s)}\right| \left|  \lambda^{\frac 12} (s) - \frac 2 {\int Q} c_0 \frac {1}{\theta-1} {x^{-\theta+1}(s)}\right|\nonumber \\
&\lesssim |f(s)| \left( \lambda^{\frac 12} (s)+x^{-\theta+1}(s)\right)
\lesssim s^{-\frac \beta 2 - \frac 1{10} } \left( s^{-\frac \beta 2} + s^{-(1-\beta)(\theta-1)}\right) \lesssim s^{-  \beta   - \frac 1{10}}.\nonumber
\end{align}
nodes.statement_short: (BS1) gives lambda close to a power of x.

nodes.name: ODE for x
nodes.statement:
Using \eqref{dx}, we find
$$
\left| x_s (s) -  \left(\frac 2 {\int Q} c_0 \frac {1}{\theta-1}\right)^2  {x^{-2 \theta+2}(s)} \right| 
\lesssim   s^{-  \beta   - \frac 1{10}} + s^{-\frac 54 -   \beta }
\lesssim s^{-  \beta   - \frac 1{10}}.
$$
and hence\begin{equation} \left| \left(x^{\frac 1{1-\beta}}\right)_s - (1-\beta)^{-(1-\beta)} \right| \lesssim s^{-\frac 1{10}},
\end{equation}
from $2\theta-1=\frac 1{1-\beta}$ 
and the choice of   $c_0$  in {\rm (\ref{defcobeta})} which gives:
$$
(1-\beta)^{-(1-\beta)}= (2\theta-1)\left(\frac 2 {\int Q} c_0 \frac {1}{\theta-1}\right)^2. 
$$
nodes.statement_short: Obtain the ODE (vnkrvrnorn) for x^{1/(1-beta)}.

nodes.name: Asymptotics of x
nodes.statement:
Since from {\rm (\ref{initixzero})}:
$$
 \frac {(1-\beta) }{s_0^{1-\beta}} x (s_0)=  1,$$
the time integration of {\rm (\ref{vnkrvrnorn})} on $[s_0,s]$ yields
$$
\left|x^{\frac 1{\beta-1}}(s) -  (1-\beta)^{-\frac 1{\beta-1}} s \right| \lesssim s^{1-\frac 1{10}}.
$$
Thus,     
 \begin{equation} \left|  \frac {(1-\beta)}{s^{1-\beta}}  x (s) - 1\right| \lesssim s^{-\frac 1{10}}.
 \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Integrate in time to get (aa2).

nodes.name: Asymptotics of lambda
nodes.statement_short: Insert into (bbb2) to get (aaa2).

nodes.name: Asymptotics of b
nodes.statement:
Finally, using $|g(s)| \leq s^{-1 + 2 \beta - \frac 1{5}}$,
we find
\begin{equation} \left| \frac {s}{\beta } b(s) -1\right|  \lesssim s^{-\frac 1{10}}.
\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Use the bound on g to get (aaaa2).

nodes.name: Conclusion
nodes.statement: From \eqref{aa2}, \eqref{aaa2} and \eqref{aaaa2}, (BS2') follows for $s_0$ large enough.
nodes.statement_short: (BS2') follows for s_0 large.

nodes.name: Goal
nodes.statement: We now claim from a standard topological argument based on the ougoing behavior of the ODE's for $(f,g)$ that we can find $(b_0,\lambda_0)\in \mathcal D$ such that the remaining condition $(BS1)$ is closed.\\
nodes.statement_short: Find (b_0,lambda_0) in D closing (BS1).
nodes.section: 3.5 Choice of $\lambda_0$ and $b_0$ by a topological argument

nodes.name: Functions G, F, H
nodes.statement:
Indeed, let $$
G(s) = g(s) s^{1-2 \beta + \frac 1{5}},\quad
F(s) = f(s) s^{\frac \beta 2+ \frac 1{10}},
$$
and
$$
H(s) = F^2(s) + G^2(s).
$$
nodes.statement_short: Introduce the renormalized G, F and H=F^2+G^2.
nodes.section: 3.5 Choice of $\lambda_0$ and $b_0$ by a topological argument

nodes.name: Exit condition
nodes.statement_short: At the exit time, H(s^*)=1.
nodes.section: 3.5 Choice of $\lambda_0$ and $b_0$ by a topological argument

nodes.name: Outgoing behavior and Brouwer argument
nodes.statement:
We first claim the strict outgoing behavior:
\begin{equation} H'(s^*)\geq \frac {1}{20 s^*}.
\end{equation}
\emph{Proof of \eqref{dFdG}.}
Since
$$
G'(s) = \left(1- 2 \beta +\frac 1{5}\right) g(s)s^{-2 \beta + \frac 1{5}}
+g'(s) s^{1-2 \beta + \frac 1{5}},
 $$
 we have using {\rm (\ref{dFdG})}:
 \begin{equation} G'(s^*)= \left(1- 2 \beta +\frac 1{5}\right) \frac {G(s^*)}{s^*}
 +O\left((s^*)^{-(1+\frac 1{20})}\right).
 \end{equation}
 Similarly,
 $$
 F'(s^*)= \left(\frac \beta 2+ \frac 1{10}\right) f(s^*) (s^*)^{\frac \beta 2+ \frac 1{10}-1}
 + f'(s^*) (s^*)^{\frac \beta 2+ \frac 1{10}}.
 $$
 We now estimate $f'(s)$. By direct computations and then \eqref{dl}, \eqref{dx}
 and (BS1)-(BS2), 
 \begin{align*}
 f'(s) &= \frac 12 \frac {\lambda_s}{\lambda} \lambda^{\frac 12} - \frac 2{\int Q}c_0 
   x_s x^{-\theta}  \\
 & = \frac 12 \lambda^{\frac 52} \left[
 \frac b{\lambda^2}  - \frac 4{\int Q} c_0  \lambda^{-\frac 32} x^{-\theta}\right]
+O\left(s^{-\frac 54-\frac \beta 2}\right) \\
 &= \frac 12 \lambda^{\frac 52} g(s) + O\left(s^{-\frac 54-\frac \beta 2}\right) 
 = O\left(s^{-1  -\frac \beta 2 -\frac 1{5}}\right).
 \end{align*}
 Thus, 
 \begin{equation} F'(s^*)=\left(\frac \beta 2+ \frac 1{10}\right) \frac {F(s^*)} {s^*} + O\left( (s^*)^{-1-\frac 1{10}} \right). 
 \end{equation}
 
 Therefore
 $$
 H'(s^*) = 2 F'(s^*)F(s^*) + 2 G'(s^*) G(s^*) 
 \geq \frac 1{10} \frac {H(s^*)}{s^*} + O\left((s^*)^{-1-\frac 1{20}}\right)
 \geq \frac 1{20s^*},
 $$
for $s_0$ large enough.

\medskip

By  standard arguments (see e.g. the proof of Lemma 6 in \cite{MMC}),
the strict outgoing behavior {\rm (\ref{dFdG})} ensures that the map $(\lambda_0,b_0)\in \mathcal D \to s^*(x_0,b_0)$
is continuous.
We  define the continuous maps
\begin{align*}
 \lambda_0(F_0) &= s_0^{-\beta}\left( 1 - F_0 s_0^{-\frac 1{10}} \right)^2
\\
  b_0(F_0,G_0) &= \beta s_0^{-1+\frac \beta 2} \lambda_0^{\frac 12}(F_0 ) \left( 1+ \frac 1\beta G_0 s_0^{\frac 32\beta - \frac 1{5}}  \lambda_0^{\frac 32} (F_0)
   \right)\\
  & = \beta s_0^{-1} \left| 1 - F_0 s_0^{-\frac 1{10}}\right|
  \left( 1+ \frac 1\beta G_0 s_0^{- \frac 1{5}}  \left| 1 - F_0 s_0^{-\frac 1{10}}\right|^3
   \right)
\end{align*}
so that
\begin{align*}
G_0 &= s_0^{1-2 \beta +\frac 1{5}} \left( \frac {b_0}{\lambda_0^2} 
- \frac 4{\int Q} c_0  \lambda_0^{-\frac 32} x_0^{-\theta}\right)\\
F_0 &= s_0^{\frac \beta 2 +\frac 1{10}} \left( \lambda_0^{\frac 12} 
+\frac 2{\int Q} c_0 \frac 1{\theta-1} x_0^{-\theta+1} \right).
\end{align*}

Now, consider the continous map
\begin{align*}
\mathcal M \ : \ \   \   \mathcal B_{\mathbb{R}^2}  &\to  \mathcal S_{\mathbb{R}^2} ,\\
   (F_0,G_0) &\mapsto \left(F(s^*(\lambda_0(F_0),b_0(F_0,G_0))), G(s^*(\lambda_0(F_0),b_0(F_0,G_0)))\right).
\end{align*}
where $\mathcal B_{\mathbb{R}^2}$ and $\mathcal S_{\mathbb{R}^2} $ are, respectively, the ball and  the sphere of $\mathbb{R}^2$ of radius $1$. For $(F_0,G_0)\in \mathcal S_{\mathbb{R}^2}$, we have
$\mathcal M(F_0,G_0) = (F_0,G_0)$, in other words, 
$\mathcal M$ is the identity on the sphere
$\mathcal S_{\mathbb{R}^2}$. The existence of such a continuous map 
$\mathcal M$ is  in contradiction with Brouwer's fixed point theorem. Therefore, there exists $\lambda_0$ and $b_0$ such that
\begin{equation} | \lambda_0 - s_0^{-\beta}| \leq s_0^{-\beta - \frac 1{10}},
\quad |b_0 - \beta s_0^{-1}| \leq s_0^{-1- \frac 1{10}},
\end{equation}
and $s^*(\lambda_0,b_0)=+\infty$. 
In particular (BS1)-(BS2)-(BS3) hold on $[s_0,+\infty)$.\\
Finally, \eqref{aa2}, \eqref{aaa2} and \eqref{aaaa2} imply \eqref{sharp}.\\

This concludes the proof of Proposition \ref{PR:BS} and therefore also of Theorem \ref{th:1}.
