nodes.name: G' at exit
nodes.statement_short: Compute G'(s^*).
nodes.section: 3.5 Choice of $\lambda_0$ and $b_0$ by a topological argument

nodes.name: F' formula
nodes.statement:
Similarly,
 $$
 F'(s^*)= \left(\frac \beta 2+ \frac 1{10}\right) f(s^*) (s^*)^{\frac \beta 2+ \frac 1{10}-1}
 + f'(s^*) (s^*)^{\frac \beta 2+ \frac 1{10}}.
 $$
nodes.statement_short: Formula for F'(s^*).
nodes.section: 3.5 Choice of $\lambda_0$ and $b_0$ by a topological argument

nodes.name: Estimate of f'
nodes.statement:
We now estimate $f'(s)$. By direct computations and then \eqref{dl}, \eqref{dx}
 and (BS1)-(BS2), 
 \begin{align*}
 f'(s) &= \frac 12 \frac {\lambda_s}{\lambda} \lambda^{\frac 12} - \frac 2{\int Q}c_0 
   x_s x^{-\theta}  \\
 & = \frac 12 \lambda^{\frac 52} \left[
 \frac b{\lambda^2}  - \frac 4{\int Q} c_0  \lambda^{-\frac 32} x^{-\theta}\right]
+O\left(s^{-\frac 54-\frac \beta 2}\right) \\
 &= \frac 12 \lambda^{\frac 52} g(s) + O\left(s^{-\frac 54-\frac \beta 2}\right) 
 = O\left(s^{-1  -\frac \beta 2 -\frac 1{5}}\right).
 \end{align*}
 Thus, 
 \begin{equation} F'(s^*)=\left(\frac \beta 2+ \frac 1{10}\right) \frac {F(s^*)} {s^*} + O\left( (s^*)^{-1-\frac 1{10}} \right). 
 \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: f'(s) = lambda^{5/2} g/2 + small, giving (fstar).
nodes.section: 3.5 Choice of $\lambda_0$ and $b_0$ by a topological argument

nodes.name: Outgoing inequality
nodes.statement:
Therefore
 $$
 H'(s^*) = 2 F'(s^*)F(s^*) + 2 G'(s^*) G(s^*) 
 \geq \frac 1{10} \frac {H(s^*)}{s^*} + O\left((s^*)^{-1-\frac 1{20}}\right)
 \geq \frac 1{20s^*},
 $$
for $s_0$ large enough.

\medskip
nodes.section: 3.5 Choice of $\lambda_0$ and $b_0$ by a topological argument

nodes.name: Continuity of exit time
nodes.statement:
By  standard arguments (see e.g. the proof of Lemma 6 in \cite{MMC}),
the strict outgoing behavior {\rm (\ref{dFdG})} ensures that the map $(\lambda_0,b_0)\in \mathcal D \to s^*(x_0,b_0)$
is continuous.
nodes.statement_short: Outgoing behaviour makes the exit time continuous.
nodes.section: 3.5 Choice of $\lambda_0$ and $b_0$ by a topological argument

nodes.name: Parametrization of initial data
nodes.statement_short: Parametrize (lambda_0,b_0) by (F_0,G_0).
nodes.section: 3.5 Choice of $\lambda_0$ and $b_0$ by a topological argument

nodes.name: Exit map M
nodes.statement:
Now, consider the continous map
\begin{align*}
\mathcal M \ : \ \   \   \mathcal B_{\mathbb{R}^2}  &\to  \mathcal S_{\mathbb{R}^2} ,\\
   (F_0,G_0) &\mapsto \left(F(s^*(\lambda_0(F_0),b_0(F_0,G_0))), G(s^*(\lambda_0(F_0),b_0(F_0,G_0)))\right).
\end{align*}
where $\mathcal B_{\mathbb{R}^2}$ and $\mathcal S_{\mathbb{R}^2} $ are, respectively, the ball and  the sphere of $\mathbb{R}^2$ of radius $1$. For $(F_0,G_0)\in \mathcal S_{\mathbb{R}^2}$, we have
$\mathcal M(F_0,G_0) = (F_0,G_0)$, in other words, 
$\mathcal M$ is the identity on the sphere
$\mathcal S_{\mathbb{R}^2}$.
nodes.statement_short: The exit map M from the ball to the sphere is the identity on the sphere.
nodes.section: 3.5 Choice of $\lambda_0$ and $b_0$ by a topological argument

nodes.name: Brouwer contradiction
nodes.statement:
The existence of such a continuous map 
$\mathcal M$ is  in contradiction with Brouwer's fixed point theorem.
nodes.statement_short: Such a retraction contradicts Brouwer's fixed point theorem.
nodes.section: 3.5 Choice of $\lambda_0$ and $b_0$ by a topological argument

nodes.name: Conclusion
nodes.statement:
Therefore, there exists $\lambda_0$ and $b_0$ such that
\begin{equation} | \lambda_0 - s_0^{-\beta}| \leq s_0^{-\beta - \frac 1{10}},
\quad |b_0 - \beta s_0^{-1}| \leq s_0^{-1- \frac 1{10}},
\end{equation}
and $s^*(\lambda_0,b_0)=+\infty$. 
In particular (BS1)-(BS2)-(BS3) hold on $[s_0,+\infty)$.\\
Finally, \eqref{aa2}, \eqref{aaa2} and \eqref{aaaa2} imply \eqref{sharp}.\\

This concludes the proof of Proposition \ref{PR:BS} and therefore also of Theorem \ref{th:1}. 
  
  








\appendix
nodes.statement_short: Some (lambda_0,b_0) never exits; (sharp) follows.
nodes.section: 3.5 Choice of $\lambda_0$ and $b_0$ by a topological argument

nodes.name: Recall setting
nodes.statement:
Recall that  $c_0\in \mathbb{R}$ and $\theta>1$ are  fixed,  $x_0\gg 1$ is to be taken large enough and $q_0$ is the solution of 
\begin{equation} \partial_t q_0 + \partial_x(\partial_x^2 q_0 + q_0^5)=0,\quad
 q_0(0,x)= f_0(x),
\end{equation}
where the function $f_0$ is   smooth and satisfies
\begin{equation} f_0(x)= c_0 x^{-\theta} \hbox{ for $x>\frac {x_0}2$},\quad
f_0(x)=0 \hbox{ for $x<\frac {x_0}4$}, 
\end{equation}
\begin{equation} \hbox{ for all $x\in \mathbb{R}$, for all $k\geq 0$},\quad 
\left|\frac {d^{k}f_0}{dx^k} (x)\right| \lesssim c_0 |x|^{-\theta - k}.
\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Recall the tail f_0 and the equation of q_0.

nodes.name: Global existence of q_0
nodes.statement:
First, for $x_0$ large enough, $\|f_0\|_{L^2}$ is small and it follows from the $L^2$ and $H^s$ Cauchy theory (Corollary 2.9 in \cite{KPV})
that $q_0$ is global and bounded in $H^s$ for all $s\geq 0$, with
$$\mathop{\rm sup}_t\|q_0(t)\|_{H^s}\lesssim \delta(x_0^{-1}).$$
nodes.statement_short: Small L^2 data: q_0 is global and bounded in H^s (KPV).

nodes.name: q_1 = q_0 - f_0
nodes.statement:
We define
$$
q_1(t,x)  = q_0(t,x) -f_0(x),
$$
\begin{equation} \partial_t q_1 + \partial_x(\partial_x^2 q_1 + (q_1+f_0)^5-f_0^5)=F_0,\quad
 q_1(0,x)= 0, 
\end{equation}
where
$$
F_0 = -\partial_x^3 f_0 - \partial_x(f_0^5).
$$
nodes.statement_short: Introduce q_1 and its forced equation.

nodes.name: Weights and functionals
nodes.statement:
For any $\bar \theta\geq 0$, define a smooth function $\varphi_{\bar \theta}$ such that
\begin{equation} \varphi_{\bar \theta}(x) = x^{\bar \theta}  \text{ for $x\geq 4$},\quad
\varphi_{\bar \theta}(x) =  e^{\frac x8}   \text{ for $x\leq 0$},\quad
\varphi'\geq 0,\  \varphi'''\leq \frac 14 \varphi' \text{ on $\mathbb{R}$}.
\end{equation}
For 
$$
0\leq \theta_1< 2 \theta+4, \quad \theta_1 \neq 2 \theta+3,
$$
    set
\begin{align*}
M_{\theta_1}(t)& = \int q_1^2(t) \varphi_{\theta_1}\left( x - \frac t 4 - \frac {x_0} 4\right) dx,
\\
E_{\theta_1}(t) &= \int \left( (\partial_x q_1)^2(t) -\frac 13 \left( (q_1+f_0)^6 - f_0^6 - 6 q_1 f_0^5\right)   \right)\varphi_{\theta_1+2}\left( x - \frac t 4 - \frac {x_0} 4 \right) dx,\\\
F_{\theta_1,k}(t) &= \int (\partial_x^k q_1)^2(t) \varphi_{\theta_1+2k}\left( x - \frac t 4 - \frac {x_0} 4\right) dx, \ k\geq 2.
\end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Define weights phi and weighted functionals M, E, F.

nodes.name: Weighted mass derivative
nodes.statement:
We differentiate $M_{\theta_1}(t)$ (omitting the variable $x - \frac t 4 - \frac {x_0} 4$ for the function $\varphi_{\theta_1}$):
\begin{align*}
M_{\theta_1}'(t) & = - 3 \int (\partial_x q_1)^2 \varphi_{\theta_1}' -\frac 14 \int q_1^2 \varphi_{\theta_1}'
+ \int q_1^2 \varphi_{\theta_1}'''  \\ &
+ 2 \int \left((q_1+f_0)^5 - f_0^5\right) (q_1 \varphi_{\theta_1})_x + 
2 \left|\int F_0 q_1 \varphi_{\theta_1} \right|\\
& \leq - 3 \int (\partial_x q_1)^2 \varphi_{\theta_1}' -\frac 3{16} \int q_1^2 \varphi_{\theta_1}'
- 2 \int \left[ \frac {(q_1+f_0)^6}6 - \frac   {f_0^6} 6-(q_1+f_0)^5 q_1\right] \varphi_{\theta_1}'
\\ & + 2 \int \left[ (q_1+f_0)^5 - 5 q_1^4 f_0-f_0^5\right] f_0' \varphi_{\theta_1}
+ 2 \left|\int F_0^2  \frac {\varphi_{\theta_1}^2}{\varphi_{\theta_1}'} \right|^{\frac 12}
 \left| \int q_1^2 \varphi_{\theta_1}'\right|^{\frac 12} \\
& \leq - 3 \int (\partial_x q_1)^2 \varphi_{\theta_1}' -\frac 1 8 \int q_1^2 \varphi_{\theta_1}' 
+\delta(x_0^{-1}) \int q_1^2 \varphi_{\theta_1}'   + C \int F_0^2  \frac {\varphi_{\theta_1}^2}{\varphi_{\theta_1}'}     .
\end{align*}
Thus, for $x_0$ large enough, we have obtained
$$
M_{\theta_1}'(t) + \frac 1{10}  \int \left[ (\partial_x q_1)^2 + q_1^2 \right] \varphi_{\theta_1}'
\lesssim \int F_0^2  \frac {\varphi_{\theta_1}^2}{\varphi_{\theta_1}'}   .
$$
nodes.statement_short: Differentiate M and bound by the source term.

nodes.name: Source term bound
nodes.statement_short: Bound the F_0 term, (Fzero).

nodes.name: Weighted mass estimate
nodes.statement:
Therefore, using also $M_{\theta_1}(0)=0$, we find by integration:
\begin{equation} M_{\theta_1}(t) +  \int_0^t\int \left[ (\partial_x q_1)^2 + q_1^2 \right] \varphi_{\theta_1}' \lesssim 
\begin{cases} (t+x_0)^{ \theta_1 -2 \theta-3 } & \hbox{if $0<\theta_1 {-}2 \theta{-}3<1$}  \\
  x_0^{ \theta_1 -2 \theta-3 } & \hbox{if $\theta_1 {-}2 \theta{-}3<0$} \end{cases} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Integrate to obtain (eqM).

nodes.name: Energy derivative
nodes.statement:
We argue similarly for $E_{\theta_1}(t)$. 
\begin{align*}
E_{\theta_1}'(t) & = 2 \int \partial_t q_1 \left[ - \partial_x^2 q_1 - \left((q_1+f_0)^5 - f_0^5\right)\right] \varphi_{\theta_1+2}\\
&  - 2 \int \partial_t q_1 \partial_x q_1 \varphi_{\theta_1+2}'
- \frac  14 \int\left[ (\partial_x q_1)^2(t) -\frac 13 \left( (q_1+f_0)^6 - f_0^6 - 6 q_1 f_0^5\right)   \right]\varphi_{\theta_1+2}'
\\ &= - \int \left[ \partial_x^2 q_1 + \left((q_1+f_0)^5 - f_0^5\right) \right]^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+2}'\\
& - 2 \int \left[ \partial_x^2 q_1 + (q_1 + f_0)^5 - f_0^5\right] F_0\varphi_{\theta_1+2}\\
& + 2 \int \left[ \partial_x^2 q_1 + (q_1 + f_0)^5 - f_0^5\right]_x \partial_x q_1 \varphi_{\theta_1+2}'
  - 2 \int F_0 \partial_x q_1 \varphi_{\theta_1+2}' 
\\ &- \frac  14 \int\left[ (\partial_x q_1)^2(t) -\frac 13 \left( (q_1+f_0)^6 - f_0^6 - 6 q_1 f_0^5\right)   \right]\varphi_{\theta_1+2}'.
\end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Differentiate the weighted energy.

nodes.name: Term estimates
nodes.statement_short: Estimate each term of E'.

nodes.name: Weighted energy estimate
nodes.statement_short: Combine and integrate to obtain (eqE).

nodes.name: Coercivity of E
nodes.statement_short: Lower bound on E gives (eqEbb).

nodes.name: Pointwise decay
nodes.statement_short: Pointwise bounds (linfty), (A11).

nodes.name: Induction hypothesis
nodes.statement:
Finally, we briefly treat the case of higher order derivatives.
We use an induction argument, assuming at the rank $k$  that for all
$1\leq k'<k$,  for all $x$, $t$
\begin{align}\nonumber
& \int_0^t \int (\partial_x^{k'} q_1)^2(t) \varphi_{\theta_1+2k'}' \left( x - \frac t4-\frac {x_0} 4\right) dt
+
\int (\partial_x^{k'} q_1(t))^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+2k'}\left( x - \frac t4-\frac {x_0} 4\right) \\ & +|\partial_x^{k'-1} q_1(t)|^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+2k'-1}\left( x - \frac t4-\frac {x_0} 4\right) 
  \lesssim \begin{cases} (t+x_0)^{ \theta_1 -2 \theta-3 } & \hbox{if $0<\theta_1 {-}2 \theta{-}3<1$}  \\
  x_0^{ \theta_1 -2 \theta-3 } & \hbox{if $\theta_1 {-}2 \theta{-}3<0$} \end{cases}
\end{align}
we prove the same estimates for $k'=k$ using $F_{\theta_1,k}$.
nodes.statement_short: Induction on the number of derivatives.

nodes.name: Derivative of F_k
nodes.statement:
Indeed, by simple computation:
\begin{align*}
F_{\theta_1,k}'(t) & = 2 \int (\partial_x^k  q_1)_t (\partial_x^k q_1) \varphi_{\theta_1+2k} -
\frac 12 \int (\partial_x^k q_1)^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+2k}'\\
& = - 2 \int (\partial_x^{k+3} q_1) (\partial_x^k q_1) \varphi_{\theta_1+2k} 
- 2 \int \partial_x^{k+1} \left( (q_1+f_0)^5 -f_0^5\right) \partial_x^k q_1 \varphi_{\theta_1+2k}\\
& - \frac 12 \int (\partial_x^k q_1)^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+2k}'+ \int (\partial_x^k F_0) (\partial_x^k q_1) \varphi_{\theta_1+2k} \\
& \leq - 3 \int (\partial_x^{k+1} q_1)^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+2k}' - \frac 14 \int (\partial_x^k q_1)^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+2k}'\\
& + 2 \int \partial_x^k \left( (q_1+f_0)^5 - f_0^5\right) 
\left( (\partial_x^{k+1} q_1) \varphi_{\theta_1+2k} + (\partial_x^k q_1) \varphi_{\theta_1+2k}'\right)
\\ & + \int (\partial_x^k F_0) (\partial_x^k q_1) \varphi_{\theta_1+2k}.
\end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Compute F_k'.

nodes.name: Source term
nodes.statement:
We claim, arguing as \eqref{Fzero},
$$
\left| \int (\partial_x^k F_0) (\partial_x^k q_1) \varphi_{\theta_1+2k} \right| 
\leq \frac 1{100}\int (\partial_x^k q_1)^2  \varphi_{\theta_1+2k}'+ C t^{\theta_1-2 \theta -4}.
$$
nodes.statement_short: Bound the source term as in (Fzero).

nodes.name: Nonlinear term
nodes.statement_short: Bound the nonlinear terms, (ply3).

nodes.name: Induction step and conclusion
nodes.statement:
By integration of $F'_k$ using \eqref{ply3} and \eqref{ply2}, we obtain
$$
F_{\theta_1,k}(t) + \int_0^t \int (\partial_x^{k+1} q_1)^2 \varphi_{\theta_1+2k}' \lesssim  
\begin{cases} (t+x_0)^{ \theta_1 -2 \theta-3 } & \hbox{if $0<\theta_1 {-}2 \theta{-}3<1$}  \\
  x_0^{ \theta_1 -2 \theta-3 } & \hbox{if $\theta_1 {-}2 \theta{-}3<0$} \end{cases} 
$$
Arguing as in the proof of \eqref{linfty}, we prove \eqref{ply2}   for $k'=k$.
The induction argument being complete, we finish the proof as in \eqref{A11}.
nodes.statement_short: Integrate to close the induction, then conclude as in (A11).

nodes.name: Derivative of weighted mass
nodes.statement:
We compute from {\rm (\ref{eqofeps})}:
\begin{align*}
&\frac 12\frac{d}{ds}\int\varphi_{10}\varepsilon^2  =   \int \varepsilon_s \varepsilon \varphi_{10}\\
&=\int\varphi_{10}\varepsilon\bigg[\frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda}\Lambda \varepsilon+\left(-\varepsilon_{yy} + \varepsilon - (\varepsilon +pY_0 +Q_b )^5 + Q_b ^5 +p5 Q^4 Y_0\right)_y      \\
   &      - p_s Y_0 + (5Q^4(p-q))_y +\frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} p \Lambda Y_0+\left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right) {\Lambda} Q_b
+ \left(\frac { x_{{s}}}{\lambda} -1\right) (Q_b  + \varepsilon +pY_0)_y \\
& + \Phi_{{b}} + \Psi_{{b}} -W_y\bigg].
\end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Differentiate int phi_10 eps^2 using the eps equation.

nodes.name: Linear term
nodes.statement_short: Integrate by parts in the linear term.

nodes.name: Nonlinear term
nodes.statement_short: Remove derivatives from eps and use Sobolev.

nodes.name: pY_0 terms
nodes.statement_short: Bound terms with pY_0 by the bootstrap.

nodes.name: p_s term
nodes.statement:
By \eqref{BSbsps} and $Y_0 \in \mathcal{Y}$,
$$
\left| p_s  \int Y_0 \varphi_{10} \varepsilon\right| \lesssim 
\mathcal N_{1,\rm loc} +\frac 1{s^2}.
$$
nodes.statement_short: Bound the p_s term.

nodes.name: p-q term
nodes.statement_short: Bound the (5Q^4(p-q))_y term.

nodes.name: lambda_s p term
nodes.statement:
By \eqref{BSparam},
$$
\left|\frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} p  \int \Lambda Y_0 \varphi_{10} \varepsilon\right|
\lesssim \mathcal N_{1,\rm loc} +\frac 1{s^2}.
$$
nodes.statement_short: Bound the lambda_s p Lambda Y_0 term.

nodes.name: Modulation terms
nodes.statement:
The terms involving the geometrical parameters are controlled from the exponential localization of $Q_b$ on the right and {\rm (\ref{BSlsl})}--{\rm (\ref{BSparam})}:
$$\left|\frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda}+b\right|\left|\int\varphi_{10}\varepsilon(\Lambda Q_b)\right|\lesssim \left(\frac 1{s^2} +\mathcal N_{1,\rm loc}^{\frac12}\right)\mathcal N_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac12}\lesssim \mathcal N_{1,\rm loc}+\frac 1{s^2},$$
\begin{align*}\left|\frac{x_s}{\lambda}-1\right|\left|\int\varphi_{10}\varepsilon(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0)_y\right|&\lesssim \left(\frac 1{s^2}+\mathcal N_{1,\rm loc}^{\frac12}\right)\left[\mathcal N_{1,\rm loc}^{\frac12}+\int\varphi_{10}'\varepsilon^2\right]\\ &\lesssim \mathcal N_{1,\rm loc}+\frac 1{s^2}+\delta(\alpha^*) \int\varphi_{10}'\varepsilon^2,\end{align*}
$$\int\left|\varphi_{10}\varepsilon\Phi_b\right|\lesssim |b_s| \mathcal N_{1,\rm loc}^{\frac 12}\lesssim \frac 1{s^2} +\mathcal N_{1,\rm loc}.$$
We control similarily the interaction with the error from {\rm (\ref{eq:202})}: $$\int\left|\varphi_{10}\varepsilon\Psi_b\right|\lesssim \frac 1{s^2} \mathcal N_{1,\rm loc}^{\frac 12}\lesssim \frac 1{s^2}+\mathcal N_{1,\rm loc}.$$
nodes.statement_short: Bound geometric parameter terms and Psi_b.

nodes.name: Bound on W term
nodes.statement:
Finally, we claim
\begin{equation} \left| \int \varphi_{10} \varepsilon W_y\right|
\leq C \mathcal N_{1,\rm loc}+\frac C{s^2}  +  \frac 1{50} \int \varepsilon^2 \varphi_{10}'
\end{equation}
We only treat the first term in $W$, the other terms are similar and easier.
First,  integrating by parts, we remove the derivative from $\varepsilon$ to obtain derivative on $q$, $\varphi_{10}$.
Indeed,
\begin{align*}
& - \int \left[ 5 (Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0 )^4 q - 5 Q^4 q\right]_y \varepsilon \varphi_{10}  = \int \left[ 5 (Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0 )^4 q - 5 Q^4 q\right]  (\varepsilon \varphi_{10})_y\\
& =\int \bigg\{\left[\left(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0\right)^5- (Q_b+pY_0)^5 - 5Q^4 \varepsilon\right]_y
\\
&- 5(Q_b+pY_0)_y\left[(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0)^4-(Q_b+pY_0)^4\right] + 20 Q^3 Q_y \varepsilon \bigg\}q\varphi_{10}  
\\ &+ 5\int \left[   (Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0 )^4   -   Q^4 \right]   \varepsilon q\varphi_{10}' 
\\
& = - \int \left[\left(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0\right)^5-(Q_b+pY_0)^5 - 5Q^4 \varepsilon\right] (q_y\varphi_{10}+q \varphi_{10}') 
\\
&- 5\int \left\{(Q_b+pY_0)_y \left[(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0)^4-(Q_b+pY_0)^4\right] - 4 Q^3 Q_y \varepsilon \right\}  q\varphi_{10} 
\\ & + 5 \int \left[   (Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0 )^4  -   Q^4  \right]   \varepsilon q \varphi_{10}'
.
\end{align*}
From the above expression, we obtain for $s$ large enough (using $\|\varepsilon\|_{L^\infty} \lesssim \|\varepsilon\|_{H^1}\lesssim 
\delta(\alpha^*)$ and $\|q\|_{L^\infty(y>0)} \lesssim \frac 1s$)
\begin{align*}
&\left| \int \left[ 5 (Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0 )^4 q - 5 Q^4 q\right]_y \varepsilon \varphi_{10} \right|\\
& \lesssim 
\int (|q|+|q_y|) e^{-\frac {|y|}2} (|\varepsilon|+|p|+|b|)|\varepsilon|
+\int (|q_y|\varphi_{10} + |q|\varphi_{10}') |\varepsilon|^5 \\
& \leq  
C \mathcal N_{1,\rm loc}+\frac C{s^2}  +  \frac 1{100} \int \varepsilon^2 \varphi_{10}'+\delta(\alpha^*)\int   |\varepsilon|^2|q_y|\varphi_{10} .
\end{align*}
To control the last term above, we use
$q_y(t,y)=\lambda^{\frac 32} \partial_x q_0(t,\lambda y + x(t)) $ so that 
$
|q_y(t,y)|\lesssim \lambda^{\frac 32}  (\lambda y +x(t))^{-\theta-1} 
\lesssim \lambda^{\frac 12} x^{-\theta}(t) (y+1)^{-1},
$ for $y>10$,
and
$$
\int |\varepsilon|^2|q_y|\varphi_{10} \lesssim
\frac {\lambda^{\frac 12}}{x^{\theta}} \int_{y>0} \varepsilon^2 (y+1)^{-1} \varphi_{10}
\leq  \frac 1{100} \int \varepsilon^2 \varphi_{10}'.
$$
nodes.statement_short: Claim (Wdix) and prove it for the leading term.

nodes.name: Reduction
nodes.statement: We only treat the first term in $W$, the other terms are similar and easier.
nodes.statement_short: Treat only the first term of W.

nodes.name: Integration by parts
nodes.statement:
First,  integrating by parts, we remove the derivative from $\varepsilon$ to obtain derivative on $q$, $\varphi_{10}$.
Indeed,
\begin{align*}
& - \int \left[ 5 (Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0 )^4 q - 5 Q^4 q\right]_y \varepsilon \varphi_{10}  = \int \left[ 5 (Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0 )^4 q - 5 Q^4 q\right]  (\varepsilon \varphi_{10})_y\\
& =\int \bigg\{\left[\left(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0\right)^5- (Q_b+pY_0)^5 - 5Q^4 \varepsilon\right]_y
\\
&- 5(Q_b+pY_0)_y\left[(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0)^4-(Q_b+pY_0)^4\right] + 20 Q^3 Q_y \varepsilon \bigg\}q\varphi_{10}  
\\ &+ 5\int \left[   (Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0 )^4   -   Q^4 \right]   \varepsilon q\varphi_{10}' 
\\
& = - \int \left[\left(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0\right)^5-(Q_b+pY_0)^5 - 5Q^4 \varepsilon\right] (q_y\varphi_{10}+q \varphi_{10}') 
\\
&- 5\int \left\{(Q_b+pY_0)_y \left[(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0)^4-(Q_b+pY_0)^4\right] - 4 Q^3 Q_y \varepsilon \right\}  q\varphi_{10} 
\\ & + 5 \int \left[   (Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0 )^4  -   Q^4  \right]   \varepsilon q \varphi_{10}'
.
\end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Move derivatives onto q and phi_10.

nodes.name: Estimate
nodes.statement:
From the above expression, we obtain for $s$ large enough (using $\|\varepsilon\|_{L^\infty} \lesssim \|\varepsilon\|_{H^1}\lesssim 
\delta(\alpha^*)$ and $\|q\|_{L^\infty(y>0)} \lesssim \frac 1s$)
\begin{align*}
&\left| \int \left[ 5 (Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0 )^4 q - 5 Q^4 q\right]_y \varepsilon \varphi_{10} \right|\\
& \lesssim 
\int (|q|+|q_y|) e^{-\frac {|y|}2} (|\varepsilon|+|p|+|b|)|\varepsilon|
+\int (|q_y|\varphi_{10} + |q|\varphi_{10}') |\varepsilon|^5 \\
& \leq  
C \mathcal N_{1,\rm loc}+\frac C{s^2}  +  \frac 1{100} \int \varepsilon^2 \varphi_{10}'+\delta(\alpha^*)\int   |\varepsilon|^2|q_y|\varphi_{10} .
\end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound using smallness of eps and q.

nodes.name: Last term
nodes.statement:
To control the last term above, we use
$q_y(t,y)=\lambda^{\frac 32} \partial_x q_0(t,\lambda y + x(t)) $ so that 
$
|q_y(t,y)|\lesssim \lambda^{\frac 32}  (\lambda y +x(t))^{-\theta-1} 
\lesssim \lambda^{\frac 12} x^{-\theta}(t) (y+1)^{-1},
$ for $y>10$,
and
$$
\int |\varepsilon|^2|q_y|\varphi_{10} \lesssim
\frac {\lambda^{\frac 12}}{x^{\theta}} \int_{y>0} \varepsilon^2 (y+1)^{-1} \varphi_{10}
\leq  \frac 1{100} \int \varepsilon^2 \varphi_{10}'.
$$
nodes.statement_short: Use decay of q_y to absorb the last term.

nodes.name: Conclusion
nodes.statement:
The collection of above estimates yields the bound: 
$$\frac{d}{ds}\int\varphi_{10}\varepsilon^2+{10}\frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda}\int\varphi_{10}\varepsilon^2\lesssim \mathcal N_{1,\rm loc}+\frac 1{s^2},$$ and {\rm (\ref{keyestimate})} is proved.
nodes.statement_short: Collect estimates to obtain (keyestimate).

nodes.name: Step 1: weighted L2 controls
nodes.statement_short: Recall weighted L^2 controls on the right from MMR1.

nodes.name: Step 2: algebraic computations on F_i
nodes.statement:
{\bf step 2} Algebraic computations on $\mathcal F_{i}$.
 
First, note that the equation of $\varepsilon$ \eqref{eqofeps} can be rewritten as follows:
\begin{align}  \nonumber  
  \partial_s \varepsilon -\frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda}  \Lambda \varepsilon & = \left(-\partial_{y}^2 \varepsilon  + \varepsilon  - Z\right)_y
\\ & -p_s Y_0 +(  5 Q^4 (p-q) )_y +\frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} p\Lambda Y_0
 + \left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right) {\Lambda} Q_b 
\nonumber \\
&+ \left(\frac { x_{s}}{\lambda} -1\right) (Q_b + \varepsilon+p  Y_0)_y   
+ \Phi_{b}  
 + \Psi_{{b}} , \end{align}
where
$$
Z=(Q_b+pY_0+q+ \varepsilon )^5 -Q_b^5 - 5Q^4 (pY_0+q)-q^5,
$$
$$\Phi_b = - {b}_{s} \left(\chi_b   + \gamma   y (\chi_b)_y\right) P,\quad  -\Psi_b=\left(Q_b''- Q_b+ Q_b^5\right)'+b {\Lambda} Q_b.$$


We compute
\begin{align*}
  s^{-j} \frac d{d{s}}\left[ s^j {\mathcal F_{i}} \right]  &=
 2\int \psi_B(\varepsilon_y)_s \varepsilon_y\\
 & + 2\int \varepsilon_s \left[ \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B} - \psi_B Z\right]\\
&  -2 \int \psi_B(Q_b)_s \left[(\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5 \varepsilon Q_b^4\right]\\
& - 2 \int \psi_B (p_s Y_0+ q_s) \left[(\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 -(Q_b+pY_0+q)^5  - 5 \varepsilon Q^4\right]
\\& + 10 \int \psi_B q_s q^4 \varepsilon + \frac j s \mathcal F_{i}
\end{align*}
which we rewrite 
\begin{equation} s^{-j} \frac d{d{s}}\left[ s^j {\mathcal F_{i}} \right]  =  f^{(i)}_{1}+f^{(i)}_2+f^{(i)}_3,
 \end{equation}
  where 
{\allowdisplaybreaks
\begin{align*}
  f^{(i)}_{1} &=
      2 \int \left( \varepsilon_{s} - {\frac{{\lambda}_s}{{\lambda}}} {\Lambda} \varepsilon\right) \left( - (\psi_B\varepsilon_y)_{y} + \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B} -\psi_BZ\right) ,\\
f^{(i,j)}_2  &= 
 2 {\frac{{\lambda}_s}{{\lambda}}}  \int    {\Lambda} \varepsilon  \left( - (\psi_B\varepsilon_y)_y +  \varepsilon\varphi_{i,B} -\psi_B Z \right) +\frac js\mathcal F_{i}, \\
 f^{(i)}_3 &= 
  - 2  \int \psi_B(Q_b)_{s} \left[(\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5 \varepsilon Q_b^4\right]\\
& - 2 \int \psi_B (p_s Y_0+ q_s) \left[(\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0+q)^5  -(Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5 \varepsilon Q^4\right]\\
&+ 10 \int \psi_B q_s q^4 \varepsilon.
\end{align*}
}

We claim the following estimates on the above terms: for some $\mu_0>0$,  
\begin{align} & \frac{d }{ds} f^{(i)}_{1}\leq - \mu_0  \int   \left(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2\right)   \varphi'_{i,B}  + 
 C s^{-4},
\\ & \left|\frac{d }{ds} f^{(i)}_{k}\right|\leq \frac {\mu_0}{10}    \int   \left(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2\right)   \varphi'_{i,B}  +  C s^{-4}+  C s^{10\beta -9}, \quad \hbox{for $k=2,3.$}
\end{align}
  Inserting \eqref{re1} and \eqref{re2} into {\rm (\ref{eqfnoneoge})}   yields {\rm (\ref{lyapounovconrolbis})}
  for all $j$.
In steps 3 - step 5, we prove \eqref{re1} and \eqref{re2}.

Observe that the  definitions of $\varphi_i$ and $\psi$ imply the following estimates:
\begin{align} \forall y\in \mathbb{R}, \quad  &|\varphi_i'''(y) | + | \varphi_i''(y) |+|\psi'''(y)|+|y\psi'(y)|+|\psi(y)|
   \lesssim  \varphi'_i(y)\lesssim \varphi_i(y),\\
   \forall y\in (-\infty,2], \quad &    e^{ |y|} \psi(y)  + e^{  |y|} \psi'(y) +\varphi_i(y)\lesssim \varphi_i'(y),\\
  \forall y\in \mathbb{R}, \quad  &
  \varphi_2'(y)\lesssim \varphi_1(y) \lesssim \varphi'_2(y). \end{align}
In particular,
\begin{equation} {\mathcal{N}_{1,\rm loc}} (s) \lesssim{\mathcal{N}_{2,\rm loc}} (s) \lesssim  {\mathcal{N}_{1}} (s)\lesssim {\mathcal{N}_2} (s),\quad
\int\varepsilon^2 (s,y)     \varphi_{1,B} (y) dy\lesssim {\mathcal{N}_{2,\rm loc}} (s) .
\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Compute d/ds(s^j F_i) and split it into f_1, f_2, f_3.

nodes.name: Rewritten eps equation
nodes.statement:
{\bf step 2} Algebraic computations on $\mathcal F_{i}$.
 
First, note that the equation of $\varepsilon$ \eqref{eqofeps} can be rewritten as follows:
\begin{align}  \nonumber  
  \partial_s \varepsilon -\frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda}  \Lambda \varepsilon & = \left(-\partial_{y}^2 \varepsilon  + \varepsilon  - Z\right)_y
\\ & -p_s Y_0 +(  5 Q^4 (p-q) )_y +\frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} p\Lambda Y_0
 + \left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right) {\Lambda} Q_b 
\nonumber \\
&+ \left(\frac { x_{s}}{\lambda} -1\right) (Q_b + \varepsilon+p  Y_0)_y   
+ \Phi_{b}  
 + \Psi_{{b}} , \end{align}
where
$$
Z=(Q_b+pY_0+q+ \varepsilon )^5 -Q_b^5 - 5Q^4 (pY_0+q)-q^5,
$$
$$\Phi_b = - {b}_{s} \left(\chi_b   + \gamma   y (\chi_b)_y\right) P,\quad  -\Psi_b=\left(Q_b''- Q_b+ Q_b^5\right)'+b {\Lambda} Q_b.$$
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite the eps equation with Z, Phi_b, Psi_b.

nodes.name: Derivative of s^j F_i
nodes.statement:
We compute
\begin{align*}
  s^{-j} \frac d{d{s}}\left[ s^j {\mathcal F_{i}} \right]  &=
 2\int \psi_B(\varepsilon_y)_s \varepsilon_y\\
 & + 2\int \varepsilon_s \left[ \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B} - \psi_B Z\right]\\
&  -2 \int \psi_B(Q_b)_s \left[(\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5 \varepsilon Q_b^4\right]\\
& - 2 \int \psi_B (p_s Y_0+ q_s) \left[(\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 -(Q_b+pY_0+q)^5  - 5 \varepsilon Q^4\right]
\\& + 10 \int \psi_B q_s q^4 \varepsilon + \frac j s \mathcal F_{i}
\end{align*}
which we rewrite 
\begin{equation} s^{-j} \frac d{d{s}}\left[ s^j {\mathcal F_{i}} \right]  =  f^{(i)}_{1}+f^{(i)}_2+f^{(i)}_3,
 \end{equation}
  where 
{\allowdisplaybreaks
\begin{align*}
  f^{(i)}_{1} &=
      2 \int \left( \varepsilon_{s} - {\frac{{\lambda}_s}{{\lambda}}} {\Lambda} \varepsilon\right) \left( - (\psi_B\varepsilon_y)_{y} + \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B} -\psi_BZ\right) ,\\
f^{(i,j)}_2  &= 
 2 {\frac{{\lambda}_s}{{\lambda}}}  \int    {\Lambda} \varepsilon  \left( - (\psi_B\varepsilon_y)_y +  \varepsilon\varphi_{i,B} -\psi_B Z \right) +\frac js\mathcal F_{i}, \\
 f^{(i)}_3 &= 
  - 2  \int \psi_B(Q_b)_{s} \left[(\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5 \varepsilon Q_b^4\right]\\
& - 2 \int \psi_B (p_s Y_0+ q_s) \left[(\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0+q)^5  -(Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5 \varepsilon Q^4\right]\\
&+ 10 \int \psi_B q_s q^4 \varepsilon.
\end{align*}
}
nodes.statement_short: Compute s^{-j} d/ds(s^j F_i) = f_1+f_2+f_3.

nodes.name: Estimates (re1), (re2)
nodes.statement_short: Claim (re1), (re2), which give (lyapounovconrolbis).

nodes.name: Plan
nodes.statement: In steps 3 - step 5, we prove \eqref{re1} and \eqref{re2}.
nodes.statement_short: Steps 3-5 prove (re1), (re2).

nodes.name: Weight properties
nodes.statement:
Observe that the  definitions of $\varphi_i$ and $\psi$ imply the following estimates:
\begin{align} \forall y\in \mathbb{R}, \quad  &|\varphi_i'''(y) | + | \varphi_i''(y) |+|\psi'''(y)|+|y\psi'(y)|+|\psi(y)|
   \lesssim  \varphi'_i(y)\lesssim \varphi_i(y),\\
   \forall y\in (-\infty,2], \quad &    e^{ |y|} \psi(y)  + e^{  |y|} \psi'(y) +\varphi_i(y)\lesssim \varphi_i'(y),\\
  \forall y\in \mathbb{R}, \quad  &
  \varphi_2'(y)\lesssim \varphi_1(y) \lesssim \varphi'_2(y). \end{align}
In particular,
\begin{equation} {\mathcal{N}_{1,\rm loc}} (s) \lesssim{\mathcal{N}_{2,\rm loc}} (s) \lesssim  {\mathcal{N}_{1}} (s)\lesssim {\mathcal{N}_2} (s),\quad
\int\varepsilon^2 (s,y)     \varphi_{1,B} (y) dy\lesssim {\mathcal{N}_{2,\rm loc}} (s) .
\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Properties of the weights and comparison of norms.

nodes.name: Step 3: control of f_1
nodes.statement:
{\bf step 3} Control of $f_1^{(i)}$. Proof of \eqref{re1}. 
 We compute 
$ f_{1}^{(i)} $
using \eqref{eqebis}
\begin{align*}
  \rm f_{1}^{(i)}& = 2 \int   \left(  -\varepsilon_{yy} {+} \varepsilon  {-}Z  \right)_y \left(-(\psi_B\varepsilon_y)_y{+}\varepsilon\varphi_{i,B}{-}\psi_BZ \right) 
\\ & +2\left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right) \int {\Lambda} Q_b  \left( - (\psi_B\varepsilon_y)_y + \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B Z   \right)
\\ &   + 2 \left(\frac { x_{{s}}}{\lambda} -1\right) \int (Q_b  + \varepsilon+pY_0)_y
 \left( -(\psi_B \varepsilon_y)_y + \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B}-\psi_BZ  \right)
 \\ & + 2 \int  \Phi_{{b}}  \left( -(\psi_B \varepsilon_y)_y + \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B}-\psi_BZ   \right)
\\ & + 2 \int  \Psi_{{b}}   \left( -(\psi_B \varepsilon_y)_y + \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B}-\psi_BZ  \right) \\
& + \int \left(-p_sY_0 +(5Q^4(p-q))_y + \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} p \Lambda Y_0\right) \left( -(\psi_B \varepsilon_y)_y + \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B}-\psi_BZ  \right) 
\\ & = {{\rm f}^{(i)}_{1,1}}+ {{\rm f}^{(i)}_{1,2}}+{{\rm f}^{(i)}_{1,3}}+{{\rm f}^{(i)}_{1,4}}+{{\rm f}^{(i)}_{1,5}}+{{\rm f}^{(i)}_{1,6}}.
\end{align*}
\underline{{\em Term $f^{(i)}_{1,1}$}}:  We first integrate by parts  
\begin{eqnarray*}
f^{(i)}_{1,1}& = &  2 \int\left[  -\varepsilon_{yy} + \varepsilon  -Z  \right]_y\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon  -Z\right] \psi_B \\
& + & 2\int\left[  -\varepsilon_{yy} + \varepsilon  -Z\right]_y\left(-\psi_B'\varepsilon_y+\varepsilon(\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)\right). 
\end{eqnarray*}
We compute the various terms  :
\begin{align*} & 2\int\left[  -\varepsilon_{yy} + \varepsilon  -Z  \right]_y\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon  -Z\right]\psi_B =-\int\psi_B'\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon  -Z\right]^2\\
&  =-\int\psi_B'\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon \right]^2  - \int\psi_B'\left\{\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon  -Z\right]^2-\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+\varepsilon\right]^2\right\}\\
&   = -\left[\int\psi_B'(\varepsilon_{yy}^2+2\varepsilon_y^2)+\int\varepsilon^2(\psi_B'-\psi_B''')\right]\\
&  -\int\psi_B'\left\{\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon  -Z\right]^2-\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+\varepsilon\right]^2\right\}.
\end{align*}
Next after integration by parts:
\begin{eqnarray*}
& & 2 \int\left[  -\varepsilon_{yy} + \varepsilon\right]_y\left[-\psi_B'\varepsilon_y+\varepsilon(\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)\right]\\
&  &  =-2 \Big\{\int\psi_B'\varepsilon_{yy}^2+\int\varepsilon_y^2(\tfrac32\varphi_{i,B}'-\tfrac12\psi'_B-\tfrac12\psi_B''')\\&&+\int\varepsilon^2(\tfrac12(\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)'-\tfrac12(\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)''')\Big\},
\end{eqnarray*}

\begin{eqnarray*}
&-& 2 \int Z_y(\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)\varepsilon =
2 \int Z (\varphi_{i,B}'-\psi_B')\varepsilon + 2\int Z (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)\varepsilon_y\\
& = & 2 \int Z (\varphi_{i,B}'-\psi_B')\varepsilon - \frac 13\int(\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)'\\ &&\left\{[(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^6-(Q_b+pY_0+q)^6-6Q_b^5\varepsilon -6q^5 \varepsilon -30 Q^4(pY_0+q)\varepsilon  \right\}\\
& - & 2\int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)(Q_b)_y[(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5-(Q_b +pY_0+q)^5-5Q_b^4\varepsilon]\\
& + & 40 \int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B) Q' Q^3 (pY_0+q) \varepsilon\\
& - & 2 \int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)(p Y_0'+q_y) [(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5-(Q_b +pY_0+q)^5-5Q^4\varepsilon].
\end{eqnarray*}

We collect the above computations and obtain the following
\begin{align*}
& f^{(i)}_{1,1} = -\int\left[3\psi_B'\varepsilon_{yy}^2+(3\varphi_{i,B}'+\psi_B'-\psi_B''')\varepsilon_y^2+(\varphi_{i,B}'-\varphi_{i,B}''')\varepsilon^2\right]\\
& -\frac 13 \int \left[ (\varepsilon {+} Q_b {+}pY_0{+}q )^6{-}  {(Q_b{+}pY_0{+}q) ^6}  {-}6 Q_b ^5 \varepsilon {-} 6 q^5 \varepsilon{-} 30 Q^4(pY_0{+}q)\varepsilon{-}6Z \varepsilon \right](\varphi_{i,B}'{-}\psi_B')\\
& -   2\int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)(Q_b)_y[(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5-(Q_b +pY_0+q)^5-5Q_b^4\varepsilon]\\
& + 40 \int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B) Q' Q^3 (pY_0+q) \varepsilon\\
& -   2 \int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)(p  Y_0'+q_y) [(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5-(Q_b +pY_0+q)^5-5Q^4\varepsilon]\\
& +    2 \int Z_y \varepsilon_y \psi_B'  -  \int\psi_B'\left\{\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon  -Z \right]^2-\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+\varepsilon\right]^2\right\}\\
& =  (f^{(i)}_{1,1})^<+(f^{(i)}_{1,1})^{\sim}+(f^{(i)}_{1,1})^>
\end{align*}
where $(f^{(i)}_{1,1})^{<,\sim,>}$ respectively corresponds to integration on $y<-\frac B2$, $|y|\leq \frac B2$, $y>\frac B2$.

We recall
\begin{equation} \|\varepsilon \|_{L^\infty} \lesssim \|\varepsilon\|_{H^1} \lesssim  {\delta(\alpha^*)}  .
\end{equation}

 


$\bullet$ For the region $y<-B/2$, we rely on monotonicity type arguments and estimate using \eqref{defphi4}:
$$
\int_{y<-B/2} \varepsilon^2 |\varphi'''_{i,B}|\lesssim
  \frac 1 {B^2}  \int_{y<-B/2} \varepsilon^2 \varphi'_{i,B} \leq  \frac 1{100} \int_{y<-B/2} \varepsilon^2 \varphi'_{i,B},
$$
$$\int_{y<-B/2} \varepsilon_y^2|\psi'''_B|\lesssim
  \frac 1 {B^2}  \int_{y<-B/2} \varepsilon_y^2 \varphi'_{i,B} \leq  \frac 1{100} \int_{y<-B/2} \varepsilon_y^2 \varphi'_{i,B},$$
by choosing $B$ large enough.  
By \eqref{nonlinearsobolev} (for $B$ large and $\alpha^*$ small)
\begin{align*}
& \left| \int_{y<-B/2}  \left[ (\varepsilon {+} Q_b {+}pY_0{+}q )^6{-}  {(Q_b{+}pY_0{+}q) ^6}  {-}6 Q_b ^5 \varepsilon {-} 6 q^5 \varepsilon{-}30 Q^4(pY_0{+}q)\varepsilon{-} 6Z \varepsilon \right](\varphi_{i,B}'{-}\psi_B') \right|
\\ 
& \lesssim    
 \int_{y<-B/2} \left(\delta(\alpha^*)  + (|Q_b| ^4+|p|^4+|q|^4) \varepsilon^2
 +(|b|+|p|+|q|)^2 |\varepsilon| \right)\varphi'_{i,B} 
 \\& \lesssim  \left(\delta(\alpha^*)+\delta(s_0^{-1})+e^{-\frac B{10} }\right)\int_{y<-B/2}  \varphi_{i,B}' \varepsilon^2 
 +\frac 1{s^2} \left( \int_{y<-B/2}  \varepsilon^2   \varphi'_{i,B}\right)^{\frac 12}
 \\
& \leq    \frac 1{100} \int_{y<-B/2}  \varepsilon^2   \varphi'_{i,B}+\frac 1{s^4},
\end{align*}
where we have used from the definition of $q$ and \eqref{BSp}
$$
\left(\int q^4  \varphi'_{i,B}\right)^{\frac 12} \lesssim \frac 1{s^2}.
$$
Similarily for $\alpha^*$ small depending on $B$,
\begin{eqnarray*}
&& \bigg| \int_{y<-\frac{B}{2}}  (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)(Q_b)_y\left[(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5-(Q_b +pY_0+q)^5-5Q_b^4\varepsilon\right] \\ &&-   20 \int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B) Q' Q^3 (pY_0+q) \varepsilon 
\bigg|\\
&& \lesssim   B \int_{y<-\frac B2}\left(|\varepsilon|^5+\varepsilon^2(|Q_b|^3+|p|^3+|q|^3)\right)(|Q_y|+|b||(P\chi_b)'|)\varphi_{i,B}' \\
&&+B \int |\varepsilon|\left(  |p|^2+|q|^2\right)
(|Q_y|+|b||(P\chi_b)'| )\varphi_{i,B}'\\
&&+B \int |\varepsilon|  (|p|+|q|)   
\left| (Q_b)_y Q_b^3 - Q'Q^3\right|\varphi_{i,B}'\\&&\leq \frac 1{100} \int_{y<-B/2}  (\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2)  \varphi'_{i,B}+\frac 1{s^4}.
\end{eqnarray*}
The next term in $(f^{(i)}_{1,1})^<$ is
$$- 2\int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)(p Y_0'+q_y) [(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5-(Q_b +pY_0+q)^5-5Q^4\varepsilon].$$
To estimate it, we note the following
\begin{align*}
&\left|(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5-(Q_b +pY_0+q)^5-5Q^4\varepsilon \right|\\
& \lesssim   |\varepsilon|^5 +|\varepsilon|^2+|\varepsilon| (|b|+|p|+|q|).
\end{align*}
Now, using
\begin{equation} \int  |p|  \varphi_{i,B} dy \lesssim \frac 1{s}, 
\quad \int  |q_y|    \varphi_{i,B} dy \lesssim \frac 1{s^2},  \end{equation}
we obtain proceeding as before
\begin{align*}
&\left|\int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)(p  Y_0'+q_y) [(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5-(Q_b +pY_0+q)^5-5Q^4\varepsilon]
\right|\\ &\lesssim     \frac 1{100} \int_{y<-B/2} (\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2)  \varphi'_{i,B}+\frac 1{s^4}.
\end{align*}
  We further estimate using {\rm (\ref{nonlinearsobolev})} and   $(\varphi'_i)^2\lesssim \psi'\lesssim (\varphi'_i)^2$ for $y<-\frac 12$:
\begin{eqnarray*}
&& \left|\int Z_y \varepsilon_y \psi_b'\right| \\&& \lesssim 
\left|\int_{y<-\frac B2}\psi_B'\varepsilon_y\left\{(Q_b)_y[(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^4-Q_b^4]-Q'Q^3(pY_0+q)\right\} \right|\\
&&+\left|\int_{y<-\frac B2}\psi_B'\varepsilon_y   (pY_0'+q_y) ((Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^4-Q^4) \right| + \left| \int q_y q^4 \varepsilon\psi_B'\right|\\
&& +\left| \int_{y<-\frac B2}\psi_B'\varepsilon_y^2 (Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^4\right|\\
&& \lesssim  \left( e^{- \frac 12 B} +\delta(s_0^{-1}) +\delta(\alpha^*)\right) \int_{y<-\frac B2}\varphi'_{i,B}(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2) 
+\frac 1{s^4}\\
&& \leq 
 \frac 1{100}  \int_{y<-B/2}  (\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2)  \varphi'_{i,B}+\frac C{s^4}.
\end{eqnarray*}

 
The remaining nonlinear term is estimated using the local $H^2$ control provided by localization
(see more details in \cite{MMR1})
\begin{eqnarray*}
& & \left|\int_{y<-\frac B2}\psi_B'\left\{\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon  -Z\right]^2-\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+\varepsilon\right]^2\right\}\right|
\\
&=&   \left|\int_{y<-\frac B2}\psi_B' \left(-2\varepsilon_{yy}+ 2\varepsilon  -Z\right)  Z  \right|\\
& \leq & \frac{1}{100}\int_{y<-\frac B2}\psi_{B}'(|\varepsilon_{yy}|^2+|\varepsilon|^2)+C\int_{y<-\frac B2}(\varphi'_{i,B})^2Z^2\\
& \leq &  \frac 1{100} \int_{y<-B/2} \left[ \varepsilon_{yy}^2\psi_B'+(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2)  \varphi'_{i,B}\right]
+\frac 1{s^4}.
\end{eqnarray*}

$\bullet$ In the region $y>\frac B2$, we have $\psi_B(y)=1$, so that several terms cancel in $f_{1,1}^{(i)}$. For the remainding terms, we argue as before.
We rely on \eqref{defphi4} to estimate:
$$\int_{y>B/2} \varepsilon^2 |\varphi'''_{i,B}|\lesssim
  \frac 1 {B^2}  \int_{y>B/2} \varepsilon^2 \varphi'_{i,B} \leq  \frac 1{100} \int_{y>B/2} \varepsilon^2 \varphi'_{i,B},$$ and we use the exponential localization of $Q_b$ to the right and \eqref{nonlinearsobolev},   to control:  
  \begin{align*}
& \left| \int_{y>B/2} \left(\frac {(\varepsilon {+} Q_b {+}pY_0{+}q )^6} 6
-\frac {(Q_b{+}pY_0{+}q)^6} 6 -Q_b^5 \varepsilon - 5 Q^4 (pY_0{+}q) - Z \varepsilon  \right)  \varphi_{i,B}' \right|
\\ 
&   \lesssim 
 \int_{y>B/2} \left(\varepsilon^6  + \left(|Q_b| ^4 +p^4 +q^4 \right)\varepsilon^2
 + (|b|+|q|+|p|)^2 |\varepsilon|\right)\varphi_{i,B}' \\
 & \lesssim  (\delta(\alpha^*)+\delta(s_0^{-1})+e^{-\frac B{10}})\int_{y>B/2}  \varepsilon^2   \varphi_{i,B}' + \frac 1{s^4}\\
& \leq  \frac 1{100} \int_{y>B/2}  \varepsilon^2   \varphi'_{i,B}
+\frac C{s^4},
\end{align*}
\begin{align*}
& \Bigg| \int_{y>B/2} \left[(\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0+q )^5 -(Q_b+pY_0+q) ^5- 5 Q_b ^4 \varepsilon\right](Q_b )_y (\psi_B-\varphi_{i,B}) \\
&-20 \int_{y>B/2}  Q'Q^3 (pY_0+q) \varepsilon (\psi_B-\varphi_{i,B})\Bigg|\\
&  \leq \frac 1{100} \int_{y>B/2}   \varepsilon^2   \varphi'_{i,B} +\frac C{s^4}.
\end{align*}
Since $Y_0\in \mathcal{Y}$, we   argue similarly to obtain
\begin{align*}
&\left| \int (\psi_B-\varphi_{i,B}) pY_0' 
\left[ (Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5Q^4 \varepsilon\right]\right| \\
&\leq \frac 1{100} \int_{y>B/2}   \varepsilon^2   \varphi'_{i,B} +\frac C{s^4}.
\end{align*}
Next, we have from \eqref{BSqy},
\begin{align*}
&\left| \int (\varphi_{i,B} - \psi_B) q_y \left[ (Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5Q^4 \varepsilon\right]\right| \\
& 
 \leq \frac 1{100} \int_{y>B/2}   \varepsilon^2   \varphi'_{i,B} +\frac C{s^4}.
\end{align*}
Also,
\begin{align*}
\left| \int Z_y \varepsilon_y \psi_B'\right| =
\left| \int Z (\varepsilon_{yy} \psi_B' + \varepsilon_y \psi_B'')\right|
\leq \frac 1{100} \int (\varepsilon_{yy}^2 + \varepsilon_y^2 + \varepsilon^2) \psi_B' +\frac C{s^4}.
\end{align*}

$\bullet$ In the   region $|y|<B/2$, $\varphi_{i,B}(s,y) = 1+ y/B$ and $\psi_B(y)=1$. In particular, $\varphi_{i,B}'''=\psi_B'=0$ in this region, and we obtain:
\begin{align*}
(f^{(i)}_{1,1})^{\sim}  
&    = - \frac {1}{B} \int_{|y|<B/2}  \Big\{ 3 \varepsilon_y^2 + \varepsilon^2  \\
  &   + \frac 13  \left( (\varepsilon + Q_b +pY_0+q)^6 
-(Q_b+pY_0+q)^6  - 6 Q_b^5 \varepsilon -30 Q^4(pY_0+q)\varepsilon
 -6 Z\varepsilon \right) 
  \\
  &  + 2\left( (\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0+q )^5 -(Q_b+pY_0+q)^5- 5 Q_b ^4 \varepsilon\right) y (Q_b )_y  
\\
& -40 yQ'Q^3 (pY_0+q) \varepsilon \\
& + 2 y(p Y_0'+q_y)\left((\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0+q )^5 -(Q_b+pY_0+q) ^5- 5 Q_b ^4 \varepsilon\right)\Big\} \\
&    = - \frac {1}   { B} \int_{|y|<B/2}   \left\{ 3 \varepsilon_y^2 + \varepsilon^2 - 5 Q^4 \varepsilon^2 + 20 y Q' Q^3 \varepsilon^2\right\} + R_{\rm Vir}(\varepsilon),
\end{align*}
where
\begin{align*}
R_{\rm Vir}(\varepsilon) = - \frac {1}   { B} & \int_{|y|<B/2} \Bigg\{
\frac 13 \bigg( (\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0 + q)^6 - (Q_b+pY_0+q)^6 - 6Q_b^5 \varepsilon\\ &
-30 Q^4 (pY_0+q)\varepsilon - 6Z\varepsilon  - 15 Q^4 \varepsilon^2 \bigg)\\
& +2 \left( (\varepsilon+Q_b+ pY_0 + q)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0 + q)^5 - 5 Q_b^4 \varepsilon\right) y (Q_b)_y
\\ &- 20 y Q' Q^3 (pY_0+q) \varepsilon - 10 y Q' Q^3 \varepsilon^2 \\
& +2 y (pY_0'+q_y) \left( (\varepsilon +Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0 +q)^5 - 5Q_b^4 \varepsilon\right)\Bigg\} 
\end{align*}
As before, we estimate
\begin{align*}
|R_{\rm Vir}(\varepsilon)|&\lesssim 
\int_{|y|<B} \varepsilon^2 \left( \delta(\alpha^*) + |b|+ |p|+|q|\right)
+ \int_{|y|<B} |\varepsilon| (p^2+ q^2 + b^2)
\\&\lesssim  \frac 1{100}\int_{|y|<B/2} (\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2) +\frac 1{s^4},
\end{align*}

We now recall from \cite{MMR1} the following coercivity result.

\begin{lemma}[Localized viriel estimate] There exists $B_{0}>100$ and $\mu_{3}>0$ such that
if $B\geq B_{0}$, then
$$
\int_{|y|<B/2}   \left( 3 \varepsilon_y^2 + \varepsilon^2 - 5 Q^4 \varepsilon^2 + 20 y Q' Q^3 \varepsilon^2\right) \geq \mu_{3} \int_{|y|<B/2}  \left(  \varepsilon_y^2 + \varepsilon^2 \right)
-  \frac 1 B \int \varepsilon^2 e^{-\frac{|y|}{2}}.
$$
\end{lemma}
 
Thus for $\alpha^*$ small enough:
$$(f^{(i)}_{1,1})^\sim   \leq  - \frac { \mu_{3}}   {2 B} \int_{|y|<B/2}  \left(  \varepsilon_y^2 + \varepsilon^2 \right) + \frac 1 {B^2} \int \varepsilon^2 e^{-\frac{|y|}{2}}+\frac 1{s^4}.$$ 
The collection of above estimates yields the bound:
\begin{equation} f^{(i)}_{1,1}  \leq  - \frac  {\mu_4} B    \int\left[\psi'_B\varepsilon_{yy}^2+\varphi'_{i,B}(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2)\right] + \frac C{s^4},
    \end{equation}
    for some universal $\mu_4>0$ independent of $B$.
    
    \medskip
    
   
   
  \underline{{\em Term $f^{(i)}_{1,2}$}}:  We decompose  $f_{1,2}$ in a suitable way:
\begin{align*}
f^{(i)}_{1,2} & =  2 \left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right)  \int {\Lambda} Q  (L \varepsilon) -2\left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right)\int\varepsilon (1-\varphi_{i,B})\Lambda Q
\\
&+ 2b \left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right)  \int {\Lambda} ( \chi_b P)  \left(-(\psi_B\varepsilon_y)_{y}  + \varepsilon\varphi_{i,B} - \psi_B Z\right)\\
& + 2 \left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right)  \int {\Lambda} Q      \left(-(\psi_B)_y\varepsilon_y
-(1-\psi_B)\varepsilon_{yy}+(1-\psi_B)Z\right) \\&
+ 2\left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right)  \int {\Lambda} Q  (Z-5Q^4\varepsilon)
\end{align*}
Observe from {\rm (\ref{ortho1})}: $$\int \Lambda Q (L\varepsilon)=(\varepsilon,L\Lambda Q)=-2(\varepsilon,Q)=0.$$  We now use the orthogonality conditions $( \varepsilon, y {\Lambda} Q)=0$ and the definition of $\varphi_{i,B}$ to estimate:
$$
	\left| \int {\Lambda} Q \varepsilon (1-\varphi_{i,B}) \right| = \left| \int {\Lambda} Q \varepsilon \left(1-\varphi_{i,B}+ \frac yB\right)\right|
	\lesssim e^{- \frac B 8 } \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12}  ,
$$
so that  for $B$ large enough:
\begin{align*}
  \left|  \left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right)  \int {\Lambda} Q\varepsilon (1-\varphi_{i,B}) \right| 
&\lesssim \left( \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12}  +\frac 1{s^2} \right) e^{- \frac B 8}  \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12}  
\\ &
\leq 
 \frac 1 {500}  \frac {\mu_4} {B} \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc} 
+\frac C{s^4}.
\end{align*}
For the next term in $f_{1,2}^{(i)}$, we first integrate by parts to remove all derivatives on $\varepsilon$.
Then, by   the properties of $\varphi_{i,B}$, $\psi_B$, $P$  and $\chi_b$ \eqref{eq:210}, we obtain
for $\alpha^*$ small,
 \begin{eqnarray*}
&&\left| 2b \left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right)  \int {\Lambda} ( \chi_b P)  \left(-(\psi_B\varepsilon_y)_{y}  + \varepsilon\varphi_{i,B} - \psi_B Z\right)\right|\\
& \lesssim & |b| \left( \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12}  + \frac 1{s^2}\right)^2   \leq \frac 1 {500}  \frac {\mu_4} {B } \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc} (s)
+\frac C{s^4}.
\end{eqnarray*}
Next, integrating by parts,   using   the exponential decay of $Q$ and since $\psi_B(y)\equiv 1$ on $[-\frac B2,\infty)$:
\begin{eqnarray*}
&&\left|  \left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right)  \int {\Lambda} Q      \left(-(\psi_B)_y\varepsilon_y
-(1-\psi_B)\varepsilon_{yy}+(1-\psi_B)Z\right) \right|\\
& \lesssim & \left( \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12}  + \frac 1{s^2}\right)^2  \leq \frac 1 {500}  \frac {\mu_4} {B} \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc} +\frac C{s^4},
\end{eqnarray*}
and finally
\begin{align*}
&\left| \left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right)  \int {\Lambda} Q  \left[Z-5Q^4\varepsilon\right]
\right|  \lesssim \left( \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12} + \frac 1{s^2}\right) 
\left( \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc} + \frac 1{s^2}\right) 
\\
& \leq \frac 1 {500}  \frac {\mu_4} {B } \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc} (s)
+\frac C{s^4}.
\end{align*}
The collection of above estimates yields the bound:
 $$
 |f^{(i)}_{1,2}|\leq \frac 1 {100}  \frac {\mu_4} {B} \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc} + \frac C{s^4}.
 $$
\underline{{\em Term $f^{(i)}_{1,3}$}}: Integrating by parts, we claim the identity
\begin{align*}
& -\frac 16 \int \psi_B' \left[(Q_b+pY_0+q+\varepsilon)^6 -Q_b^6 - 6Q_b^5\varepsilon - 6Q^5(pY_0+q)
-6 Q_b q^5\right]\\
& = \int \psi_B (Q_b)_y Z - 5 \int \psi_B Q' Q^4 \varepsilon + \int (Q_b^5-Q^5)_y \varepsilon\psi_B+  5\int (Q_b-Q)_y Q^4(pY_0+q) \psi_B \\
&+\int \psi_B p Y_0' Z +\int (Q^5-Q_b^5) pY_0' \psi_B + 5\int Q^4(pY_0+q) pY_0'\psi_B
+\int \psi_B p Y_0' q^5 Q_b\\
& +\int \psi_B q_y \left[(Q_b+pY_0+q+\varepsilon)^5 -Q^5\right]
+\int \psi_B \varepsilon_y Z + 5\int \psi_B \varepsilon_y Q^4 (pY_0+q).
\end{align*}
Therefore,
\begin{eqnarray*}
f^{(i)}_{1,3}& = &   \left(\frac{x_s}{\lambda}-1\right) \bigg\{2\int Q'\left[L\varepsilon-\psi_B' \varepsilon_y + (1-\psi_B)\varepsilon_{yy}-\varepsilon(1-\varphi_{i,B})\right]\\
& + & 2 \int(Q_b-Q+\varepsilon+pY_0)_y\left[-\psi_B'\varepsilon_y-\psi_B\varepsilon_{yy}+\varepsilon\varphi_{i,B}\right]\\
& + & \frac 13 \int\psi_B'\left[(Q_b+pY_0+q+\varepsilon)^6-Q_b^6-6Q_b^5\varepsilon-6Q^5(pY_0+q)
-6 Q_b q^5\right]\\
& + & 2  \int\varepsilon\psi_B(Q_b^5-Q^5)_y+ 10    \int \psi_B (Q_b-Q)_y Q^4 (pY_0+q)\\
& + & 2   \int \psi_B(Q^5-Q_b^5) pY_0' +10 \int Q^4 (pY_0+q) pY_0' \psi_B
+2 \int \psi_B pY_0' q^5 Q_b\\
& + & 2    \int \psi_Bq_y \left[ (Q_b+pY_0+q+\varepsilon)^5-Q^5-5Q_b q^4\right] +10\int \psi_B \varepsilon_y Q^4(pY_0+q)\bigg\}.
\end{eqnarray*}
The first term is treated using the cancellation $L Q'=0$ and the orthogonality conditions $(\varepsilon, \Lambda Q)=(\varepsilon,Q)=0$, so that $(yQ',\varepsilon)=0$. Thus, by the definitions of $\varphi_{i,B}$ and $\psi_B$,
\begin{eqnarray*}
&&\left|2\left(\frac{x_s}{\lambda}-1\right) \int Q'\left[L\varepsilon-\psi_B' \varepsilon_y + (1-\psi_B)\varepsilon_{yy}-\varepsilon(1-\varphi_{i,B})\right]\right| 
\\
&&=\left|2\left(\frac{x_s}{\lambda}-1\right) \int Q'\left[-\psi_B' \varepsilon_y + (1-\psi_B)\varepsilon_{yy}-\varepsilon\left(1+\frac yB-\varphi_{i,B}\right)\right]\right| 
\\&& \lesssim   \left(\mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12}+ \frac 1{s^2}\right)e^{-\frac B {10}}\mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12} \leq   \frac 1 {500}  \frac {\mu_4} {B} \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}+\frac C{s^4}.
\end{eqnarray*}
Then, as before, integrating by parts, and using Cauchy-Schwarz inequality,
\begin{eqnarray*}
&&\left|2b \left(\frac{x_s}{\lambda}-1\right)\int (\chi_bP)_y\left[-\psi_B'\varepsilon_y-\psi_B\varepsilon_{yy}+\varepsilon\varphi_{i,B}\right]\right|\\\
&&\lesssim
\frac 1{s} \left(\mathcal N_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12} + \frac 1{s^2} \right)
B^{\frac 12} \mathcal N_{i,\rm loc}\leq \frac 1 {500}  \frac {\mu_4} {B} \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}+\frac C{s^4}.
\end{eqnarray*}
\begin{eqnarray*}
&&\left|2\left(\frac{x_s}{\lambda}-1\right)\int  \varepsilon_y\left[-\psi_B'\varepsilon_y-\psi_B\varepsilon_{yy}+\varepsilon\varphi_{i,B}\right]\right|
\\ &&\lesssim \delta(\alpha^*) \int   \left(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2\right)   \varphi'_{i,B}\leq \frac1{500} \frac  {\mu_4}{B}\int   \left(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2\right)   \varphi'_{i,B}+\frac C{s^4}.
\end{eqnarray*}
\begin{align*}
& \left|\frac{x_s}{\lambda}-1\right| \left| \int pY_0' \left[ - \psi_B' \varepsilon_y
- \psi_B \varepsilon_{yy} + \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B}\right]\right|\\
& \lesssim \left(\mathcal N_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12} + \frac 1{s^2} \right)
\frac 1s \mathcal N_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12} 
\leq \frac1{500} \frac  {\mu_4}{B}\int   \left(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2\right)   \varphi'_{i,B}+\frac C{s^4}.
\end{align*}
 In conclusion for $f^{(i)}_{1,3}$, on gets
$$
|f^{(i)}_{1,3}| \leq \frac1{50} \frac  {\mu_4}{B}\int   \left(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2\right)   \varphi'_{i,B}+ \frac C{s^4},
$$
for $B$ large enough and $\alpha^*$ small enough, $s_0$ large enough.

\medskip

\underline{{\em Term $f^{(i)}_{1,4}$}}:  Recall
$$
f^{(i)}_{1,4} = - 2{b}_{s}  \int   \left(\chi_b   + \gamma   y (\chi_b)_y\right) P  \left(   - \psi_B\varepsilon_{yy} -\psi_B'\varepsilon_y+ \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B}-\psi_BZ   \right).$$
 We estimate after   integrations by parts
 \begin{eqnarray*}
 \left| \int   \left(\chi_b   + \gamma   y (\chi_b)_y\right) P  \left(   - \psi_B\varepsilon_{y } \right)_y\right|&\lesssim& \int|\varepsilon|\left|(\psi_B (  (\chi_b   + \gamma   y (\chi_b)_y) P)_y)_y\right| \\
 & \lesssim & B^{\frac 12}\mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12}.
 \end{eqnarray*}
 $$\left|\int   \left(\chi_b   + \gamma   y (\chi_b)_y\right) P \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B}\right|\lesssim B^{\frac 12}\mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12}.$$ The estimate of the nonlinear term follows from   {\rm (\ref{nonlinearsobolev})} and $\psi\leq (\varphi'_i)^2$ for $y<-\frac 12$:
 \begin{eqnarray*}
 && \left|\int   \left(\chi_b   + \gamma   y (\chi_b)_y\right) P \psi_BZ\right|  \lesssim  \int\psi_B((|Q_b|^4|+p^4+q^4) \varepsilon|+|\varepsilon|^5
 +b^2 + p^2 + q^2)\\
 && \lesssim    B^{\frac 12}\left( \int (|\varepsilon|^2+ |\varepsilon|^6) \psi_B\right)^{\frac 12} +\frac 1{s^2}  \lesssim B^{\frac 12}
\left(\int   \left(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2\right)   \varphi'_{i,B} \right)^{\frac 12} 
+\frac 1{s^2}  .
 \end{eqnarray*} 
Together with \eqref{BSparam}, these estimates yield the bound:
$$|f_{1,4}| 
\leq  \frac 1 {500}  \frac {\mu_4} {B } 
 \int   \left(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2\right)   \varphi'_{i,B}   +\frac C{s^4}.$$
 
 \medskip
 
\underline{{\em Term $f^{(i)}_{1,5}$}}:  Recall:
$$
f^{(i)}_{1,5}=    
 2  \int  \Psi_b    \left(   -(\psi_B\varepsilon_{y})_y  + \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B Z   \right).
$$
We now rely on \eqref{BSbsps} to estimate by integration by parts and Cauchy-Schwarz's inequality,
$$
\left|  \int  (\Psi_b)_y    \psi_B\varepsilon_{y}\right| \lesssim    B^{\frac 12}  b^2 \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac12} \leq  \frac 1 {500}  \frac {\mu_4} {B} \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc} +\frac C{s^4}.
$$
By \eqref{eq:202}  and   the exponential decay of $\varphi_{i,B}$ in the left,
$$\left|  \int  \Psi_b \varphi_{i,B}\varepsilon\right|\lesssim \left( b^2 B^{\frac 12}+ e^{-\frac 1{2 |b|^{\gamma}}}\right)|b|^{1+\gamma}\mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac12}\leq  \frac 1 {500}  \frac {\mu_4} {B } \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc} +C|b|^{4}.$$ For the nonlinear term, similarly and using \eqref{nonlinearsobolev},
\begin{eqnarray*}
 \left| \int  \Psi_b   \psi_B Z   \right|  \leq  \frac 1 {500}  \frac {\mu_4} {B} \int   \left(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2\right)   \varphi'_{i,B}  +\frac C{s^4}.
\end{eqnarray*}
The collection of above estimates yields the bound:
$$
| f^{(i)}_{1,5}| \leq \frac 1 {100}  \frac {\mu_4} {B} \int   \left(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2\right)   \varphi'_{i,B}+\frac C{s^4}.$$
\medskip
 
\underline{{\em Term $f^{(i)}_{1,6}$}}: Recall that this term writes
\begin{align*}
\left| \int \left( -p_s Y_0 + (5Q^4 (p-q))_y + \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} p\Lambda Y_0\right)
\left( - (\psi_B \varepsilon_y)_y + \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B} - \psi_B Z\right) \right|
\end{align*} 
By \eqref{BSbsps}, \eqref{cl.2}, \eqref{BSparam},
\begin{align*}
& \left|  \left( -p_s Y_0 + (5Q^4 (p-q))_y + \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} p\Lambda Y_0\right)  \right|
+\left|  \left( -p_s Y_0 + (5Q^4 (p-q))_y + \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} p\Lambda Y_0\right)_y  \right|
\\ & \lesssim e^{-\frac {|y|}{2}} \left( \frac 1{s^2} + \int \varepsilon^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{2}} \right), 
\end{align*}
and thus
$$
| f^{(i)}_{1,6}| \lesssim \delta(\alpha^*) \int \varepsilon^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{2} } 
+\frac 1{s^4}.
$$

\medskip
nodes.statement_short: Bound each part of f_1 to prove (re1).

nodes.name: Expansion of f_1
nodes.statement:
{\bf step 3} Control of $f_1^{(i)}$. Proof of \eqref{re1}. 
 We compute 
$ f_{1}^{(i)} $
using \eqref{eqebis}
\begin{align*}
  \rm f_{1}^{(i)}& = 2 \int   \left(  -\varepsilon_{yy} {+} \varepsilon  {-}Z  \right)_y \left(-(\psi_B\varepsilon_y)_y{+}\varepsilon\varphi_{i,B}{-}\psi_BZ \right) 
\\ & +2\left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right) \int {\Lambda} Q_b  \left( - (\psi_B\varepsilon_y)_y + \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B Z   \right)
\\ &   + 2 \left(\frac { x_{{s}}}{\lambda} -1\right) \int (Q_b  + \varepsilon+pY_0)_y
 \left( -(\psi_B \varepsilon_y)_y + \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B}-\psi_BZ  \right)
 \\ & + 2 \int  \Phi_{{b}}  \left( -(\psi_B \varepsilon_y)_y + \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B}-\psi_BZ   \right)
\\ & + 2 \int  \Psi_{{b}}   \left( -(\psi_B \varepsilon_y)_y + \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B}-\psi_BZ  \right) \\
& + \int \left(-p_sY_0 +(5Q^4(p-q))_y + \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} p \Lambda Y_0\right) \left( -(\psi_B \varepsilon_y)_y + \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B}-\psi_BZ  \right) 
\\ & = {{\rm f}^{(i)}_{1,1}}+ {{\rm f}^{(i)}_{1,2}}+{{\rm f}^{(i)}_{1,3}}+{{\rm f}^{(i)}_{1,4}}+{{\rm f}^{(i)}_{1,5}}+{{\rm f}^{(i)}_{1,6}}.
\end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Expand f_1 into f_{1,1}..f_{1,6}.

nodes.name: Term f_11
nodes.statement:
\underline{{\em Term $f^{(i)}_{1,1}$}}:  We first integrate by parts  
\begin{eqnarray*}
f^{(i)}_{1,1}& = &  2 \int\left[  -\varepsilon_{yy} + \varepsilon  -Z  \right]_y\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon  -Z\right] \psi_B \\
& + & 2\int\left[  -\varepsilon_{yy} + \varepsilon  -Z\right]_y\left(-\psi_B'\varepsilon_y+\varepsilon(\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)\right). 
\end{eqnarray*}
We compute the various terms  :
\begin{align*} & 2\int\left[  -\varepsilon_{yy} + \varepsilon  -Z  \right]_y\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon  -Z\right]\psi_B =-\int\psi_B'\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon  -Z\right]^2\\
&  =-\int\psi_B'\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon \right]^2  - \int\psi_B'\left\{\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon  -Z\right]^2-\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+\varepsilon\right]^2\right\}\\
&   = -\left[\int\psi_B'(\varepsilon_{yy}^2+2\varepsilon_y^2)+\int\varepsilon^2(\psi_B'-\psi_B''')\right]\\
&  -\int\psi_B'\left\{\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon  -Z\right]^2-\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+\varepsilon\right]^2\right\}.
\end{align*}
Next after integration by parts:
\begin{eqnarray*}
& & 2 \int\left[  -\varepsilon_{yy} + \varepsilon\right]_y\left[-\psi_B'\varepsilon_y+\varepsilon(\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)\right]\\
&  &  =-2 \Big\{\int\psi_B'\varepsilon_{yy}^2+\int\varepsilon_y^2(\tfrac32\varphi_{i,B}'-\tfrac12\psi'_B-\tfrac12\psi_B''')\\&&+\int\varepsilon^2(\tfrac12(\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)'-\tfrac12(\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)''')\Big\},
\end{eqnarray*}

\begin{eqnarray*}
&-& 2 \int Z_y(\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)\varepsilon =
2 \int Z (\varphi_{i,B}'-\psi_B')\varepsilon + 2\int Z (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)\varepsilon_y\\
& = & 2 \int Z (\varphi_{i,B}'-\psi_B')\varepsilon - \frac 13\int(\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)'\\ &&\left\{[(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^6-(Q_b+pY_0+q)^6-6Q_b^5\varepsilon -6q^5 \varepsilon -30 Q^4(pY_0+q)\varepsilon  \right\}\\
& - & 2\int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)(Q_b)_y[(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5-(Q_b +pY_0+q)^5-5Q_b^4\varepsilon]\\
& + & 40 \int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B) Q' Q^3 (pY_0+q) \varepsilon\\
& - & 2 \int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)(p Y_0'+q_y) [(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5-(Q_b +pY_0+q)^5-5Q^4\varepsilon].
\end{eqnarray*}

We collect the above computations and obtain the following
\begin{align*}
& f^{(i)}_{1,1} = -\int\left[3\psi_B'\varepsilon_{yy}^2+(3\varphi_{i,B}'+\psi_B'-\psi_B''')\varepsilon_y^2+(\varphi_{i,B}'-\varphi_{i,B}''')\varepsilon^2\right]\\
& -\frac 13 \int \left[ (\varepsilon {+} Q_b {+}pY_0{+}q )^6{-}  {(Q_b{+}pY_0{+}q) ^6}  {-}6 Q_b ^5 \varepsilon {-} 6 q^5 \varepsilon{-} 30 Q^4(pY_0{+}q)\varepsilon{-}6Z \varepsilon \right](\varphi_{i,B}'{-}\psi_B')\\
& -   2\int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)(Q_b)_y[(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5-(Q_b +pY_0+q)^5-5Q_b^4\varepsilon]\\
& + 40 \int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B) Q' Q^3 (pY_0+q) \varepsilon\\
& -   2 \int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)(p  Y_0'+q_y) [(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5-(Q_b +pY_0+q)^5-5Q^4\varepsilon]\\
& +    2 \int Z_y \varepsilon_y \psi_B'  -  \int\psi_B'\left\{\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon  -Z \right]^2-\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+\varepsilon\right]^2\right\}\\
& =  (f^{(i)}_{1,1})^<+(f^{(i)}_{1,1})^{\sim}+(f^{(i)}_{1,1})^>
\end{align*}
where $(f^{(i)}_{1,1})^{<,\sim,>}$ respectively corresponds to integration on $y<-\frac B2$, $|y|\leq \frac B2$, $y>\frac B2$.

We recall
\begin{equation} \|\varepsilon \|_{L^\infty} \lesssim \|\varepsilon\|_{H^1} \lesssim  {\delta(\alpha^*)}  .
\end{equation}

 


$\bullet$ For the region $y<-B/2$, we rely on monotonicity type arguments and estimate using \eqref{defphi4}:
$$
\int_{y<-B/2} \varepsilon^2 |\varphi'''_{i,B}|\lesssim
  \frac 1 {B^2}  \int_{y<-B/2} \varepsilon^2 \varphi'_{i,B} \leq  \frac 1{100} \int_{y<-B/2} \varepsilon^2 \varphi'_{i,B},
$$
$$\int_{y<-B/2} \varepsilon_y^2|\psi'''_B|\lesssim
  \frac 1 {B^2}  \int_{y<-B/2} \varepsilon_y^2 \varphi'_{i,B} \leq  \frac 1{100} \int_{y<-B/2} \varepsilon_y^2 \varphi'_{i,B},$$
by choosing $B$ large enough.  
By \eqref{nonlinearsobolev} (for $B$ large and $\alpha^*$ small)
\begin{align*}
& \left| \int_{y<-B/2}  \left[ (\varepsilon {+} Q_b {+}pY_0{+}q )^6{-}  {(Q_b{+}pY_0{+}q) ^6}  {-}6 Q_b ^5 \varepsilon {-} 6 q^5 \varepsilon{-}30 Q^4(pY_0{+}q)\varepsilon{-} 6Z \varepsilon \right](\varphi_{i,B}'{-}\psi_B') \right|
\\ 
& \lesssim    
 \int_{y<-B/2} \left(\delta(\alpha^*)  + (|Q_b| ^4+|p|^4+|q|^4) \varepsilon^2
 +(|b|+|p|+|q|)^2 |\varepsilon| \right)\varphi'_{i,B} 
 \\& \lesssim  \left(\delta(\alpha^*)+\delta(s_0^{-1})+e^{-\frac B{10} }\right)\int_{y<-B/2}  \varphi_{i,B}' \varepsilon^2 
 +\frac 1{s^2} \left( \int_{y<-B/2}  \varepsilon^2   \varphi'_{i,B}\right)^{\frac 12}
 \\
& \leq    \frac 1{100} \int_{y<-B/2}  \varepsilon^2   \varphi'_{i,B}+\frac 1{s^4},
\end{align*}
where we have used from the definition of $q$ and \eqref{BSp}
$$
\left(\int q^4  \varphi'_{i,B}\right)^{\frac 12} \lesssim \frac 1{s^2}.
$$
Similarily for $\alpha^*$ small depending on $B$,
\begin{eqnarray*}
&& \bigg| \int_{y<-\frac{B}{2}}  (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)(Q_b)_y\left[(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5-(Q_b +pY_0+q)^5-5Q_b^4\varepsilon\right] \\ &&-   20 \int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B) Q' Q^3 (pY_0+q) \varepsilon 
\bigg|\\
&& \lesssim   B \int_{y<-\frac B2}\left(|\varepsilon|^5+\varepsilon^2(|Q_b|^3+|p|^3+|q|^3)\right)(|Q_y|+|b||(P\chi_b)'|)\varphi_{i,B}' \\
&&+B \int |\varepsilon|\left(  |p|^2+|q|^2\right)
(|Q_y|+|b||(P\chi_b)'| )\varphi_{i,B}'\\
&&+B \int |\varepsilon|  (|p|+|q|)   
\left| (Q_b)_y Q_b^3 - Q'Q^3\right|\varphi_{i,B}'\\&&\leq \frac 1{100} \int_{y<-B/2}  (\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2)  \varphi'_{i,B}+\frac 1{s^4}.
\end{eqnarray*}
The next term in $(f^{(i)}_{1,1})^<$ is
$$- 2\int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)(p Y_0'+q_y) [(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5-(Q_b +pY_0+q)^5-5Q^4\varepsilon].$$
To estimate it, we note the following
\begin{align*}
&\left|(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5-(Q_b +pY_0+q)^5-5Q^4\varepsilon \right|\\
& \lesssim   |\varepsilon|^5 +|\varepsilon|^2+|\varepsilon| (|b|+|p|+|q|).
\end{align*}
Now, using
\begin{equation} \int  |p|  \varphi_{i,B} dy \lesssim \frac 1{s}, 
\quad \int  |q_y|    \varphi_{i,B} dy \lesssim \frac 1{s^2},  \end{equation}
we obtain proceeding as before
\begin{align*}
&\left|\int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)(p  Y_0'+q_y) [(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5-(Q_b +pY_0+q)^5-5Q^4\varepsilon]
\right|\\ &\lesssim     \frac 1{100} \int_{y<-B/2} (\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2)  \varphi'_{i,B}+\frac 1{s^4}.
\end{align*}
  We further estimate using {\rm (\ref{nonlinearsobolev})} and   $(\varphi'_i)^2\lesssim \psi'\lesssim (\varphi'_i)^2$ for $y<-\frac 12$:
\begin{eqnarray*}
&& \left|\int Z_y \varepsilon_y \psi_b'\right| \\&& \lesssim 
\left|\int_{y<-\frac B2}\psi_B'\varepsilon_y\left\{(Q_b)_y[(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^4-Q_b^4]-Q'Q^3(pY_0+q)\right\} \right|\\
&&+\left|\int_{y<-\frac B2}\psi_B'\varepsilon_y   (pY_0'+q_y) ((Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^4-Q^4) \right| + \left| \int q_y q^4 \varepsilon\psi_B'\right|\\
&& +\left| \int_{y<-\frac B2}\psi_B'\varepsilon_y^2 (Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^4\right|\\
&& \lesssim  \left( e^{- \frac 12 B} +\delta(s_0^{-1}) +\delta(\alpha^*)\right) \int_{y<-\frac B2}\varphi'_{i,B}(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2) 
+\frac 1{s^4}\\
&& \leq 
 \frac 1{100}  \int_{y<-B/2}  (\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2)  \varphi'_{i,B}+\frac C{s^4}.
\end{eqnarray*}

 
The remaining nonlinear term is estimated using the local $H^2$ control provided by localization
(see more details in \cite{MMR1})
\begin{eqnarray*}
& & \left|\int_{y<-\frac B2}\psi_B'\left\{\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon  -Z\right]^2-\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+\varepsilon\right]^2\right\}\right|
\\
&=&   \left|\int_{y<-\frac B2}\psi_B' \left(-2\varepsilon_{yy}+ 2\varepsilon  -Z\right)  Z  \right|\\
& \leq & \frac{1}{100}\int_{y<-\frac B2}\psi_{B}'(|\varepsilon_{yy}|^2+|\varepsilon|^2)+C\int_{y<-\frac B2}(\varphi'_{i,B})^2Z^2\\
& \leq &  \frac 1{100} \int_{y<-B/2} \left[ \varepsilon_{yy}^2\psi_B'+(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2)  \varphi'_{i,B}\right]
+\frac 1{s^4}.
\end{eqnarray*}

$\bullet$ In the region $y>\frac B2$, we have $\psi_B(y)=1$, so that several terms cancel in $f_{1,1}^{(i)}$. For the remainding terms, we argue as before.
We rely on \eqref{defphi4} to estimate:
$$\int_{y>B/2} \varepsilon^2 |\varphi'''_{i,B}|\lesssim
  \frac 1 {B^2}  \int_{y>B/2} \varepsilon^2 \varphi'_{i,B} \leq  \frac 1{100} \int_{y>B/2} \varepsilon^2 \varphi'_{i,B},$$ and we use the exponential localization of $Q_b$ to the right and \eqref{nonlinearsobolev},   to control:  
  \begin{align*}
& \left| \int_{y>B/2} \left(\frac {(\varepsilon {+} Q_b {+}pY_0{+}q )^6} 6
-\frac {(Q_b{+}pY_0{+}q)^6} 6 -Q_b^5 \varepsilon - 5 Q^4 (pY_0{+}q) - Z \varepsilon  \right)  \varphi_{i,B}' \right|
\\ 
&   \lesssim 
 \int_{y>B/2} \left(\varepsilon^6  + \left(|Q_b| ^4 +p^4 +q^4 \right)\varepsilon^2
 + (|b|+|q|+|p|)^2 |\varepsilon|\right)\varphi_{i,B}' \\
 & \lesssim  (\delta(\alpha^*)+\delta(s_0^{-1})+e^{-\frac B{10}})\int_{y>B/2}  \varepsilon^2   \varphi_{i,B}' + \frac 1{s^4}\\
& \leq  \frac 1{100} \int_{y>B/2}  \varepsilon^2   \varphi'_{i,B}
+\frac C{s^4},
\end{align*}
\begin{align*}
& \Bigg| \int_{y>B/2} \left[(\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0+q )^5 -(Q_b+pY_0+q) ^5- 5 Q_b ^4 \varepsilon\right](Q_b )_y (\psi_B-\varphi_{i,B}) \\
&-20 \int_{y>B/2}  Q'Q^3 (pY_0+q) \varepsilon (\psi_B-\varphi_{i,B})\Bigg|\\
&  \leq \frac 1{100} \int_{y>B/2}   \varepsilon^2   \varphi'_{i,B} +\frac C{s^4}.
\end{align*}
Since $Y_0\in \mathcal{Y}$, we   argue similarly to obtain
\begin{align*}
&\left| \int (\psi_B-\varphi_{i,B}) pY_0' 
\left[ (Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5Q^4 \varepsilon\right]\right| \\
&\leq \frac 1{100} \int_{y>B/2}   \varepsilon^2   \varphi'_{i,B} +\frac C{s^4}.
\end{align*}
Next, we have from \eqref{BSqy},
\begin{align*}
&\left| \int (\varphi_{i,B} - \psi_B) q_y \left[ (Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5Q^4 \varepsilon\right]\right| \\
& 
 \leq \frac 1{100} \int_{y>B/2}   \varepsilon^2   \varphi'_{i,B} +\frac C{s^4}.
\end{align*}
Also,
\begin{align*}
\left| \int Z_y \varepsilon_y \psi_B'\right| =
\left| \int Z (\varepsilon_{yy} \psi_B' + \varepsilon_y \psi_B'')\right|
\leq \frac 1{100} \int (\varepsilon_{yy}^2 + \varepsilon_y^2 + \varepsilon^2) \psi_B' +\frac C{s^4}.
\end{align*}

$\bullet$ In the   region $|y|<B/2$, $\varphi_{i,B}(s,y) = 1+ y/B$ and $\psi_B(y)=1$. In particular, $\varphi_{i,B}'''=\psi_B'=0$ in this region, and we obtain:
\begin{align*}
(f^{(i)}_{1,1})^{\sim}  
&    = - \frac {1}{B} \int_{|y|<B/2}  \Big\{ 3 \varepsilon_y^2 + \varepsilon^2  \\
  &   + \frac 13  \left( (\varepsilon + Q_b +pY_0+q)^6 
-(Q_b+pY_0+q)^6  - 6 Q_b^5 \varepsilon -30 Q^4(pY_0+q)\varepsilon
 -6 Z\varepsilon \right) 
  \\
  &  + 2\left( (\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0+q )^5 -(Q_b+pY_0+q)^5- 5 Q_b ^4 \varepsilon\right) y (Q_b )_y  
\\
& -40 yQ'Q^3 (pY_0+q) \varepsilon \\
& + 2 y(p Y_0'+q_y)\left((\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0+q )^5 -(Q_b+pY_0+q) ^5- 5 Q_b ^4 \varepsilon\right)\Big\} \\
&    = - \frac {1}   { B} \int_{|y|<B/2}   \left\{ 3 \varepsilon_y^2 + \varepsilon^2 - 5 Q^4 \varepsilon^2 + 20 y Q' Q^3 \varepsilon^2\right\} + R_{\rm Vir}(\varepsilon),
\end{align*}
where
\begin{align*}
R_{\rm Vir}(\varepsilon) = - \frac {1}   { B} & \int_{|y|<B/2} \Bigg\{
\frac 13 \bigg( (\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0 + q)^6 - (Q_b+pY_0+q)^6 - 6Q_b^5 \varepsilon\\ &
-30 Q^4 (pY_0+q)\varepsilon - 6Z\varepsilon  - 15 Q^4 \varepsilon^2 \bigg)\\
& +2 \left( (\varepsilon+Q_b+ pY_0 + q)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0 + q)^5 - 5 Q_b^4 \varepsilon\right) y (Q_b)_y
\\ &- 20 y Q' Q^3 (pY_0+q) \varepsilon - 10 y Q' Q^3 \varepsilon^2 \\
& +2 y (pY_0'+q_y) \left( (\varepsilon +Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0 +q)^5 - 5Q_b^4 \varepsilon\right)\Bigg\} 
\end{align*}
As before, we estimate
\begin{align*}
|R_{\rm Vir}(\varepsilon)|&\lesssim 
\int_{|y|<B} \varepsilon^2 \left( \delta(\alpha^*) + |b|+ |p|+|q|\right)
+ \int_{|y|<B} |\varepsilon| (p^2+ q^2 + b^2)
\\&\lesssim  \frac 1{100}\int_{|y|<B/2} (\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2) +\frac 1{s^4},
\end{align*}

We now recall from \cite{MMR1} the following coercivity result.

\begin{lemma}[Localized viriel estimate] There exists $B_{0}>100$ and $\mu_{3}>0$ such that
if $B\geq B_{0}$, then
$$
\int_{|y|<B/2}   \left( 3 \varepsilon_y^2 + \varepsilon^2 - 5 Q^4 \varepsilon^2 + 20 y Q' Q^3 \varepsilon^2\right) \geq \mu_{3} \int_{|y|<B/2}  \left(  \varepsilon_y^2 + \varepsilon^2 \right)
-  \frac 1 B \int \varepsilon^2 e^{-\frac{|y|}{2}}.
$$
\end{lemma}
 
Thus for $\alpha^*$ small enough:
$$(f^{(i)}_{1,1})^\sim   \leq  - \frac { \mu_{3}}   {2 B} \int_{|y|<B/2}  \left(  \varepsilon_y^2 + \varepsilon^2 \right) + \frac 1 {B^2} \int \varepsilon^2 e^{-\frac{|y|}{2}}+\frac 1{s^4}.$$ 
The collection of above estimates yields the bound:
\begin{equation} f^{(i)}_{1,1}  \leq  - \frac  {\mu_4} B    \int\left[\psi'_B\varepsilon_{yy}^2+\varphi'_{i,B}(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2)\right] + \frac C{s^4},
    \end{equation}
    for some universal $\mu_4>0$ independent of $B$.
    
    \medskip
nodes.statement_short: Region-wise estimates and virial coercivity give (eq:cf11).

nodes.name: Integration by parts
nodes.statement:
\underline{{\em Term $f^{(i)}_{1,1}$}}:  We first integrate by parts  
\begin{eqnarray*}
f^{(i)}_{1,1}& = &  2 \int\left[  -\varepsilon_{yy} + \varepsilon  -Z  \right]_y\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon  -Z\right] \psi_B \\
& + & 2\int\left[  -\varepsilon_{yy} + \varepsilon  -Z\right]_y\left(-\psi_B'\varepsilon_y+\varepsilon(\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)\right). 
\end{eqnarray*}
We compute the various terms  :
\begin{align*} & 2\int\left[  -\varepsilon_{yy} + \varepsilon  -Z  \right]_y\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon  -Z\right]\psi_B =-\int\psi_B'\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon  -Z\right]^2\\
&  =-\int\psi_B'\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon \right]^2  - \int\psi_B'\left\{\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon  -Z\right]^2-\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+\varepsilon\right]^2\right\}\\
&   = -\left[\int\psi_B'(\varepsilon_{yy}^2+2\varepsilon_y^2)+\int\varepsilon^2(\psi_B'-\psi_B''')\right]\\
&  -\int\psi_B'\left\{\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon  -Z\right]^2-\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+\varepsilon\right]^2\right\}.
\end{align*}
Next after integration by parts:
\begin{eqnarray*}
& & 2 \int\left[  -\varepsilon_{yy} + \varepsilon\right]_y\left[-\psi_B'\varepsilon_y+\varepsilon(\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)\right]\\
&  &  =-2 \Big\{\int\psi_B'\varepsilon_{yy}^2+\int\varepsilon_y^2(\tfrac32\varphi_{i,B}'-\tfrac12\psi'_B-\tfrac12\psi_B''')\\&&+\int\varepsilon^2(\tfrac12(\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)'-\tfrac12(\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)''')\Big\},
\end{eqnarray*}

\begin{eqnarray*}
&-& 2 \int Z_y(\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)\varepsilon =
2 \int Z (\varphi_{i,B}'-\psi_B')\varepsilon + 2\int Z (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)\varepsilon_y\\
& = & 2 \int Z (\varphi_{i,B}'-\psi_B')\varepsilon - \frac 13\int(\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)'\\ &&\left\{[(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^6-(Q_b+pY_0+q)^6-6Q_b^5\varepsilon -6q^5 \varepsilon -30 Q^4(pY_0+q)\varepsilon  \right\}\\
& - & 2\int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)(Q_b)_y[(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5-(Q_b +pY_0+q)^5-5Q_b^4\varepsilon]\\
& + & 40 \int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B) Q' Q^3 (pY_0+q) \varepsilon\\
& - & 2 \int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)(p Y_0'+q_y) [(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5-(Q_b +pY_0+q)^5-5Q^4\varepsilon].
\end{eqnarray*}

We collect the above computations and obtain the following
\begin{align*}
& f^{(i)}_{1,1} = -\int\left[3\psi_B'\varepsilon_{yy}^2+(3\varphi_{i,B}'+\psi_B'-\psi_B''')\varepsilon_y^2+(\varphi_{i,B}'-\varphi_{i,B}''')\varepsilon^2\right]\\
& -\frac 13 \int \left[ (\varepsilon {+} Q_b {+}pY_0{+}q )^6{-}  {(Q_b{+}pY_0{+}q) ^6}  {-}6 Q_b ^5 \varepsilon {-} 6 q^5 \varepsilon{-} 30 Q^4(pY_0{+}q)\varepsilon{-}6Z \varepsilon \right](\varphi_{i,B}'{-}\psi_B')\\
& -   2\int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)(Q_b)_y[(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5-(Q_b +pY_0+q)^5-5Q_b^4\varepsilon]\\
& + 40 \int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B) Q' Q^3 (pY_0+q) \varepsilon\\
& -   2 \int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)(p  Y_0'+q_y) [(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5-(Q_b +pY_0+q)^5-5Q^4\varepsilon]\\
& +    2 \int Z_y \varepsilon_y \psi_B'  -  \int\psi_B'\left\{\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon  -Z \right]^2-\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+\varepsilon\right]^2\right\}\\
& =  (f^{(i)}_{1,1})^<+(f^{(i)}_{1,1})^{\sim}+(f^{(i)}_{1,1})^>
\end{align*}
where $(f^{(i)}_{1,1})^{<,\sim,>}$ respectively corresponds to integration on $y<-\frac B2$, $|y|\leq \frac B2$, $y>\frac B2$.

nodes.name: Left region
nodes.statement:

$$

 +\frac 1{s^2} \left( \int_{y<-B/2}  \varepsilon^2   \varphi'_{i,B}\right)^{\frac 12}
 \\

\end{align*}

$$
\left(\int q^4  \varphi'_{i,B}\right)^{\frac 12} \lesssim \frac 1{s^2}.
$$
