\begin{eqnarray*}
&& \bigg| \int_{y<-\frac{B}{2}}  (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)(Q_b)_y\left[(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5-(Q_b +pY_0+q)^5-5Q_b^4\varepsilon\right] \\ &&-   20 \int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B) Q' Q^3 (pY_0+q) \varepsilon 
\bigg|\\
&& \lesssim   B \int_{y<-\frac B2}\left(|\varepsilon|^5+\varepsilon^2(|Q_b|^3+|p|^3+|q|^3)\right)(|Q_y|+|b||(P\chi_b)'|)\varphi_{i,B}' \\
&&+B \int |\varepsilon|\left(  |p|^2+|q|^2\right)
(|Q_y|+|b||(P\chi_b)'| )\varphi_{i,B}'\\
&&+B \int |\varepsilon|  (|p|+|q|)   
\left| (Q_b)_y Q_b^3 - Q'Q^3\right|\varphi_{i,B}'\\&&\leq \frac 1{100} \int_{y<-B/2}  (\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2)  \varphi'_{i,B}+\frac 1{s^4}.
\end{eqnarray*}
The next term in $(f^{(i)}_{1,1})^<$ is
$$- 2\int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)(p Y_0'+q_y) [(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5-(Q_b +pY_0+q)^5-5Q^4\varepsilon].$$
To estimate it, we note the following
\begin{align*}
&\left|(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5-(Q_b +pY_0+q)^5-5Q^4\varepsilon \right|\\
& \lesssim   |\varepsilon|^5 +|\varepsilon|^2+|\varepsilon| (|b|+|p|+|q|).
\end{align*}
Now, using
\begin{equation} \int  |p|  \varphi_{i,B} dy \lesssim \frac 1{s}, 
\quad \int  |q_y|    \varphi_{i,B} dy \lesssim \frac 1{s^2},  \end{equation}
we obtain proceeding as before
\begin{align*}
&\left|\int (\varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B)(p  Y_0'+q_y) [(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5-(Q_b +pY_0+q)^5-5Q^4\varepsilon]
\right|\\ &\lesssim     \frac 1{100} \int_{y<-B/2} (\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2)  \varphi'_{i,B}+\frac 1{s^4}.
\end{align*}
  We further estimate using {\rm (\ref{nonlinearsobolev})} and   $(\varphi'_i)^2\lesssim \psi'\lesssim (\varphi'_i)^2$ for $y<-\frac 12$:
\begin{eqnarray*}
&& \left|\int Z_y \varepsilon_y \psi_b'\right| \\&& \lesssim 
\left|\int_{y<-\frac B2}\psi_B'\varepsilon_y\left\{(Q_b)_y[(Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^4-Q_b^4]-Q'Q^3(pY_0+q)\right\} \right|\\
&&+\left|\int_{y<-\frac B2}\psi_B'\varepsilon_y   (pY_0'+q_y) ((Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^4-Q^4) \right| + \left| \int q_y q^4 \varepsilon\psi_B'\right|\\
&& +\left| \int_{y<-\frac B2}\psi_B'\varepsilon_y^2 (Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^4\right|\\
&& \lesssim  \left( e^{- \frac 12 B} +\delta(s_0^{-1}) +\delta(\alpha^*)\right) \int_{y<-\frac B2}\varphi'_{i,B}(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2) 
+\frac 1{s^4}\\
&& \leq 
 \frac 1{100}  \int_{y<-B/2}  (\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2)  \varphi'_{i,B}+\frac C{s^4}.
\end{eqnarray*}

 
The remaining nonlinear term is estimated using the local $H^2$ control provided by localization
(see more details in \cite{MMR1})
\begin{eqnarray*}
& & \left|\int_{y<-\frac B2}\psi_B'\left\{\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+ \varepsilon  -Z\right]^2-\left[-\varepsilon_{yy}+\varepsilon\right]^2\right\}\right|
\\
&=&   \left|\int_{y<-\frac B2}\psi_B' \left(-2\varepsilon_{yy}+ 2\varepsilon  -Z\right)  Z  \right|\\
& \leq & \frac{1}{100}\int_{y<-\frac B2}\psi_{B}'(|\varepsilon_{yy}|^2+|\varepsilon|^2)+C\int_{y<-\frac B2}(\varphi'_{i,B})^2Z^2\\
& \leq &  \frac 1{100} \int_{y<-B/2} \left[ \varepsilon_{yy}^2\psi_B'+(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2)  \varphi'_{i,B}\right]
+\frac 1{s^4}.
\end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: Monotonicity estimates for y<-B/2.

nodes.name: Right region
nodes.statement:
$\bullet$ In the region $y>\frac B2$, we have $\psi_B(y)=1$, so that several terms cancel in $f_{1,1}^{(i)}$. For the remainding terms, we argue as before.
We rely on \eqref{defphi4} to estimate:
$$\int_{y>B/2} \varepsilon^2 |\varphi'''_{i,B}|\lesssim
  \frac 1 {B^2}  \int_{y>B/2} \varepsilon^2 \varphi'_{i,B} \leq  \frac 1{100} \int_{y>B/2} \varepsilon^2 \varphi'_{i,B},$$ and we use the exponential localization of $Q_b$ to the right and \eqref{nonlinearsobolev},   to control:  
  \begin{align*}
& \left| \int_{y>B/2} \left(\frac {(\varepsilon {+} Q_b {+}pY_0{+}q )^6} 6
-\frac {(Q_b{+}pY_0{+}q)^6} 6 -Q_b^5 \varepsilon - 5 Q^4 (pY_0{+}q) - Z \varepsilon  \right)  \varphi_{i,B}' \right|
\\ 
&   \lesssim 
 \int_{y>B/2} \left(\varepsilon^6  + \left(|Q_b| ^4 +p^4 +q^4 \right)\varepsilon^2
 + (|b|+|q|+|p|)^2 |\varepsilon|\right)\varphi_{i,B}' \\
 & \lesssim  (\delta(\alpha^*)+\delta(s_0^{-1})+e^{-\frac B{10}})\int_{y>B/2}  \varepsilon^2   \varphi_{i,B}' + \frac 1{s^4}\\
& \leq  \frac 1{100} \int_{y>B/2}  \varepsilon^2   \varphi'_{i,B}
+\frac C{s^4},
\end{align*}
\begin{align*}
& \Bigg| \int_{y>B/2} \left[(\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0+q )^5 -(Q_b+pY_0+q) ^5- 5 Q_b ^4 \varepsilon\right](Q_b )_y (\psi_B-\varphi_{i,B}) \\
&-20 \int_{y>B/2}  Q'Q^3 (pY_0+q) \varepsilon (\psi_B-\varphi_{i,B})\Bigg|\\
&  \leq \frac 1{100} \int_{y>B/2}   \varepsilon^2   \varphi'_{i,B} +\frac C{s^4}.
\end{align*}
Since $Y_0\in \mathcal{Y}$, we   argue similarly to obtain
\begin{align*}
&\left| \int (\psi_B-\varphi_{i,B}) pY_0' 
\left[ (Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5Q^4 \varepsilon\right]\right| \\
&\leq \frac 1{100} \int_{y>B/2}   \varepsilon^2   \varphi'_{i,B} +\frac C{s^4}.
\end{align*}
Next, we have from \eqref{BSqy},
\begin{align*}
&\left| \int (\varphi_{i,B} - \psi_B) q_y \left[ (Q_b+\varepsilon+pY_0+q)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5Q^4 \varepsilon\right]\right| \\
& 
 \leq \frac 1{100} \int_{y>B/2}   \varepsilon^2   \varphi'_{i,B} +\frac C{s^4}.
\end{align*}
Also,
\begin{align*}
\left| \int Z_y \varepsilon_y \psi_B'\right| =
\left| \int Z (\varepsilon_{yy} \psi_B' + \varepsilon_y \psi_B'')\right|
\leq \frac 1{100} \int (\varepsilon_{yy}^2 + \varepsilon_y^2 + \varepsilon^2) \psi_B' +\frac C{s^4}.
\end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Estimates for y>B/2.

nodes.name: Middle region
nodes.statement_short: Virial quadratic form in |y|<B/2.

nodes.name: Lemma B.1
nodes.statement:
We now recall from \cite{MMR1} the following coercivity result.

\begin{lemma}[Localized viriel estimate] There exists $B_{0}>100$ and $\mu_{3}>0$ such that
if $B\geq B_{0}$, then
$$
\int_{|y|<B/2}   \left( 3 \varepsilon_y^2 + \varepsilon^2 - 5 Q^4 \varepsilon^2 + 20 y Q' Q^3 \varepsilon^2\right) \geq \mu_{3} \int_{|y|<B/2}  \left(  \varepsilon_y^2 + \varepsilon^2 \right)
-  \frac 1 B \int \varepsilon^2 e^{-\frac{|y|}{2}}.
$$
\end{lemma}
nodes.statement_short: Recall the localized virial lemma.

nodes.name: Bound (eq:cf11)
nodes.statement:
Thus for $\alpha^*$ small enough:
$$(f^{(i)}_{1,1})^\sim   \leq  - \frac { \mu_{3}}   {2 B} \int_{|y|<B/2}  \left(  \varepsilon_y^2 + \varepsilon^2 \right) + \frac 1 {B^2} \int \varepsilon^2 e^{-\frac{|y|}{2}}+\frac 1{s^4}.$$ 
The collection of above estimates yields the bound:
\begin{equation} f^{(i)}_{1,1}  \leq  - \frac  {\mu_4} B    \int\left[\psi'_B\varepsilon_{yy}^2+\varphi'_{i,B}(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2)\right] + \frac C{s^4},
    \end{equation}
    for some universal $\mu_4>0$ independent of $B$.
    
    \medskip
nodes.statement_short: Conclude (eq:cf11).

nodes.name: Term f_12
nodes.statement:
\underline{{\em Term $f^{(i)}_{1,2}$}}:  We decompose  $f_{1,2}$ in a suitable way:
\begin{align*}
f^{(i)}_{1,2} & =  2 \left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right)  \int {\Lambda} Q  (L \varepsilon) -2\left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right)\int\varepsilon (1-\varphi_{i,B})\Lambda Q
\\
&+ 2b \left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right)  \int {\Lambda} ( \chi_b P)  \left(-(\psi_B\varepsilon_y)_{y}  + \varepsilon\varphi_{i,B} - \psi_B Z\right)\\
& + 2 \left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right)  \int {\Lambda} Q      \left(-(\psi_B)_y\varepsilon_y
-(1-\psi_B)\varepsilon_{yy}+(1-\psi_B)Z\right) \\&
+ 2\left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right)  \int {\Lambda} Q  (Z-5Q^4\varepsilon)
\end{align*}
Observe from {\rm (\ref{ortho1})}: $$\int \Lambda Q (L\varepsilon)=(\varepsilon,L\Lambda Q)=-2(\varepsilon,Q)=0.$$  We now use the orthogonality conditions $( \varepsilon, y {\Lambda} Q)=0$ and the definition of $\varphi_{i,B}$ to estimate:
$$
	\left| \int {\Lambda} Q \varepsilon (1-\varphi_{i,B}) \right| = \left| \int {\Lambda} Q \varepsilon \left(1-\varphi_{i,B}+ \frac yB\right)\right|
	\lesssim e^{- \frac B 8 } \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12}  ,
$$
so that  for $B$ large enough:
\begin{align*}
  \left|  \left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right)  \int {\Lambda} Q\varepsilon (1-\varphi_{i,B}) \right| 
&\lesssim \left( \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12}  +\frac 1{s^2} \right) e^{- \frac B 8}  \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12}  
\\ &
\leq 
 \frac 1 {500}  \frac {\mu_4} {B} \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc} 
+\frac C{s^4}.
\end{align*}
For the next term in $f_{1,2}^{(i)}$, we first integrate by parts to remove all derivatives on $\varepsilon$.
Then, by   the properties of $\varphi_{i,B}$, $\psi_B$, $P$  and $\chi_b$ \eqref{eq:210}, we obtain
for $\alpha^*$ small,
 \begin{eqnarray*}
&&\left| 2b \left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right)  \int {\Lambda} ( \chi_b P)  \left(-(\psi_B\varepsilon_y)_{y}  + \varepsilon\varphi_{i,B} - \psi_B Z\right)\right|\\
& \lesssim & |b| \left( \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12}  + \frac 1{s^2}\right)^2   \leq \frac 1 {500}  \frac {\mu_4} {B } \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc} (s)
+\frac C{s^4}.
\end{eqnarray*}
Next, integrating by parts,   using   the exponential decay of $Q$ and since $\psi_B(y)\equiv 1$ on $[-\frac B2,\infty)$:
\begin{eqnarray*}
&&\left|  \left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right)  \int {\Lambda} Q      \left(-(\psi_B)_y\varepsilon_y
-(1-\psi_B)\varepsilon_{yy}+(1-\psi_B)Z\right) \right|\\
& \lesssim & \left( \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12}  + \frac 1{s^2}\right)^2  \leq \frac 1 {500}  \frac {\mu_4} {B} \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc} +\frac C{s^4},
\end{eqnarray*}
and finally
\begin{align*}
&\left| \left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right)  \int {\Lambda} Q  \left[Z-5Q^4\varepsilon\right]
\right|  \lesssim \left( \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12} + \frac 1{s^2}\right) 
\left( \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc} + \frac 1{s^2}\right) 
\\
& \leq \frac 1 {500}  \frac {\mu_4} {B } \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc} (s)
+\frac C{s^4}.
\end{align*}
The collection of above estimates yields the bound:
 $$
 |f^{(i)}_{1,2}|\leq \frac 1 {100}  \frac {\mu_4} {B} \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc} + \frac C{s^4}.
 $$
nodes.statement_short: Orthogonality bounds f_12.

nodes.name: Decomposition
nodes.statement:
\underline{{\em Term $f^{(i)}_{1,2}$}}:  We decompose  $f_{1,2}$ in a suitable way:
\begin{align*}
f^{(i)}_{1,2} & =  2 \left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right)  \int {\Lambda} Q  (L \varepsilon) -2\left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right)\int\varepsilon (1-\varphi_{i,B})\Lambda Q
\\
&+ 2b \left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right)  \int {\Lambda} ( \chi_b P)  \left(-(\psi_B\varepsilon_y)_{y}  + \varepsilon\varphi_{i,B} - \psi_B Z\right)\\
& + 2 \left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right)  \int {\Lambda} Q      \left(-(\psi_B)_y\varepsilon_y
-(1-\psi_B)\varepsilon_{yy}+(1-\psi_B)Z\right) \\&
+ 2\left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right)  \int {\Lambda} Q  (Z-5Q^4\varepsilon)
\end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Decompose f_12.

nodes.name: Orthogonality
nodes.statement:
Observe from {\rm (\ref{ortho1})}: $$\int \Lambda Q (L\varepsilon)=(\varepsilon,L\Lambda Q)=-2(\varepsilon,Q)=0.$$  We now use the orthogonality conditions $( \varepsilon, y {\Lambda} Q)=0$ and the definition of $\varphi_{i,B}$ to estimate:
$$
	\left| \int {\Lambda} Q \varepsilon (1-\varphi_{i,B}) \right| = \left| \int {\Lambda} Q \varepsilon \left(1-\varphi_{i,B}+ \frac yB\right)\right|
	\lesssim e^{- \frac B 8 } \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12}  ,
$$
so that  for $B$ large enough:
\begin{align*}
  \left|  \left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right)  \int {\Lambda} Q\varepsilon (1-\varphi_{i,B}) \right| 
&\lesssim \left( \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12}  +\frac 1{s^2} \right) e^{- \frac B 8}  \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12}  
\\ &
\leq 
 \frac 1 {500}  \frac {\mu_4} {B} \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc} 
+\frac C{s^4}.
\end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Use orthogonality to bound the first terms.

nodes.name: chi_b P term
nodes.statement_short: Bound the chi_b P term.

nodes.name: Remaining terms
nodes.statement:
Next, integrating by parts,   using   the exponential decay of $Q$ and since $\psi_B(y)\equiv 1$ on $[-\frac B2,\infty)$:
\begin{eqnarray*}
&&\left|  \left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right)  \int {\Lambda} Q      \left(-(\psi_B)_y\varepsilon_y
-(1-\psi_B)\varepsilon_{yy}+(1-\psi_B)Z\right) \right|\\
& \lesssim & \left( \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12}  + \frac 1{s^2}\right)^2  \leq \frac 1 {500}  \frac {\mu_4} {B} \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc} +\frac C{s^4},
\end{eqnarray*}
and finally
\begin{align*}
&\left| \left(\frac {{\lambda}_{s}}{{\lambda}}+{b}\right)  \int {\Lambda} Q  \left[Z-5Q^4\varepsilon\right]
\right|  \lesssim \left( \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12} + \frac 1{s^2}\right) 
\left( \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc} + \frac 1{s^2}\right) 
\\
& \leq \frac 1 {500}  \frac {\mu_4} {B } \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc} (s)
+\frac C{s^4}.
\end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound the remaining terms.

nodes.name: Bound on f_12
nodes.statement:
The collection of above estimates yields the bound:
 $$
 |f^{(i)}_{1,2}|\leq \frac 1 {100}  \frac {\mu_4} {B} \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc} + \frac C{s^4}.
 $$
nodes.statement_short: Collect the bounds.

nodes.name: Term f_13
nodes.statement:
\underline{{\em Term $f^{(i)}_{1,3}$}}: Integrating by parts, we claim the identity
\begin{align*}
& -\frac 16 \int \psi_B' \left[(Q_b+pY_0+q+\varepsilon)^6 -Q_b^6 - 6Q_b^5\varepsilon - 6Q^5(pY_0+q)
-6 Q_b q^5\right]\\
& = \int \psi_B (Q_b)_y Z - 5 \int \psi_B Q' Q^4 \varepsilon + \int (Q_b^5-Q^5)_y \varepsilon\psi_B+  5\int (Q_b-Q)_y Q^4(pY_0+q) \psi_B \\
&+\int \psi_B p Y_0' Z +\int (Q^5-Q_b^5) pY_0' \psi_B + 5\int Q^4(pY_0+q) pY_0'\psi_B
+\int \psi_B p Y_0' q^5 Q_b\\
& +\int \psi_B q_y \left[(Q_b+pY_0+q+\varepsilon)^5 -Q^5\right]
+\int \psi_B \varepsilon_y Z + 5\int \psi_B \varepsilon_y Q^4 (pY_0+q).
\end{align*}
Therefore,
\begin{eqnarray*}
f^{(i)}_{1,3}& = &   \left(\frac{x_s}{\lambda}-1\right) \bigg\{2\int Q'\left[L\varepsilon-\psi_B' \varepsilon_y + (1-\psi_B)\varepsilon_{yy}-\varepsilon(1-\varphi_{i,B})\right]\\
& + & 2 \int(Q_b-Q+\varepsilon+pY_0)_y\left[-\psi_B'\varepsilon_y-\psi_B\varepsilon_{yy}+\varepsilon\varphi_{i,B}\right]\\
& + & \frac 13 \int\psi_B'\left[(Q_b+pY_0+q+\varepsilon)^6-Q_b^6-6Q_b^5\varepsilon-6Q^5(pY_0+q)
-6 Q_b q^5\right]\\
& + & 2  \int\varepsilon\psi_B(Q_b^5-Q^5)_y+ 10    \int \psi_B (Q_b-Q)_y Q^4 (pY_0+q)\\
& + & 2   \int \psi_B(Q^5-Q_b^5) pY_0' +10 \int Q^4 (pY_0+q) pY_0' \psi_B
+2 \int \psi_B pY_0' q^5 Q_b\\
& + & 2    \int \psi_Bq_y \left[ (Q_b+pY_0+q+\varepsilon)^5-Q^5-5Q_b q^4\right] +10\int \psi_B \varepsilon_y Q^4(pY_0+q)\bigg\}.
\end{eqnarray*}
The first term is treated using the cancellation $L Q'=0$ and the orthogonality conditions $(\varepsilon, \Lambda Q)=(\varepsilon,Q)=0$, so that $(yQ',\varepsilon)=0$. Thus, by the definitions of $\varphi_{i,B}$ and $\psi_B$,
\begin{eqnarray*}
&&\left|2\left(\frac{x_s}{\lambda}-1\right) \int Q'\left[L\varepsilon-\psi_B' \varepsilon_y + (1-\psi_B)\varepsilon_{yy}-\varepsilon(1-\varphi_{i,B})\right]\right| 
\\
&&=\left|2\left(\frac{x_s}{\lambda}-1\right) \int Q'\left[-\psi_B' \varepsilon_y + (1-\psi_B)\varepsilon_{yy}-\varepsilon\left(1+\frac yB-\varphi_{i,B}\right)\right]\right| 
\\&& \lesssim   \left(\mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12}+ \frac 1{s^2}\right)e^{-\frac B {10}}\mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12} \leq   \frac 1 {500}  \frac {\mu_4} {B} \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}+\frac C{s^4}.
\end{eqnarray*}
Then, as before, integrating by parts, and using Cauchy-Schwarz inequality,
\begin{eqnarray*}
&&\left|2b \left(\frac{x_s}{\lambda}-1\right)\int (\chi_bP)_y\left[-\psi_B'\varepsilon_y-\psi_B\varepsilon_{yy}+\varepsilon\varphi_{i,B}\right]\right|\\\
&&\lesssim
\frac 1{s} \left(\mathcal N_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12} + \frac 1{s^2} \right)
B^{\frac 12} \mathcal N_{i,\rm loc}\leq \frac 1 {500}  \frac {\mu_4} {B} \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}+\frac C{s^4}.
\end{eqnarray*}
\begin{eqnarray*}
&&\left|2\left(\frac{x_s}{\lambda}-1\right)\int  \varepsilon_y\left[-\psi_B'\varepsilon_y-\psi_B\varepsilon_{yy}+\varepsilon\varphi_{i,B}\right]\right|
\\ &&\lesssim \delta(\alpha^*) \int   \left(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2\right)   \varphi'_{i,B}\leq \frac1{500} \frac  {\mu_4}{B}\int   \left(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2\right)   \varphi'_{i,B}+\frac C{s^4}.
\end{eqnarray*}
\begin{align*}
& \left|\frac{x_s}{\lambda}-1\right| \left| \int pY_0' \left[ - \psi_B' \varepsilon_y
- \psi_B \varepsilon_{yy} + \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B}\right]\right|\\
& \lesssim \left(\mathcal N_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12} + \frac 1{s^2} \right)
\frac 1s \mathcal N_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12} 
\leq \frac1{500} \frac  {\mu_4}{B}\int   \left(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2\right)   \varphi'_{i,B}+\frac C{s^4}.
\end{align*}
 In conclusion for $f^{(i)}_{1,3}$, on gets
$$
|f^{(i)}_{1,3}| \leq \frac1{50} \frac  {\mu_4}{B}\int   \left(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2\right)   \varphi'_{i,B}+ \frac C{s^4},
$$
for $B$ large enough and $\alpha^*$ small enough, $s_0$ large enough.

\medskip
nodes.statement_short: Bound f_13 via LQ'=0 and orthogonality.

nodes.name: Identity
nodes.statement:
\underline{{\em Term $f^{(i)}_{1,3}$}}: Integrating by parts, we claim the identity
\begin{align*}
& -\frac 16 \int \psi_B' \left[(Q_b+pY_0+q+\varepsilon)^6 -Q_b^6 - 6Q_b^5\varepsilon - 6Q^5(pY_0+q)
-6 Q_b q^5\right]\\
& = \int \psi_B (Q_b)_y Z - 5 \int \psi_B Q' Q^4 \varepsilon + \int (Q_b^5-Q^5)_y \varepsilon\psi_B+  5\int (Q_b-Q)_y Q^4(pY_0+q) \psi_B \\
&+\int \psi_B p Y_0' Z +\int (Q^5-Q_b^5) pY_0' \psi_B + 5\int Q^4(pY_0+q) pY_0'\psi_B
+\int \psi_B p Y_0' q^5 Q_b\\
& +\int \psi_B q_y \left[(Q_b+pY_0+q+\varepsilon)^5 -Q^5\right]
+\int \psi_B \varepsilon_y Z + 5\int \psi_B \varepsilon_y Q^4 (pY_0+q).
\end{align*}
Therefore,
\begin{eqnarray*}
f^{(i)}_{1,3}& = &   \left(\frac{x_s}{\lambda}-1\right) \bigg\{2\int Q'\left[L\varepsilon-\psi_B' \varepsilon_y + (1-\psi_B)\varepsilon_{yy}-\varepsilon(1-\varphi_{i,B})\right]\\
& + & 2 \int(Q_b-Q+\varepsilon+pY_0)_y\left[-\psi_B'\varepsilon_y-\psi_B\varepsilon_{yy}+\varepsilon\varphi_{i,B}\right]\\
& + & \frac 13 \int\psi_B'\left[(Q_b+pY_0+q+\varepsilon)^6-Q_b^6-6Q_b^5\varepsilon-6Q^5(pY_0+q)
-6 Q_b q^5\right]\\
& + & 2  \int\varepsilon\psi_B(Q_b^5-Q^5)_y+ 10    \int \psi_B (Q_b-Q)_y Q^4 (pY_0+q)\\
& + & 2   \int \psi_B(Q^5-Q_b^5) pY_0' +10 \int Q^4 (pY_0+q) pY_0' \psi_B
+2 \int \psi_B pY_0' q^5 Q_b\\
& + & 2    \int \psi_Bq_y \left[ (Q_b+pY_0+q+\varepsilon)^5-Q^5-5Q_b q^4\right] +10\int \psi_B \varepsilon_y Q^4(pY_0+q)\bigg\}.
\end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: Integration by parts identity for f_13.

nodes.name: First term
nodes.statement:
The first term is treated using the cancellation $L Q'=0$ and the orthogonality conditions $(\varepsilon, \Lambda Q)=(\varepsilon,Q)=0$, so that $(yQ',\varepsilon)=0$. Thus, by the definitions of $\varphi_{i,B}$ and $\psi_B$,
\begin{eqnarray*}
&&\left|2\left(\frac{x_s}{\lambda}-1\right) \int Q'\left[L\varepsilon-\psi_B' \varepsilon_y + (1-\psi_B)\varepsilon_{yy}-\varepsilon(1-\varphi_{i,B})\right]\right| 
\\
&&=\left|2\left(\frac{x_s}{\lambda}-1\right) \int Q'\left[-\psi_B' \varepsilon_y + (1-\psi_B)\varepsilon_{yy}-\varepsilon\left(1+\frac yB-\varphi_{i,B}\right)\right]\right| 
\\&& \lesssim   \left(\mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12}+ \frac 1{s^2}\right)e^{-\frac B {10}}\mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12} \leq   \frac 1 {500}  \frac {\mu_4} {B} \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}+\frac C{s^4}.
\end{eqnarray*}
nodes.statement_short: Cancellation LQ'=0 and orthogonality.

nodes.name: Other terms
nodes.statement_short: Cauchy-Schwarz bounds.

nodes.name: Bound on f_13
nodes.statement:
In conclusion for $f^{(i)}_{1,3}$, on gets
$$
|f^{(i)}_{1,3}| \leq \frac1{50} \frac  {\mu_4}{B}\int   \left(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2\right)   \varphi'_{i,B}+ \frac C{s^4},
$$
for $B$ large enough and $\alpha^*$ small enough, $s_0$ large enough.

\medskip
nodes.statement_short: Collect the bounds.

nodes.name: Term f_14
nodes.statement_short: Bound f_14 by integration by parts and (BSparam).

nodes.name: Recall f_14
nodes.statement:
\underline{{\em Term $f^{(i)}_{1,4}$}}:  Recall
$$
f^{(i)}_{1,4} = - 2{b}_{s}  \int   \left(\chi_b   + \gamma   y (\chi_b)_y\right) P  \left(   - \psi_B\varepsilon_{yy} -\psi_B'\varepsilon_y+ \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B}-\psi_BZ   \right).$$
nodes.statement_short: Recall the form of f_14.

nodes.name: Estimates
nodes.statement_short: Integrations by parts and nonlinear estimate.

nodes.name: Bound on f_14
nodes.statement:
Together with \eqref{BSparam}, these estimates yield the bound:
$$|f_{1,4}| 
\leq  \frac 1 {500}  \frac {\mu_4} {B } 
 \int   \left(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2\right)   \varphi'_{i,B}   +\frac C{s^4}.$$
 
 \medskip
nodes.statement_short: Conclude the bound.

nodes.name: Term f_15
nodes.statement:
\underline{{\em Term $f^{(i)}_{1,5}$}}:  Recall:
$$
f^{(i)}_{1,5}=    
 2  \int  \Psi_b    \left(   -(\psi_B\varepsilon_{y})_y  + \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B Z   \right).
$$
We now rely on \eqref{BSbsps} to estimate by integration by parts and Cauchy-Schwarz's inequality,
$$
\left|  \int  (\Psi_b)_y    \psi_B\varepsilon_{y}\right| \lesssim    B^{\frac 12}  b^2 \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac12} \leq  \frac 1 {500}  \frac {\mu_4} {B} \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc} +\frac C{s^4}.
$$
By \eqref{eq:202}  and   the exponential decay of $\varphi_{i,B}$ in the left,
$$\left|  \int  \Psi_b \varphi_{i,B}\varepsilon\right|\lesssim \left( b^2 B^{\frac 12}+ e^{-\frac 1{2 |b|^{\gamma}}}\right)|b|^{1+\gamma}\mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac12}\leq  \frac 1 {500}  \frac {\mu_4} {B } \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc} +C|b|^{4}.$$ For the nonlinear term, similarly and using \eqref{nonlinearsobolev},
\begin{eqnarray*}
 \left| \int  \Psi_b   \psi_B Z   \right|  \leq  \frac 1 {500}  \frac {\mu_4} {B} \int   \left(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2\right)   \varphi'_{i,B}  +\frac C{s^4}.
\end{eqnarray*}
The collection of above estimates yields the bound:
$$
| f^{(i)}_{1,5}| \leq \frac 1 {100}  \frac {\mu_4} {B} \int   \left(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2\right)   \varphi'_{i,B}+\frac C{s^4}.$$
\medskip
nodes.statement_short: Bound the Psi_b term.

nodes.name: Recall f_15
nodes.statement:
\underline{{\em Term $f^{(i)}_{1,5}$}}:  Recall:
$$
f^{(i)}_{1,5}=    
 2  \int  \Psi_b    \left(   -(\psi_B\varepsilon_{y})_y  + \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B}-\psi_B Z   \right).
$$
nodes.statement_short: Recall the form of f_15.

nodes.name: Derivative term
nodes.statement:
We now rely on \eqref{BSbsps} to estimate by integration by parts and Cauchy-Schwarz's inequality,
$$
\left|  \int  (\Psi_b)_y    \psi_B\varepsilon_{y}\right| \lesssim    B^{\frac 12}  b^2 \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac12} \leq  \frac 1 {500}  \frac {\mu_4} {B} \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc} +\frac C{s^4}.
$$
nodes.statement_short: Cauchy-Schwarz on the derivative term.

nodes.name: Other terms
nodes.statement_short: Use (eq:202) and decay of the weights.

nodes.name: Bound on f_15
nodes.statement:
The collection of above estimates yields the bound:
$$
| f^{(i)}_{1,5}| \leq \frac 1 {100}  \frac {\mu_4} {B} \int   \left(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2\right)   \varphi'_{i,B}+\frac C{s^4}.$$
\medskip
nodes.statement_short: Collect the bounds.

nodes.name: Term f_16
nodes.statement:
\underline{{\em Term $f^{(i)}_{1,6}$}}: Recall that this term writes
\begin{align*}
\left| \int \left( -p_s Y_0 + (5Q^4 (p-q))_y + \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} p\Lambda Y_0\right)
\left( - (\psi_B \varepsilon_y)_y + \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B} - \psi_B Z\right) \right|
\end{align*} 
By \eqref{BSbsps}, \eqref{cl.2}, \eqref{BSparam},
\begin{align*}
& \left|  \left( -p_s Y_0 + (5Q^4 (p-q))_y + \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} p\Lambda Y_0\right)  \right|
+\left|  \left( -p_s Y_0 + (5Q^4 (p-q))_y + \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} p\Lambda Y_0\right)_y  \right|
\\ & \lesssim e^{-\frac {|y|}{2}} \left( \frac 1{s^2} + \int \varepsilon^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{2}} \right), 
\end{align*}
and thus
$$
| f^{(i)}_{1,6}| \lesssim \delta(\alpha^*) \int \varepsilon^2 e^{-\frac {|y|}{2} } 
+\frac 1{s^4}.
$$

\medskip
nodes.statement_short: Bound the tail forcing term.

nodes.name: Step 4: f_2 term
nodes.statement:
{\bf step 4} $f_2^{(i,j)}$ term. 
 
Recall:
\begin{eqnarray*}
f^{(i,j)}_2 &= & 2 {\frac{{\lambda}_s}{{\lambda}}}  \int    {\Lambda} \varepsilon  \left( - (\psi_B\varepsilon_y)_y +  \varepsilon\varphi_{i,B} -\psi_BZ \right)+\frac js\mathcal F_{i}.
\end{eqnarray*}
We integrate by parts to compute:
\begin{align*}
 & \int {\Lambda} \varepsilon (\psi_B\varepsilon_{y})_{y} =  -\int \varepsilon_y^2 \psi_B + \frac 12 \int \varepsilon^2_y y \psi_B',\\
 & \int  ({\Lambda} \varepsilon )    \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B} =- \frac 12 \int     \varepsilon^2    y\varphi_{i,B}',\\
 & \int {\Lambda} \varepsilon\psi_BZ
 = 
\int \left( \frac \varepsilon 2 + y\varepsilon_y\right) \psi_B  \left[ (Q_b+pY_0+q+\varepsilon)^5 - Q_b^5 
-5 Q^4 (pY_0+q)-q^5\right]\\
& = \int \frac \varepsilon 2 \psi_B \left[ (Q_b+pY_0+q+\varepsilon)^5 - Q_b^5 
-5 Q^4 (pY_0+q)-q^5\right]\\
& - \int (y\psi_B)_y  \bigg[ \frac {(Q_b+pY_0+q+\varepsilon)^6} 6  
- \frac {(Q_b+pY_0+q)^6} 6  - Q_b^5 \varepsilon \\&\qquad  - 5 Q^4(pY_0+q) \varepsilon- Q_b^5 (pY_0+q) -q^5 \varepsilon\bigg]\\
& - \int y \psi_B (Q_b)_y \big[ (Q_b+pY_0+q+\varepsilon)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5Q_b^4 \varepsilon - 5 Q_b^4 (pY_0+q) \varepsilon \\ &\qquad - 20 Q_b^3 (pY_0+q) \varepsilon\big] \\
& - \int y \psi_B pY_0' \left[ (Q_b+pY_0+q+\varepsilon)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5Q^4 \varepsilon\right]\\
&+5 \int (Q_b^4 - Q^4)_y (pY_0+q) \varepsilon y \psi_B\\
& - \int y \psi_B \left[ (Q_b+pY_0+q+\varepsilon)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0 + q)^5 - 5Q^4 \varepsilon - Q_b^5 - 5 q^4 \varepsilon\right].
\end{align*}
Thus,
 \begin{align*}
& f^{(i,j)}_2 = 2 \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} \bigg\{   \int \varepsilon_y^2 \psi_B -\frac 12 \int \varepsilon^2_y y \psi_B' - \frac 12 \int     \varepsilon^2    y\varphi_{i,B}'
 \\& + \int \frac \varepsilon 2 \psi_B \left[ (Q_b+pY_0+q+\varepsilon)^5 - Q_b^5 
-5 Q^4 (pY_0+q)-q^5\right]\\
& - \int (y\psi_B)_y  \bigg[ \frac {(Q_b+pY_0+q+\varepsilon)^6} 6  
- \frac {(Q_b+pY_0+q)^6} 6  - Q_b^5 \varepsilon \\ &  \qquad  - 5 Q^4(pY_0+q) \varepsilon- Q_b^5 (pY_0+q) -q^5 \varepsilon\bigg]\\
& - \int y \psi_B (Q_b)_y \big[ (Q_b+pY_0+q+\varepsilon)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5Q_b^4 \varepsilon - 5 Q_b^4 (pY_0+q) \varepsilon \\ &\qquad - 20 Q_b^3 (pY_0+q) \varepsilon\big] \\
& - \int y \psi_B pY_0' \left[ (Q_b+pY_0+q+\varepsilon)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5Q^4 \varepsilon\right]\\
&+5 \int (Q_b^4 - Q^4)_y (pY_0+q) \varepsilon y \psi_B\\
& - \int y \psi_B \left[ (Q_b+pY_0+q+\varepsilon)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0 + q)^5 - 5Q^4 \varepsilon - Q_b^5 - 5 q^4 \varepsilon\right]\bigg\} +\frac js\mathcal F_{i}.
  \end{align*}
  For $y<-B$, we use the exponential decay of $\psi_B, \varphi_{i,B}$ and   {\rm (\ref{defphi4})}
to estimate:
\begin{eqnarray*}
&&\int_{y<-\frac B2}(\psi_B+|y|\psi'_B+\varphi_{i,B})(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2) +|y|\varphi'_{i,B} \varepsilon^2\\
&& \lesssim  \int_{y<-\frac B2} \varepsilon_y^2 \varphi'_{i,B}+\int_{y<-\frac B2}|y|\varphi'_{i,B}\varepsilon^2\\
&&\lesssim  \int   \varepsilon_y^2    \varphi'_{i,B}  + \left(\int_{y<-\frac B2}|y|^{100}e^{\frac yB}\varepsilon^2\right)^{\frac{1}{100}}\left(\int_{y<-\frac B2}e^{\frac yB}\varepsilon^2\right)^{\frac{99}{100}} \\
&& \lesssim \int   \varepsilon_y^2    \varphi'_{i,B} +\mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac{9}{10}},
\end{eqnarray*}
where we have used $\int_{y<-\frac B2}|y|^{100}e^{\frac yB}\varepsilon^2\leq \|\varepsilon\|_{L^2}^2\leq \delta(\alpha^*)$.

 Together with similar estimates for the other terms,
this yields the bound:
$$|(f_2^{(i,j)})^<|\lesssim (\frac 1s+\mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12})\left(\int   \varepsilon_y^2    \varphi'_{i,B} +\mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac{9}{10}}+\frac 1{s^4}\right)\lesssim \delta(\alpha^*) \int  ( \varepsilon_y^2 +\varepsilon^2)   \varphi'_{i,B}  +
\frac 1{s^4}.$$

The middle term $f_{2}^{(i,j)}$ is also   estimated as follows
$$
|f_{2}^{(i,j)}|\leq \delta(\alpha^*) \int  ( \varepsilon_y^2 +\varepsilon^2)   \varphi'_{i,B}  +
\frac 1{s^4}.
$$

 
It only remains to estimate $(f_{2}^{(i,j)})^>$.
Most terms in $(f_{2}^{(i,j)}$ are easily estimated similarly as before. We focus on the following two delicate terms (because of weight at $+\infty$):
$$\int_{y> \frac B2}   \varepsilon^2    y\varphi_{i,B}', \quad
\frac j{s} \int_{y>\frac B2} \varepsilon^2 \varphi_{i,B}.$$
The function $\psi_B$ being bounded, the other terms are easier.

First, using \eqref{weightedonebis},
\begin{align*}
 \frac 1 s\int_{y>\frac B2} \varepsilon^2 \varphi_{i,B} & \lesssim
\frac 1s \left( 1+ \frac 1{\lambda^{\frac {10}9}}\right) \mathcal N_{2,\rm loc}^{\frac 89}\\
& \lesssim s^{\frac {10}9 \beta -1}\mathcal N_{2,\rm loc}^{\frac 89} 
\leq \frac 1 {100} \frac {\mu_4}{B} \mathcal N_{2, \rm loc} + s^{10 \beta -9}.
\end{align*}
Second, using $\mathcal N_{2,\rm loc}  \lesssim s^{-\frac 52 }$ and
$\beta<\frac 78$,
\begin{align*}
\int_{y> \frac B2}   \varepsilon^2    y\varphi_{i,B}' & \lesssim  \left(\frac 1s + \left( \int \varepsilon^2 e^{-\frac{|y|}{10}}\right)^{\frac 12} \right) \int_{y>\frac B2}   \varepsilon^2 \varphi_{i,B}\\
& \lesssim  \left(\frac 1s + \mathcal N_{2,\rm loc}^{\frac 12}  \right) s^{\frac {10}9 \beta }\mathcal N_{2,\rm loc}^{\frac 89} \leq \frac 1 {100} \frac {\mu_4}{B} \mathcal N_{2, \rm loc} + s^{10 \beta -9}.
\end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound f_2 using weighted controls of Step 1.

nodes.name: Recall f_2
nodes.statement_short: Recall f_2.

nodes.name: Integration by parts
nodes.statement:
We integrate by parts to compute:
\begin{align*}
 & \int {\Lambda} \varepsilon (\psi_B\varepsilon_{y})_{y} =  -\int \varepsilon_y^2 \psi_B + \frac 12 \int \varepsilon^2_y y \psi_B',\\
 & \int  ({\Lambda} \varepsilon )    \varepsilon \varphi_{i,B} =- \frac 12 \int     \varepsilon^2    y\varphi_{i,B}',\\
 & \int {\Lambda} \varepsilon\psi_BZ
 = 
\int \left( \frac \varepsilon 2 + y\varepsilon_y\right) \psi_B  \left[ (Q_b+pY_0+q+\varepsilon)^5 - Q_b^5 
-5 Q^4 (pY_0+q)-q^5\right]\\
& = \int \frac \varepsilon 2 \psi_B \left[ (Q_b+pY_0+q+\varepsilon)^5 - Q_b^5 
-5 Q^4 (pY_0+q)-q^5\right]\\
& - \int (y\psi_B)_y  \bigg[ \frac {(Q_b+pY_0+q+\varepsilon)^6} 6  
- \frac {(Q_b+pY_0+q)^6} 6  - Q_b^5 \varepsilon \\&\qquad  - 5 Q^4(pY_0+q) \varepsilon- Q_b^5 (pY_0+q) -q^5 \varepsilon\bigg]\\
& - \int y \psi_B (Q_b)_y \big[ (Q_b+pY_0+q+\varepsilon)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5Q_b^4 \varepsilon - 5 Q_b^4 (pY_0+q) \varepsilon \\ &\qquad - 20 Q_b^3 (pY_0+q) \varepsilon\big] \\
& - \int y \psi_B pY_0' \left[ (Q_b+pY_0+q+\varepsilon)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5Q^4 \varepsilon\right]\\
&+5 \int (Q_b^4 - Q^4)_y (pY_0+q) \varepsilon y \psi_B\\
& - \int y \psi_B \left[ (Q_b+pY_0+q+\varepsilon)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0 + q)^5 - 5Q^4 \varepsilon - Q_b^5 - 5 q^4 \varepsilon\right].
\end{align*}
Thus,
 \begin{align*}
& f^{(i,j)}_2 = 2 \frac{\lambda_s}{\lambda} \bigg\{   \int \varepsilon_y^2 \psi_B -\frac 12 \int \varepsilon^2_y y \psi_B' - \frac 12 \int     \varepsilon^2    y\varphi_{i,B}'
 \\& + \int \frac \varepsilon 2 \psi_B \left[ (Q_b+pY_0+q+\varepsilon)^5 - Q_b^5 
-5 Q^4 (pY_0+q)-q^5\right]\\
& - \int (y\psi_B)_y  \bigg[ \frac {(Q_b+pY_0+q+\varepsilon)^6} 6  
- \frac {(Q_b+pY_0+q)^6} 6  - Q_b^5 \varepsilon \\ &  \qquad  - 5 Q^4(pY_0+q) \varepsilon- Q_b^5 (pY_0+q) -q^5 \varepsilon\bigg]\\
& - \int y \psi_B (Q_b)_y \big[ (Q_b+pY_0+q+\varepsilon)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5Q_b^4 \varepsilon - 5 Q_b^4 (pY_0+q) \varepsilon \\ &\qquad - 20 Q_b^3 (pY_0+q) \varepsilon\big] \\
& - \int y \psi_B pY_0' \left[ (Q_b+pY_0+q+\varepsilon)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5Q^4 \varepsilon\right]\\
&+5 \int (Q_b^4 - Q^4)_y (pY_0+q) \varepsilon y \psi_B\\
& - \int y \psi_B \left[ (Q_b+pY_0+q+\varepsilon)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0 + q)^5 - 5Q^4 \varepsilon - Q_b^5 - 5 q^4 \varepsilon\right]\bigg\} +\frac js\mathcal F_{i}.
  \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Integrate by parts the terms of f_2.

nodes.name: Left region
nodes.statement:
For $y<-B$, we use the exponential decay of $\psi_B, \varphi_{i,B}$ and   {\rm (\ref{defphi4})}
to estimate:
\begin{eqnarray*}
&&\int_{y<-\frac B2}(\psi_B+|y|\psi'_B+\varphi_{i,B})(\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2) +|y|\varphi'_{i,B} \varepsilon^2\\
&& \lesssim  \int_{y<-\frac B2} \varepsilon_y^2 \varphi'_{i,B}+\int_{y<-\frac B2}|y|\varphi'_{i,B}\varepsilon^2\\
&&\lesssim  \int   \varepsilon_y^2    \varphi'_{i,B}  + \left(\int_{y<-\frac B2}|y|^{100}e^{\frac yB}\varepsilon^2\right)^{\frac{1}{100}}\left(\int_{y<-\frac B2}e^{\frac yB}\varepsilon^2\right)^{\frac{99}{100}} \\
&& \lesssim \int   \varepsilon_y^2    \varphi'_{i,B} +\mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac{9}{10}},
\end{eqnarray*}
where we have used $\int_{y<-\frac B2}|y|^{100}e^{\frac yB}\varepsilon^2\leq \|\varepsilon\|_{L^2}^2\leq \delta(\alpha^*)$.

 Together with similar estimates for the other terms,
this yields the bound:
$$|(f_2^{(i,j)})^<|\lesssim (\frac 1s+\mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac 12})\left(\int   \varepsilon_y^2    \varphi'_{i,B} +\mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}^{\frac{9}{10}}+\frac 1{s^4}\right)\lesssim \delta(\alpha^*) \int  ( \varepsilon_y^2 +\varepsilon^2)   \varphi'_{i,B}  +
\frac 1{s^4}.$$
nodes.statement_short: Exponential decay on the left.

nodes.name: Middle region
nodes.statement:
The middle term $f_{2}^{(i,j)}$ is also   estimated as follows
$$
|f_{2}^{(i,j)}|\leq \delta(\alpha^*) \int  ( \varepsilon_y^2 +\varepsilon^2)   \varphi'_{i,B}  +
\frac 1{s^4}.
$$
nodes.statement_short: Middle region estimate.

nodes.name: Delicate terms
nodes.statement:
It only remains to estimate $(f_{2}^{(i,j)})^>$.
Most terms in $(f_{2}^{(i,j)}$ are easily estimated similarly as before. We focus on the following two delicate terms (because of weight at $+\infty$):
$$\int_{y> \frac B2}   \varepsilon^2    y\varphi_{i,B}', \quad
\frac j{s} \int_{y>\frac B2} \varepsilon^2 \varphi_{i,B}.$$
The function $\psi_B$ being bounded, the other terms are easier.
nodes.statement_short: Identify the two delicate right-side terms.

nodes.name: First delicate term
nodes.statement_short: Use (weightedonebis).

nodes.name: Second delicate term
nodes.statement_short: Use the bootstrap bound on N_2,loc and beta<7/8.

nodes.name: Step 5: f_3 term
nodes.statement:
{\bf step 5} $f_3^{(i)}$ term.

\begin{align*}
f_3^{(i)}&= 2  \int \psi_B(Q_b)_{s} \left[(\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5 \varepsilon Q_b^4\right]\\
& - 2 \int \psi_B (p_s Y_0+ q_s) \left[(\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0+q)^5  -(Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5 \varepsilon Q^4\right]\\
&+ 10 \int \psi_B q_s q^4 \varepsilon.
\end{align*}

First,
$$
|(Q_b)_s|=\left|b_s P \left( \chi(|b|^{\gamma} y) + \gamma |b|^\gamma y \chi'(|b|^{\gamma} y)\right)\right|\lesssim |b_s| .
$$

\begin{align*}
&\left| \int \psi_B(Q_b)_{s} \left[(\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5 \varepsilon Q_b^4\right]\right| \\
  & \lesssim  |b_s|\int\psi_B \left(\varepsilon^2(|Q_b|^3+|p|^3+|q|^3+\delta(\alpha^*))  +|\varepsilon| (e^{-\frac {|y|}2} p^4+q^4) \right)\\
& \lesssim    \left(\frac 1{s^2} +  \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}\right)  \left( \int (\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2)  \psi_{B} + \left( \int \varepsilon^2 \psi_B \right)^{\frac 12 } \left( \int q^8\psi_B \right)^{\frac 12}\right)\\
& \lesssim  \left(\delta(\alpha^*) + \delta(s_0^{-1}) \right) \int \varepsilon^2   \varphi_{i,B}' +\frac C{s^4}.
\end{align*}
For the next two terms, we first remark that by explicit computations:
$$
\int \psi_B (p_s Y_0+ q_s)^2\lesssim \frac 1{s^2}.
$$
Thus, as before,
\begin{align*}
& \left|\int \psi_B (p_s Y_0+ q_s) \left[(\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0+q)^5  -(Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5 \varepsilon Q^4\right] \right| \\
& \lesssim    \left(\delta(\alpha^*) + \delta(s_0^{-1}) \right) \int \varepsilon^2   \varphi_{i,B}' +\frac C{s^4}.
\end{align*}
Finally,
$$
\left|  \int \psi_B q_s q^4 \varepsilon \right| \lesssim \left( \int \psi_B (q_s q^4)^2 \right)^{\frac 12}
\left( \int \psi_B  \varepsilon^2 \right)^{\frac 12}\lesssim \int \psi_B  \varepsilon^2 +\frac 1{s^4}.
$$
\medskip
nodes.statement_short: Bound f_3 using |(Q_b)_s| <~ |b_s|.

nodes.name: Recall f_3
nodes.statement_short: Recall f_3.

nodes.name: Q_b time derivative term
nodes.statement:
First,
$$
|(Q_b)_s|=\left|b_s P \left( \chi(|b|^{\gamma} y) + \gamma |b|^\gamma y \chi'(|b|^{\gamma} y)\right)\right|\lesssim |b_s| .
$$

\begin{align*}
&\left| \int \psi_B(Q_b)_{s} \left[(\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - (Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5 \varepsilon Q_b^4\right]\right| \\
  & \lesssim  |b_s|\int\psi_B \left(\varepsilon^2(|Q_b|^3+|p|^3+|q|^3+\delta(\alpha^*))  +|\varepsilon| (e^{-\frac {|y|}2} p^4+q^4) \right)\\
& \lesssim    \left(\frac 1{s^2} +  \mathcal{N}_{i,\rm loc}\right)  \left( \int (\varepsilon_y^2+\varepsilon^2)  \psi_{B} + \left( \int \varepsilon^2 \psi_B \right)^{\frac 12 } \left( \int q^8\psi_B \right)^{\frac 12}\right)\\
& \lesssim  \left(\delta(\alpha^*) + \delta(s_0^{-1}) \right) \int \varepsilon^2   \varphi_{i,B}' +\frac C{s^4}.
\end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound the (Q_b)_s term.

nodes.name: p_s and q_s terms
nodes.statement:
For the next two terms, we first remark that by explicit computations:
$$
\int \psi_B (p_s Y_0+ q_s)^2\lesssim \frac 1{s^2}.
$$
Thus, as before,
\begin{align*}
& \left|\int \psi_B (p_s Y_0+ q_s) \left[(\varepsilon+Q_b+pY_0+q)^5  -(Q_b+pY_0+q)^5 - 5 \varepsilon Q^4\right] \right| \\
& \lesssim    \left(\delta(\alpha^*) + \delta(s_0^{-1}) \right) \int \varepsilon^2   \varphi_{i,B}' +\frac C{s^4}.
\end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound the p_s, q_s terms.

nodes.name: Last term
nodes.statement:
Finally,
$$
\left|  \int \psi_B q_s q^4 \varepsilon \right| \lesssim \left( \int \psi_B (q_s q^4)^2 \right)^{\frac 12}
\left( \int \psi_B  \varepsilon^2 \right)^{\frac 12}\lesssim \int \psi_B  \varepsilon^2 +\frac 1{s^4}.
$$
\medskip
nodes.statement_short: Cauchy-Schwarz for the last term.

nodes.name: Step 6: coercivity
nodes.statement:
{\bf step 6} Proof of {\rm (\ref{lowerbound})}.

We proceed as in \cite{MMR1}. 
Recall that for $B$ large enough, $\mu>0$,
$$\int \psi_B\varepsilon_y^2 + \varphi_{i,B}\varepsilon^2- 5 \psi_B Q^4\varepsilon^2 \geq \mu \mathcal N_i.$$ 
We only have to estimate the error term as follows. 
For $s_0$ large enough, and $\alpha^*$ small enough,
\begin{align*}
& \left| \int \left( (Q_b{+}\varepsilon{+}pY_0{+}q)^6 {-} (Q_b{+}pY_0{+}q)^6  
{-} 6 \varepsilon (Q_b^5 {+} q^5 {+} 5 Q^4(pY_0{+}q)) {-} 6 Q^4 \varepsilon^2\right) \psi_B\right| \\
& \lesssim
\frac 1 {s^2}\left( \int \psi_B  \varepsilon^2 \right)^{\frac 12}+
\frac 1s \int \psi_B  \varepsilon^2 \leq \frac \mu {10} \mathcal N_i+ \frac 1 {s^4} .
\end{align*}
This concludes the proof of Lemma \ref{propasymtp}.
nodes.statement_short: Coercivity of F_i as in MMR1, (lowerbound).

nodes.name: Recall coercivity
nodes.statement:
{\bf step 6} Proof of {\rm (\ref{lowerbound})}.

We proceed as in \cite{MMR1}. 
Recall that for $B$ large enough, $\mu>0$,
$$\int \psi_B\varepsilon_y^2 + \varphi_{i,B}\varepsilon^2- 5 \psi_B Q^4\varepsilon^2 \geq \mu \mathcal N_i.$$
nodes.statement_short: Recall coercivity of the quadratic part.

nodes.name: Error term
nodes.statement:
We only have to estimate the error term as follows. 
For $s_0$ large enough, and $\alpha^*$ small enough,
\begin{align*}
& \left| \int \left( (Q_b{+}\varepsilon{+}pY_0{+}q)^6 {-} (Q_b{+}pY_0{+}q)^6  
{-} 6 \varepsilon (Q_b^5 {+} q^5 {+} 5 Q^4(pY_0{+}q)) {-} 6 Q^4 \varepsilon^2\right) \psi_B\right| \\
& \lesssim
\frac 1 {s^2}\left( \int \psi_B  \varepsilon^2 \right)^{\frac 12}+
\frac 1s \int \psi_B  \varepsilon^2 \leq \frac \mu {10} \mathcal N_i+ \frac 1 {s^4} .
\end{align*}
This concludes the proof of Lemma \ref{propasymtp}.
